name: thermal_homogenization
doc: Expand a periodic-laminate description into a concrete ``thermal_conductivity`` material.
full_doc:
Expand a periodic-laminate description into a concrete ``thermal_conductivity`` material.

High-level sugar in the CLAUDE.md §9 sense: a deck writes
``[Actions] [./homog] type = thermal_homogenization layer_conductivities
= [...] layer_fractions = [...] target_material = k_eff []`` instead of
hand-computing the effective conductivity, and this Action injects
``config["materials"]["k_eff"] = {"kind": "thermal_conductivity", "form":
"constant", "k0": k_series}`` (or, for ``direction = parallel``,
``k_parallel``) — an ordinary ``material = k_eff`` on a ``diffusion``
kernel then uses it with no further change.

name.name: name
name.doc: Optional action name (logs warnings with this label).

layer_conductivities.name: layer_conductivities
layer_conductivities.doc: Per-layer conductivity, one per layer (>= 2 layers).

layer_fractions.name: layer_fractions
layer_fractions.doc: Per-layer volume fraction, same order, positive and summing to 1.

direction.name: direction
direction.doc: 'series': effective conductivity ACROSS the layers (harmonic mean, the Reuss bound, exact for a laminate). 'parallel': ALONG the layers (arithmetic mean, the Voigt bound, exact for a laminate).

target_material.name: target_material
target_material.doc: Name of the [Materials] entry this Action creates (kind = thermal_conductivity).

name: uzr_pin_slice
doc: Expand ``[uzr_pin_slice]`` into the composed U–Zr pin-slice block set.
full_doc:
Expand ``[uzr_pin_slice]`` into the composed U–Zr pin-slice block set.

The Action is pure assembly. It reads the block's parameters, checks
the ones that have no safe default, and writes ``mesh``, ``variables``,
``kernels``, ``bcs``, ``materials`` and ``postprocessors`` entries that
the ordinary composed builder then consumes. A deck may override any
emitted block by writing it itself.

fuel_radius.name: fuel_radius
fuel_radius.doc: Fuel outer radius, m. Mesh extent and the moment arm for thin-wall hoop stress. No default: the pin geometry is the one thing every deck must state.

wall_thickness.name: wall_thickness
wall_thickness.doc: Cladding wall thickness, m. Denominator of the wastage and CDF severities. Required with no default so a deck cannot report a penetration fraction against a guessed wall.

alloy.name: alloy
alloy.doc: Cladding alloy key ('ht9', 'd9', 'ss316'). Selects the wastage coefficients and the rupture correlation; a wrong guess here is a wrong answer, not a wrong default.

interface_temperature.name: interface_temperature
interface_temperature.doc: Fuel/cladding interface temperature, K. It is the driver of the two thermally-limited mechanisms: state it and the expansion emits the FCCI and CDF severities, leave it unstated and it emits neither. Unstated rather than zero because a pin-slice deck solves for concentration, so there is no temperature array to reduce and a zero would be read as a stated 0 K.

peak_fuel_temperature.name: peak_fuel_temperature
peak_fuel_temperature.doc: Peak fuel temperature, K, driving the solidus severity. Unstated emits no solidus block. Distinct from 'interface_temperature': the fuel centreline is hotter than the cladding wall, and using the wall temperature here would report melting margin the fuel does not have.

peak_burnup_at_pct.name: peak_burnup_at_pct
peak_burnup_at_pct.doc: Peak burnup, at%, driving the swelling severity. Unstated emits no swelling block.

clad_hoop_strain.name: clad_hoop_strain
clad_hoop_strain.doc: Thermal component of cladding plastic hoop strain, dimensionless (0.01 is 1%), driving the hoop-strain severity. Unstated emits no hoop-strain block. This phase solves no cladding thermomechanics, so it is measured or design data, not solve output -- the severity normalises the criterion rather than deriving a strain. Distinct from 'peak_burnup_at_pct', which drives FUEL swelling against gap closure: different bodies, different limits.

clad_strain_limit.name: clad_strain_limit
clad_strain_limit.doc: Allowable cladding diametral strain (dimensionless), the capacity of the hoop-strain severity. Required whenever 'clad_hoop_strain' is stated. 0.01 is the IFR design limit and 0.02 is the level at which failures are observed to begin; they differ by 2x and answer different questions, so the sugar will not pick one for you.

allowable_penetration.name: allowable_penetration
allowable_penetration.doc: Allowable FCCI penetration as a fraction of the as-built wall (0-1). Required whenever 'interface_temperature' is stated: it is the capacity of the FCCI severity, a design decision with no defensible default, and the postprocessor refuses a zero.

cdf_limit.name: cdf_limit
cdf_limit.doc: Allowable cumulative damage fraction, the capacity of the creep-rupture severity. Required whenever 'interface_temperature' is stated. 0.05 is the IFR-era design value for EBR-II metallic-fuel pins, but it is a design decision, so the sugar will not pick it for you.

exposure_s.name: exposure_s
exposure_s.doc: Total exposure, s, handed to every severity postprocessor so one deck-level duty length cannot disagree with another. Required whenever 'interface_temperature' is stated -- both thermal mechanisms integrate over it.

fast_flux.name: fast_flux
fast_flux.doc: Fast neutron flux, n m^-2 s^-1, for the irradiation terms.

internal_pressure.name: internal_pressure
internal_pressure.doc: Plenum pressure, Pa, for the thin-wall hoop stress.

gap_closure_strain.name: gap_closure_strain
gap_closure_strain.doc: Radial fuel strain at which the fuel/cladding gap closes. Denominator of the swelling severity.

fuel_porosity.name: fuel_porosity
fuel_porosity.doc: Fuel porosity the bound ``uzr_nd_diffusivity`` closure is evaluated at, a volume fraction in [0, 1). This is the variable the three transport regimes switch on, so a study of interconnection sweeps it. Used only when 'interface_temperature' is stated, since that is when the expansion binds the closure at all.

zr_weight_fraction.name: zr_weight_fraction
zr_weight_fraction.doc: Fuel Zr weight fraction, for the solidus severity.

divisions.name: divisions
divisions.doc: Radial mesh divisions across the fuel annulus.

family.name: family
family.doc: Variable family, 'fem' or 'pinn' -- the same allowed set ``Variable`` itself enforces. 'pinn' selects the PINN twin arm; the block set is otherwise identical, which is what makes the two arms comparable on one deck.

reduction.name: reduction
reduction.doc: Field reduction for every severity postprocessor. Set once here so a deck cannot reduce one mechanism with 'max' and another with 'mean' and still call the envelope an envelope.

name: bnds
doc: Grain-boundary indicator for a multi-order-parameter field.
full_doc:
Grain-boundary indicator for a multi-order-parameter field.

MOOSE ``BndsCalcAux``: ``bnds = sum_i eta_i^2``. Inside a grain a
single order parameter is ~1 and the sum is ~1; at a boundary two
order parameters are ~0.5 each and the sum dips toward ~0.5, so
thresholding ``bnds`` visualises the grain-boundary network.

Reads the multi-component order-parameter field (``field`` by default,
which is what the phase-field executioners emit) and writes a nodal
scalar.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the auxiliary variable this kernel writes. The field becomes available to later aux kernels, to [Postprocessors] (as 'field = <name>'), and to the VTK/CSV output.

field.name: field
field.doc: Name of the multi-component order-parameter field. The phase-field executioners emit it as 'field'.

name: cp_field
doc: Forward a crystal-plasticity-derived nodal field to an aux variable.
full_doc:
Forward a crystal-plasticity-derived nodal field to an aux variable.

Reads one of the named CP outputs the constitutive model exposes
(``equivalent_plastic_strain``, ``slip_activity``, ``mean_rho``,
``backstress``) and writes it under the aux variable name. This
lets a deck pick which CP quantity to export / reduce without
having to write a one-off aux kernel for each — the same job MOOSE
does with a chain of ``*AccumulateAux`` / ``*Aux`` kernels.

Note:
    The CP fields are populated by the FEM executioners that
    carry a CP constitutive law (``cp_constitutive``,
    ``cp_quasi_static``, ``monolithic``, ``staggered``). On
    pure-elastic decks the requested field is absent from the
    solve result and the kernel raises ``PinnacleError`` naming
    the available fields.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the auxiliary variable this kernel writes. The field becomes available to later aux kernels, to [Postprocessors] (as 'field = <name>'), and to the VTK/CSV output.

cp_field.name: cp_field
cp_field.doc: Which CP-derived field to forward. The FEM CP executioners populate 'equivalent_plastic_strain', 'slip_activity', 'mean_rho', and 'backstress' as nodal fields; the aux kernel re-emits the chosen one under the aux variable's name.

name: elastic_energy
doc: Elastic energy density ``0.5 sigma : epsilon`` (MOOSE ``ElasticEnergyAux``).
full_doc:
Elastic energy density ``0.5 sigma : epsilon`` (MOOSE ``ElasticEnergyAux``).

Computed per element from the stress and strain tensors the solve
produced, so it reflects whatever constitutive law was active rather
than assuming linear elasticity.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the auxiliary variable this kernel writes. The field becomes available to later aux kernels, to [Postprocessors] (as 'field = <name>'), and to the VTK/CSV output.

stress.name: stress
stress.doc: Name of the stress field in the solve result.

strain.name: strain
strain.doc: Name of the strain field in the solve result.

name: linearised_order_parameter
doc: Expose the physical order parameter :math:`\eta = h(\psi)`.
full_doc:
Expose the physical order parameter :math:`\eta = h(\psi)`.

Reads the transformed variable's field after the solve and writes
:math:`\eta = \tfrac12[1 + \tanh(\psi/\sqrt2)]` per node — the
field the ``bnds`` indicator and the ``grain_boundary_area``
postprocessor consume. The result is in :math:`(0, 1)` for every
finite :math:`\psi`, so the downstream observables never see an
out-of-band order parameter.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the auxiliary variable this kernel writes. The field becomes available to later aux kernels, to [Postprocessors] (as 'field = <name>'), and to the VTK/CSV output.

field.name: field
field.doc: Name of the transformed-variable field. The phase-field executioners emit the solved field as 'field'; only the first component is read.

name: principal_stress_direction
doc: Unit vector along the named principal-stress direction (per element).
full_doc:
Unit vector along the named principal-stress direction (per element).

Computes the eigenvector of the named principal value
(``max_principal`` / ``min_principal`` / ``mid_principal``) for each
element and writes it as a per-element, per-component nodal-like
array (the leading dimension is ``n_elements``, the trailing
dimension is the spatial ``dim``).

Useful for plotting cleavage planes and crack-opening directions.
Mirrors MOOSE ``PrincipalStressDirectionAux``.

Note:
    The output shape is ``(n_elements, dim)``. Downstream exporters
    and postprocessors interpret it as a nodal field per element
    (the same footing as a rank-two component); for visualisation
    it is typical to read it into Paraview as point data on a
    element-by-element basis.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the auxiliary variable this kernel writes. The field becomes available to later aux kernels, to [Postprocessors] (as 'field = <name>'), and to the VTK/CSV output.

tensor.name: tensor
tensor.doc: Name of the rank-two field to read: 'stress' or 'strain' (any per-quadrature-point tensor in the solve result works).

principal.name: principal
principal.doc: Which principal value's direction to return: 'max_principal', 'mid_principal', or 'min_principal'.

name: radial_displacement
doc: Radial component of the displacement (MOOSE ``RadialDisplacement*Aux``).
full_doc:
Radial component of the displacement (MOOSE ``RadialDisplacement*Aux``).

``geometry = spherical`` projects onto the direction from ``origin``
to the node (MOOSE ``RadialDisplacementSphereAux``);
``geometry = cylindrical`` first removes the component along ``axis``,
projecting onto the in-plane radial direction (MOOSE
``RadialDisplacementCylinderAux``).

A node exactly at the origin (or on the axis) has no defined radial
direction; its value is set to zero rather than dividing by zero.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the auxiliary variable this kernel writes. The field becomes available to later aux kernels, to [Postprocessors] (as 'field = <name>'), and to the VTK/CSV output.

displacement.name: displacement
displacement.doc: Name of the nodal displacement field in the solve result.

geometry.name: geometry
geometry.doc: 'spherical' projects onto the direction from the origin to the node; 'cylindrical' removes the component along 'axis' first, giving the in-plane radial displacement.

origin.name: origin
origin.doc: Centre point of the radial coordinate system (default: the mesh origin).

axis.name: axis
axis.doc: Axis direction for cylindrical geometry (default: the last coordinate axis, i.e. z in 3-D). Ignored when spherical.

name: rank_two_component
doc: One component of a rank-two tensor (MOOSE ``RankTwoAux``).
full_doc:
One component of a rank-two tensor (MOOSE ``RankTwoAux``).

Extracts ``T[i, j]`` from a per-quadrature-point tensor field and
writes it as a per-element aux variable — the usual way to look at,
say, ``sigma_xx`` on its own.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the auxiliary variable this kernel writes. The field becomes available to later aux kernels, to [Postprocessors] (as 'field = <name>'), and to the VTK/CSV output.

tensor.name: tensor
tensor.doc: Name of the rank-two field to read: 'stress' or 'strain' (any per-quadrature-point tensor in the solve result works).

index_i.name: index_i
index_i.doc: Row index of the tensor component (0-based: 0=x, 1=y, 2=z).

index_j.name: index_j
index_j.doc: Column index of the tensor component (0-based: 0=x, 1=y, 2=z).

name: rank_two_scalar
doc: A scalar invariant of a rank-two tensor (MOOSE ``RankTwoScalarAux``).
full_doc:
A scalar invariant of a rank-two tensor (MOOSE ``RankTwoScalarAux``).

Supported quantities, all computed per element:

* ``von_mises`` — ``sqrt(3/2 s:s)`` with ``s`` the deviator; the
  standard equivalent stress for yielding.
* ``hydrostatic`` — ``tr(T)/3``, the mean (pressure-like) part.
* ``trace`` — ``tr(T)``; for strain this is the volumetric strain.
* ``effective`` — ``sqrt(2/3 s:s)``, the strain counterpart of von
  Mises (use it for equivalent strain).
* ``max_principal`` / ``min_principal`` / ``mid_principal`` — ordered
  eigenvalues; the max principal stress drives cleavage-type fracture.
* ``l2_norm`` — the Frobenius norm ``sqrt(T:T)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the auxiliary variable this kernel writes. The field becomes available to later aux kernels, to [Postprocessors] (as 'field = <name>'), and to the VTK/CSV output.

tensor.name: tensor
tensor.doc: Name of the rank-two field to read: 'stress' or 'strain' (any per-quadrature-point tensor in the solve result works).

quantity.name: quantity
quantity.doc: Invariant to compute: 'von_mises' (equivalent stress), 'effective' (equivalent strain), 'hydrostatic' (mean part), 'trace' (volumetric part), 'max_principal' / 'mid_principal' / 'min_principal' (ordered eigenvalues), or 'l2_norm' (Frobenius norm).

name: stress_triaxiality
doc: Stress-triaxiality ratio ``tr(σ) / (3 σ_vm)`` per element.
full_doc:
Stress-triaxiality ratio ``tr(σ) / (3 σ_vm)`` per element.

The triaxiality is the standard ductile-fracture indicator: positive
values (>1/3) drive void growth under hydrostatic tension, while
negative values (< -1/3) suppress it. Computed per element from a
rank-two tensor field, mirroring MOOSE ``StressTriaxialityAux``.

A zero von Mises stress (pure hydrostatic or zero field) gives a
zero ratio — we return ``0.0`` rather than dividing by zero so the
diagnostic stays finite; the offending element will be obvious
from the von Mises postprocessor.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the auxiliary variable this kernel writes. The field becomes available to later aux kernels, to [Postprocessors] (as 'field = <name>'), and to the VTK/CSV output.

tensor.name: tensor
tensor.doc: Name of the rank-two field to read: 'stress' or 'strain' (any per-quadrature-point tensor in the solve result works).

name: convective
doc: Registered convective (Robin) BC factory.
full_doc: Registered convective (Robin) BC factory.

kind.name: kind
kind.doc: BC kind; must be 'convective'.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the Variable this boundary condition applies to.

side_set.name: side_set
side_set.doc: Side set the convective flux acts on.

function.name: function
function.doc: Optional [Functions] entry giving a SPATIAL profile on the convective coefficient — h(x) = function(x) * h, evaluated at the boundary nodes. A time-dependent function is refused: the boundary operator is assembled once and never advanced (the same rule the kernel coefficient route enforces).

name: dirichlet
doc: Registered dirichlet-BC factory.
full_doc: Registered dirichlet-BC factory.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this BC applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

equation.name: equation
equation.doc: Equation row this boundary term joins, for the nonlinear block transient (``pf_fem_transient``) when the deck's rows are NAMED rather than one per variable — the split Cahn-Hilliard pair's ``split_ch_conservation`` / ``split_ch_potential``, say. Leave it empty (the default) and the row is resolved from the variable's kernels: the variable's own row when it has one, else the single row its kernels feed, else (for a prescribed flux) the row carrying its accumulation, since a flux is a boundary term of the balance law. Set it only when that is ambiguous, which the executioner reports by naming the candidate rows. Ignored by the executioners whose rows are always per-variable.

kind.name: kind
kind.doc: BC kind. ``dirichlet`` is a prescribed value on a node set; ``neumann`` is a traction/pressure on a side set; ``periodic`` matches two sets (Phase 5/6 follow-up); ``hard_constraint`` is the PINN hard-Dirichlet transform.

node_set.name: node_set
node_set.doc: Node set name (for ``dirichlet``/``hard_constraint``). Must match a key in the mesh's ``node_sets``.

side_set.name: side_set
side_set.doc: Side set name (for ``neumann``). Must match a key in the mesh's ``side_sets``.

components.name: components
components.doc: Vector-component indices to constrain (e.g. ``[0, 1]`` for x and y). Defaults to *all* components (the spatial dim).

values.name: values
values.doc: Prescribed values (one per component, or a single scalar broadcast to all components).

traction.name: traction
traction.doc: Neumann traction vector ``t`` (force per unit area, general form). Use ``pressure`` for the convenient normal-only form.

pressure.name: pressure
pressure.doc: Neumann pressure scalar. ``>0`` pulls the surface outward (tension), ``<0`` pushes it inward (compression). Cannot be combined with ``traction``.

function.name: function
function.doc: Optional :class:`Function` name whose scalar value at the current time scales the BC value (time dependence).

mode.name: mode
mode.doc: Grain-boundary mode (``kind=grain_boundary``, M6). ``micro_hard`` blocks slip on the side set; ``micro_free`` leaves it unconstrained; ``transmission`` scales the slip rate by a per-system transmissivity factor.

transmissivity.name: transmissivity
transmissivity.doc: Grain-boundary transmissivity factor (``kind=grain_boundary``, M6, ``mode=transmission``). Scalar or per-system array of length ``n_systems``. ``0`` recovers ``micro_hard``; ``1`` recovers ``micro_free``.

k_hp.name: k_hp
k_hp.doc: Hall–Petch coefficient ``k_HP`` (``kind=grain_boundary``, M6). Combined with ``d`` (grain size) to add a constant ``k_HP / sqrt(d)`` to the slip resistance in the GB zone.

d.name: d
d.doc: Grain size ``d`` in metres (``kind=grain_boundary``, M6). Required for the Hall–Petch contribution; ignored when ``k_hp = 0``.

name: fcci_reactive_sink
doc: Registered FCCI reactive-sink BC factory.
full_doc: Registered FCCI reactive-sink BC factory.

kind.name: kind
kind.doc: BC kind. ``[BCs]`` sub-blocks are keyed on ``kind`` (not ``type``), and the composed builder resolves an extension kind through the registry, so this must be the registered name.

side_set.name: side_set
side_set.doc: Side set naming the fuel–cladding interface surface.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Concentration variable the sink consumes; blank for a wastage-only run with no transport field.

alloy.name: alloy
alloy.doc: Cladding alloy key. **Required, no default** — the alloys differ by more than an order of magnitude in wastage rate, so a default would silently pick a severity.

rate_threshold.name: rate_threshold
rate_threshold.doc: Rate-constant gate. The accumulator integrates only while ``K > rate_threshold``, so growth arrests during a shutdown and resumes on restart. Gating on ``K`` rather than on temperature makes one threshold work across the alloys.

kinetic_exponent.name: kinetic_exponent
kinetic_exponent.doc: Exponent ``n`` on the dimensionless time ratio. 0.5 is parabolic (diffusion-limited); above it the layer is less protective than parabolic kinetics implies.

reference_exposure.name: reference_exposure
reference_exposure.doc: Reference exposure at which every exponent agrees. A convention, not a fit: it cannot affect the answer at the default ``kinetic_exponent = 0.5``.

interface_temperature.name: interface_temperature
interface_temperature.doc: Interface temperature the kinetics are evaluated at, K (absolute). Stated because this reduction solves for concentration, not temperature. Required unless ``temperature_function`` is given.

temperature_function.name: temperature_function
temperature_function.doc: Name of a ``[Functions]`` entry giving the interface temperature as a function of TIME. This is what exercises the threshold gate: a duty cycle dropping to cold shutdown puts ``K`` below ``rate_threshold`` and growth arrests. Wins over ``interface_temperature``.

layer_species_concentration.name: layer_species_concentration
layer_species_concentration.doc: Concentration of the diffusing species INSIDE the interaction layer, in the units of the variable this BC is bound to. ``surface_flux`` is a layer-growth SPEED (m/s); the transport load needs a species flux, and this is the factor that converts one to the other (the moving-boundary statement ``j = v * c_layer``). REQUIRED whenever 'variable' is set -- no default, because only the deck knows whether its variable is at%, atoms/m^3 or mol/m^3, and a guessed factor would scale the sink by an arbitrary amount.

fast_flux.name: fast_flux
fast_flux.doc: Fast neutron flux driving the irradiation-assisted term in ``K``. Zero leaves only the thermal term.

exposure_s.name: exposure_s
exposure_s.doc: Reaction time the accumulator starts from, s. A parabolic layer is zero at zero reaction time, so a STEADY deck with no seed sees no sink at all; state the duty length here and the steady solve reports the interface condition after that exposure. A transient run accumulates on top of it.

seed_layer_thickness.name: seed_layer_thickness
seed_layer_thickness.doc: Pre-existing interaction layer, stated directly, m. The EXACT way to seed a restart: it needs no historical temperature or flux, and is right for any campaign, isothermal or not. Prefer it whenever the previous layer is known. Mutually exclusive with ``exposure_s``, which reconstructs the same quantity from the conditions that produced it and is only correct for an isothermal, iso-flux campaign.

seed_fast_flux.name: seed_fast_flux
seed_fast_flux.doc: Fast flux the seeded ``exposure_s`` accumulated under. REQUIRED alongside ``seed_temperature`` for a non-zero ``exposure_s``, because ``K`` carries a flux-linear term as well as an Arrhenius one, so a temperature alone does not determine the historical rate: seeding D9 at a run flux of 2e19 instead of a shut-down campaign's zero reads 1.92x the true layer. State ``0`` for a thermal-only campaign. Unused when ``seed_layer_thickness`` is given.

seed_temperature.name: seed_temperature
seed_temperature.doc: Interface temperature the seeded ``exposure_s`` accumulated under, K. REQUIRED whenever ``exposure_s`` is non-zero, together with ``seed_fast_flux``. The seed is history from before this run, so nothing in the run supplies it: a ``temperature_function`` gives the conditions the run STARTS in, and a constant ``interface_temperature`` is what the run is MODELLED at -- neither is the temperature the campaign happened at. Guessing understates the layer by up to 38x, in the unconservative direction. Unused when ``seed_layer_thickness`` is given.

include_thermal.name: include_thermal
include_thermal.doc: Include the Arrhenius term in ``K``. For term ablation.

include_irradiation.name: include_irradiation
include_irradiation.doc: Include the flux-linear term in ``K``. For term ablation.

name: gaussian_flux
doc: Registered Gaussian surface-beam BC factory.
full_doc: Registered Gaussian surface-beam BC factory.

kind.name: kind
kind.doc: BC kind; must be 'gaussian_flux'.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the Variable this BC applies to.

beam_center.name: beam_center
beam_center.doc: Beam-centre coordinates at t = 0 (1-3 finite components, zero-padded to 3).

velocity.name: velocity
velocity.doc: Constant beam-scan velocity (1-3 finite components, zero-padded to 3); the centre at time t is 'beam_center + velocity * t'. Only a transient executioner advances t — a steady solve evaluates the beam at t = 0.

name: grain_boundary
doc: Registered grain-boundary-BC factory (Phase M6, CP field).
full_doc:
Registered grain-boundary-BC factory (Phase M6, CP field).

The ``grain_boundary`` BC is the opt-in interface condition for the
crystal-plasticity field kernel. It tags a side set with a slip
constraint (``micro_hard`` | ``micro_free`` | ``transmission``) and
carries an optional Hall–Petch ``k_hp`` + ``d`` pair. The CP
kernel consumes it through :meth:`StressDivergenceCPKernel.bind_gb_conditions`
at :meth:`make_material` time; the BC is not consumed by the FEM
/PINN executioner's Dirichlet/Neumann pipeline.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this BC applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

equation.name: equation
equation.doc: Equation row this boundary term joins, for the nonlinear block transient (``pf_fem_transient``) when the deck's rows are NAMED rather than one per variable — the split Cahn-Hilliard pair's ``split_ch_conservation`` / ``split_ch_potential``, say. Leave it empty (the default) and the row is resolved from the variable's kernels: the variable's own row when it has one, else the single row its kernels feed, else (for a prescribed flux) the row carrying its accumulation, since a flux is a boundary term of the balance law. Set it only when that is ambiguous, which the executioner reports by naming the candidate rows. Ignored by the executioners whose rows are always per-variable.

name: pf_contact_angle
doc: Registered phase-field contact-angle (wetting) BC factory.
full_doc: Registered phase-field contact-angle (wetting) BC factory.

kind.name: kind
kind.doc: BC kind; must be 'pf_contact_angle'.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the phase-field Variable (values in [-1, 1]) this wall condition applies to. Must be a scalar fem variable whose interface kernel (``ac_interface``) lives on its own row.

side_set.name: side_set
side_set.doc: Side set of the wall the phase meets (e.g. ``ymin`` on a ``box_mesh``). The condition is integrated over the faces of the set, with the outward normal of each face.

contact_angle.name: contact_angle
contact_angle.doc: Equilibrium contact angle theta in degrees, strictly inside (0, 180): the angle between the interface normal grad(phi)/|grad(phi)| (pointing into the phi = +1 phase) and the outward wall normal. < 90 wets the wall with the phi = +1 phase, > 90 with phi = -1; 90 is the natural no-flux boundary.

surface_tension.name: surface_tension
surface_tension.doc: Interfacial tension sigma of the diffuse interface. For the double well f = W (phi^2 - 1)^2 with gradient coefficient kappa the consistent value is sigma = 2 sqrt(2) lambda / (3 eps) with eps = sqrt(kappa / (4 W)), which makes 3 sigma / (4 lambda) = 1 / ell, ell = sqrt(kappa / (2 W)).

mixing_energy.name: mixing_energy
mixing_energy.doc: Mixing-energy density lambda of the Jacqmin/Yue free energy lambda [ |grad phi|^2 / 2 + (phi^2 - 1)^2 / (4 eps^2) ]. In that form lambda IS the gradient coefficient, so it defaults to ``gradient_coefficient``; set it only for a non-standard normalisation.

gradient_coefficient.name: gradient_coefficient
gradient_coefficient.doc: Gradient-energy coefficient kappa of the interface kernel on this variable (the ``gradient_coefficient`` of ``ac_interface``). Scales the boundary integral so it matches the kappa (grad phi, grad psi) stiffness whose integration by parts produced it; a mismatch imposes a different angle than the one named.

mobility.name: mobility
mobility.doc: Mobility L multiplying the interface kernel's stiffness (the ``mobility`` of ``ac_interface``, whose weak form is L kappa (grad phi, grad psi)). The boundary integral is scaled by L * kappa. Leave at 1 for the split Cahn-Hilliard potential row, where the gradient term carries kappa alone.

adiabatic_side_sets.name: adiabatic_side_sets
adiabatic_side_sets.doc: Optional reradiating (adiabatic, q = 0) surfaces closing the enclosure. They participate in the view-factor geometry and the radiosity solve (rows sum_j (delta_ij - F_ij) J_j = 0) but are not coupled to the temperature field and need no emissivity. Listed AFTER 'side_sets' in the 'patches' / 'view_factor_matrix' ordering.

view_factor_mode.name: view_factor_mode
view_factor_mode.doc: 'quadrature': compute the view-factor matrix from 'patches' by unobstructed-planar Gauss-Legendre quadrature. 'specified': use 'view_factor_matrix' directly.

patches.name: patches
patches.doc: Flat [x0,y0,x1,y1, x0,y0,x1,y1, ...] straight-segment endpoints, one quadruple per surface in 'side_sets' order; required when 'view_factor_mode' = 'quadrature'. Flat rather than nested per-surface pairs because the '.i' lexer has no nested-vector primitive (see 'layered_line_mesh's 'bounds' doc for the same convention). This is IDEALISED geometry for the view-factor calculation only — the flux is still distributed over the mesh's own 'side_sets' node areas, so the two should describe the same physical surfaces but need not be identical.

view_factor_matrix.name: view_factor_matrix

n_quadrature.name: n_quadrature
n_quadrature.doc: Gauss-Legendre points per patch (per integration axis) in 'quadrature' mode.

full_doc: Registered composite thermal-resistance BC factory.

kind.doc: BC kind; must be 'thermal_resistance'.

thermal_conductivities.name: thermal_conductivities
thermal_conductivities.doc: Conductivity of each series conduction layer; every entry must be finite and > 0. Required — a resistance stack is its layers (a defaulted zero-thickness layer would be refused anyway).

conduction_thicknesses.name: conduction_thicknesses
conduction_thicknesses.doc: Thickness of each series conduction layer, matching 'thermal_conductivities'; every entry must be finite and > 0.

geometry.name: geometry
geometry.doc: Layer geometry. 'cartesian' sums dx_i/k_i; 'cylindrical' sums r_0 ln(r_{i+1}/r_i)/k_i (per unit inner-wall area) with radii built outward from 'inner_radius', and scales the exterior film resistance by r_0/r_N.

inner_radius.name: inner_radius
inner_radius.doc: Radius of the boundary the BC acts on (the innermost layer surface). Required > 0 when geometry = 'cylindrical'; ignored for 'cartesian'.

emissivity.name: emissivity

t_infinity.name: t_infinity
t_infinity.doc: Ambient (far-field) temperature. Always finite. Additionally >= 0 when 'emissivity' > 0, because the radiative film h_r = eps*sigma*(T_s^2 + T_inf^2)(T_s + T_inf) reads it as an ABSOLUTE temperature; with radiation disabled it appears only in the difference U*(T - T_inf), so an offset-scaled conductance deck may legitimately use a negative ambient.

stefan_boltzmann.name: stefan_boltzmann
stefan_boltzmann.doc: Stefan-Boltzmann constant; overridable for non-dimensional decks.

max_iterations.name: max_iterations

tolerance.name: tolerance
tolerance.doc: Convergence tolerance (surface-temperature change) for the fixed point.

relaxation.name: relaxation
relaxation.doc: Under-relaxation factor for the exterior-surface fixed point, in (0, 1].

name: curve
doc: Read a time- or strain-series CSV for the data term or validation.
full_doc:
Read a time- or strain-series CSV for the data term or validation.

Expected CSV columns:
- ``time`` or ``strain`` (identifies the independent axis)
- ``stress`` (required, Pa)
- optional additional state columns, e.g. ``rho``, ``c11``, ``c12``, ``c44``

Units are read from the optional ``units`` sub-dict argument:
    ``units = {col: unit_string}`` e.g. ``{"stress": "mpa", "time": "ms"}``

The ``weight`` key gives the per-series weight in CompositeLoss (default 1.0).

Example ``data`` dict::

    {
        "path": "stress_strain.csv",
        "kind": "curve",
        "columns": ["time", "stress"],
        "weight": 1.0,
        "units": {"stress": "mpa"},
    }

columns.name: columns
columns.doc: Names of the columns to extract, in order. Empty reads every column present in the file.

units.name: units
units.doc: Per-column unit strings used to convert into SI on read, e.g. {'stress': 'mpa', 'time': 'ms'}.

scale.name: scale
scale.doc: Uniform multiplier applied to the values after unit conversion.

name: field
doc: Read spatial reference fields at given coordinates/timestamps (CSV).
full_doc:
Read spatial reference fields at given coordinates/timestamps (CSV).

Expected CSV columns:
    ``x``, optionally ``y``/``z``, optionally ``t``, then one column
    per field (``field_1``, ``field_2``, ...).

Only columns listed in ``columns`` are extracted.  Units are handled per-column
via the ``units`` dict argument.

Example ``data`` dict::

    {
        "path": "ref_field.csv",
        "kind": "field",
        "columns": ["cauchy_xx", "cauchy_yy"],
        "weight": 1.0,
        "units": {"cauchy_xx": "mpa"},
    }

columns.doc: Names of the columns to extract, in order. Empty reads every column present in the file.

units.name: units

scale.name: scale
scale.doc: Uniform multiplier applied to the values after unit conversion.

time.name: time
time.doc: Timestamp the reference field corresponds to, when the file has no 't' column.

name: points
doc: Read scattered (input → observed output) point data for general supervision.
full_doc:
Read scattered (input → observed output) point data for general supervision.

Expected CSV columns:
    input_1 [, input_2 ...] <output_1> [<output_2> ...]

Column names are user-defined.  The ``columns`` entry in the data dict must
specify which columns are inputs and which are outputs::

    {
        "path": "scattered.csv",
        "kind": "points",
        "columns": {"inputs": ["x", "y"], "outputs": ["stress"]},
        "weight": 1.0,
    }

Units are handled per-column via the ``units`` dict argument.

name: bcc
doc: Return BCC slip systems for the requested ``{hkl}<111>`` families.
full_doc:
Return BCC slip systems for the requested ``{hkl}<111>`` families.

Args:
    slip_families: List of family names to include.  Supported names are
        ``"110"``, ``"112"`` and ``"123"``.  Default is ``["110"]``,
        giving the 12 conventional {110}<111> systems.

Returns:
    Dictionary with ``normals``, ``directions``, ``schmid``,
    ``schmid_sym``, ``families`` (string label per system) and
    ``counts`` (system count per family).

euler_angles.name: euler_angles
euler_angles.doc: Crystal orientation in ZXZ Bunge convention. Rotating the crystal changes the Schmid factors and therefore the flow stress, which is the point of a single-crystal study.

slip_families.name: slip_families
slip_families.doc: Slip-plane families to activate: any of '110', '112', '123'. More families means more slip systems and a more isotropic yield surface.

name: fcc
doc: Return the 12 {111}<110> FCC slip systems and Schmid tensors.
full_doc:
Return the 12 {111}<110> FCC slip systems and Schmid tensors.

Returns:
    A dictionary with keys ``normals``, ``directions``, ``schmid``,
    ``schmid_sym`` and ``families``.  ``normals[a]`` and
    ``directions[a]`` are unit vectors; ``schmid[a] = directions[a]
    \otimes normals[a]``; ``schmid_sym[a]`` is the symmetric part used
    in the resolved-shear-stress contraction.  ``families`` is a string
    array labelling each system ``"111"``.

euler_angles.name: euler_angles
euler_angles.doc: Crystal orientation in ZXZ Bunge convention. Rotating the crystal changes the Schmid factors and therefore the flow stress, which is the point of a single-crystal study.

type.doc: Registered executioner name. ``fem_steady`` solves a single Newton step (steady FEM); ``fem_quasi_static`` runs a load-stepping loop with adaptive cutback; ``fem_transient`` runs an implicit-Euler time loop on the scalar mass + gradient stiffness operators (Phase M5); ``pinn_transient`` trains a PINN over the kernels' strong residuals; ``cp_quasi_static`` drives the crystal-plasticity field with adaptive cutback (Phase M6); ``pfd_steady`` is the linearized steady-state phase-field damage driver (Phase M7); ``staggered`` / ``monolithic`` orchestrate per-variable-group sub-solves (Phase M7 coupling); ``pinn_fem_hybrid`` trains a spatial PINN and uses it as a predictor / initial guess / preconditioner for a FEM Newton corrector (Phase M13; modes registered in :mod:`pinnacle.solvers.hybrid`).

variable.name: variable

On a coupled deck that declares more than one, set it: without it the solve takes the first ``fem``-family variable the translator emitted, which depends on declaration order and silently assembles the wrong physics when it guesses wrong. The ``staggered`` and ``pinn_fem_hybrid_coupled_physics`` executioners fill this in for their sub-blocks.

n_steps.name: n_steps
n_steps.doc: Number of load steps in the program.

max_iter.name: max_iter
max_iter.doc: Maximum Newton iterations per load step.

tangent_method.name: tangent_method
tangent_method.doc: Tangent computation method (``analytic`` or ``autodiff``). ``analytic`` uses the material's ``tangent()`` callback; ``autodiff`` uses the backend Jacobian.

linear_method.name: linear_method
linear_method.doc: Linear solver method (``direct`` dense or ``cg`` iterative).

initial_load_factor.name: initial_load_factor
initial_load_factor.doc: Initial load factor at step 0 (continuation runs).

target_load_factor.name: target_load_factor
target_load_factor.doc: Final load factor reached at the last step.

load_function.name: load_function
load_function.doc: Optional :class:`Function` name that drives the load factor at each step (default: linear ramp initial → target).

safety_factor.name: safety_factor
safety_factor.doc: Multiplier applied to a step size after a cutback.

newton_tol.name: newton_tol
newton_tol.doc: **Absolute** residual L2-norm tolerance for Newton convergence (per-step). See ``newton_rel_tol`` — on a stiff material the absolute test alone is not reachable.

newton_rel_tol.name: newton_rel_tol
newton_rel_tol.doc: **Relative** residual tolerance: the step converges once ``||R|| <= max(rel_tol * ||R_0||, tol)``, where ``||R_0||`` is the first iteration's residual norm. The residual carries the units of a nodal force, so on a stiff material the absolute test can sit below the assembled system's floating-point noise floor and never fire; this scale-free test is what terminates such a solve. Set to ``0`` to use the absolute test alone.

warn_no_gnd_grad.name: warn_no_gnd_grad
warn_no_gnd_grad.doc: Warn when GND is requested but the gradient operator cannot be wired.

t_end.name: t_end
t_end.doc: Physical program duration in seconds (the CP state-update ``dt = t_end / n_steps``). When ``None`` the executioner reads it from the load function's ``t_end`` parameter, falling back to ``1.0`` (the M4 default). The legacy monolith derives it as ``total_strain / strain_rate``; the M6 action forwards the same value.

growth_factor.name: growth_factor
growth_factor.doc: Phase M15-3 grow-back multiplier applied to the effective ``dt`` after ``n_successes_before_growth`` consecutive ``accept()`` calls. ``1.0`` (default) disables grow-back, preserving the Wave-11 ``only-ever-shrinks`` behaviour. Typical value ``1.5``–``2.0``. The grown ``dt`` is capped at the nominal step's ``dt_for_step``.

n_successes_before_growth.name: n_successes_before_growth
n_successes_before_growth.doc: Phase M15-3 number of consecutive ``accept()`` calls (i.e. successful load steps without a cutback) that must accumulate before ``growth_factor`` is applied. Default ``1`` means every successful step grows the next step's ``dt``. A cutback resets the streak.

doc: Load-stepping FEM executioner with adaptive cutback.
full_doc:
Load-stepping FEM executioner with adaptive cutback.

Args:
    params: Validated parameter dict (see :meth:`FemQuasiStaticExecutioner.params`).

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered executioner name. ``fem_steady`` solves a single Newton step (steady FEM); ``fem_quasi_static`` runs a load-stepping loop with adaptive cutback; ``fem_transient`` runs an implicit-Euler time loop on the scalar mass + gradient stiffness operators (Phase M5); ``pinn_transient`` trains a PINN over the kernels' strong residuals; ``cp_quasi_static`` drives the crystal-plasticity field with adaptive cutback (Phase M6); ``pfd_steady`` is the linearized steady-state phase-field damage driver (Phase M7); ``staggered`` / ``monolithic`` orchestrate per-variable-group sub-solves (Phase M7 coupling); ``pinn_fem_hybrid`` trains a spatial PINN and uses it as a predictor / initial guess / preconditioner for a FEM Newton corrector (Phase M13; modes registered in :mod:`pinnacle.solvers.hybrid`).

n_steps.name: n_steps
n_steps.doc: Number of load steps in the program.

max_iter.name: max_iter
max_iter.doc: Maximum Newton iterations per load step.

tol.name: tol
tol.doc: **Absolute** residual L2-norm tolerance for Newton convergence. The residual has the units of a nodal force, so on a stiff material (``E`` of order ``1e11`` Pa) the assembled system's floating-point noise floor can sit *above* this value and the absolute test alone can never be met — ``rel_tol`` is the criterion that actually terminates such a solve.

rel_tol.name: rel_tol
rel_tol.doc: **Relative** residual tolerance: the step converges once ``||R|| <= max(rel_tol * ||R_0||, tol)``, where ``||R_0||`` is the first iteration's residual norm. Being scale-free, this is the criterion that works on stiff systems; set it to ``0`` to fall back to the absolute test alone.

initial_load_factor.name: initial_load_factor
initial_load_factor.doc: Initial load factor at step 0 (Phase-35 ``initial_lf``; useful for continuation runs).

target_load_factor.name: target_load_factor
target_load_factor.doc: Final load factor reached at the last step. The function value at ``t=1`` is also applied when a function is set.

load_function.name: load_function
load_function.doc: Optional :class:`Function` name that drives the load factor at each step. Defaults to a linear ramp ``initial_load_factor → target_load_factor``.

ramp_dirichlet.name: ramp_dirichlet
ramp_dirichlet.doc: Scale the Dirichlet values by the load factor at each step, so a displacement-controlled run ramps instead of jumping straight to its final displacement. Default ``false`` — ramping changes the loading *path*, and for a path-dependent material that is a different answer, so every deck written before this option keeps its behaviour. Turn it on for elastoplastic displacement control: a single jump makes the elastic/plastic active set chatter between Newton iterations and the residual stalls instead of converging.

max_cutbacks.name: max_cutbacks
max_cutbacks.doc: Maximum Newton cutbacks per step (Phase-35 contract).

safety_factor.name: safety_factor
safety_factor.doc: Multiplier applied to a step size after a cutback.

snapshots_every.name: snapshots_every
snapshots_every.doc: Record the displacement / strain / stress field every N load steps. ``0`` (the default) records nothing — the executioner only returns the final field, matching the pre-M14-10 behaviour. Set to ``1`` to record at every step; the runner forwards the snapshots to the OutputEngine for the per-timestep feature export. Memory cost grows linearly with the number of steps, so prefer a value of ``1`` / ``5`` / ``10`` for stiff problems.

growth_factor.name: growth_factor
growth_factor.doc: Phase M15-3 grow-back multiplier applied to the effective ``dt`` after ``n_successes_before_growth`` consecutive ``accept()`` calls. ``1.0`` (default) disables grow-back, preserving the Wave-11 ``only-ever-shrinks`` behaviour. Typical value ``1.5``–``2.0``. The grown ``dt`` is capped at the nominal step's ``dt_for_step``, so a run never returns a ``dt`` larger than the load-program step it represents.

n_successes_before_growth.name: n_successes_before_growth
n_successes_before_growth.doc: Phase M15-3 number of consecutive ``accept()`` calls (i.e. successful load steps without a cutback) that must accumulate before ``growth_factor`` is applied. Default ``1`` means every successful step grows the next step's ``dt``. A cutback resets the streak.

:class:`pinnacle.coupling.monolithic.MonolithicCoupler` and performs a
single coupled pass per load step. The M7 contract mirrors the
legacy monolith: one mechanics solve followed by one damage solve,
with the residual norm reported as the convergence criterion. A
true simultaneous Newton solve with a consistent coupled tangent
is left for a future phase (the legacy monolith also stopped at
the single-pass scaffold).
