Phase-field PINN executioner implementing Algorithm PF-PINN.

Args:
    params: Validated parameter dict (see :meth:`PfPinnExecutioner.params`).

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered executioner name. ``fem_steady`` solves a single Newton step (steady FEM); ``fem_quasi_static`` runs a load-stepping loop with adaptive cutback; ``fem_transient`` runs an implicit-Euler time loop on the scalar mass + gradient stiffness operators (Phase M5); ``pinn_transient`` trains a PINN over the kernels' strong residuals; ``cp_quasi_static`` drives the crystal-plasticity field with adaptive cutback (Phase M6); ``pfd_steady`` is the linearized steady-state phase-field damage driver (Phase M7); ``staggered`` / ``monolithic`` orchestrate per-variable-group sub-solves (Phase M7 coupling); ``pinn_fem_hybrid`` trains a spatial PINN and uses it as a predictor / initial guess / preconditioner for a FEM Newton corrector (Phase M13; modes registered in :mod:`pinnacle.solvers.hybrid`).

n_steps.name: n_steps
n_steps.doc: Number of time steps into the horizon. With ``t_max`` unset the horizon length is ``n_steps * dt``; with ``t_max`` set the step size is ``(t_max - t_min) / n_steps``.

dt.name: dt
dt.doc: Time-step size used to build the horizon (with ``t_max`` unset). The PINN samples collocation continuously in time; ``dt`` only fixes the horizon length.

t_max.name: t_max
t_max.doc: Optional explicit end of the time horizon; when set it overrides ``n_steps * dt`` and re-derives ``dt``.

slabs.name: slabs
slabs.doc: Number of equal-width time slabs in the curriculum. ``1`` is the single-window baseline the ablation compares against; the slab loop advances slab by slab with the configured continuity mode.

continuity.name: continuity
continuity.doc: How consecutive slabs stay continuous. ``data`` (bc-PINN, Mattey & Ghosh): one shared network, and each slab after the first carries a data constraint pinning the field at the slab's initial face to the frozen pre-slab prediction. ``reinit``: every slab restarts from a fresh network whose IC-exact ansatz base is the previous slab's frozen terminal field — continuity at the face is structural.

slab_epochs.name: slab_epochs
slab_epochs.doc: Adam epochs per slab (the per-slab training budget).

lbfgs_iters.name: lbfgs_iters
lbfgs_iters.doc: Optional L-BFGS polish iterations after each slab's Adam run.

lbfgs_lr.name: lbfgs_lr
lbfgs_lr.doc: L-BFGS learning rate (step size for the line search).

stall_patience.name: stall_patience
stall_patience.doc: Loss-history window for the stall test; when the per-slab loss shows no relative improvement over this many epochs, the slab is halved (Wight & Zhao's window reduction) and training restarts on the first half. ``0`` disables stall-triggered halving.

stall_rel_tol.name: stall_rel_tol
stall_rel_tol.doc: Relative improvement required over the stall window for the slab to count as still improving.

max_halvings.name: max_halvings
max_halvings.doc: Maximum number of times any slab may be halved.

stagger_period.name: stagger_period
stagger_period.doc: Steps per staggered stage (Sharp-PINNs). Kernel groups alternate every ``stagger_period`` steps and the collocation set is resampled every second period. ``0`` trains all groups jointly.

stagger_groups.name: stagger_groups
stagger_groups.doc: Kernel groups as comma-separated ``[Kernels]`` sub-block names, one group per stage (e.g. ``['time_deriv, transport', 'chempot']`` for the split Cahn-Hilliard pair). Empty means one joint group over every kernel bound to a PINN variable.

architecture.name: architecture
architecture.doc: Network architecture. ``modified_mlp`` (Wang et al. gated features) and ``random_weight_factorization`` (trainable per-entry weight scales) counteract the spectral bias that keeps a plain tanh MLP from resolving diffuse interfaces.

hidden_layers.name: hidden_layers
hidden_layers.doc: Number of hidden layers in each per-variable network.

fourier_features.name: fourier_features
fourier_features.doc: Apply the Fourier positional encoding to the (normalised) network input, keeping the encoding inside the autodiff graph so the residual sees its derivative contribution.

transform_bounded.name: transform_bounded
transform_bounded.doc: Hard-bounded order parameter: ``u = lo + (hi - lo) * 0.5 * (1 + tanh(psi / sqrt(2)))`` on output component 0 (the MOOSE linearised-interface transform), so the field respects ``[bound_lower, bound_upper]`` for any weights.

bound_lower.name: bound_lower
bound_lower.doc: Lower bound of the bounded transform (e.g. 0 for an order parameter, -1 for a symmetric Cahn-Hilliard concentration).

bound_upper.name: bound_upper
bound_upper.doc: Upper bound of the bounded transform.

transform_simplex.name: transform_simplex
transform_simplex.doc: Softmax-normalise all output components so their sum is exactly 1 (multiphase fractions). Mutually exclusive with ``transform_bounded`` on the same variable; the simplex wins.

transform_ic_exact.name: transform_ic_exact
transform_ic_exact.doc: IC-exact ansatz ``u = base(x) + (t - t_anchor) * N(x, t)``: the base (the deck IC, or the previous slab's frozen field under ``continuity=reinit``) is attained exactly at the anchor time for any weights, which removes the IC penalty term entirely.

ic_exact_variables.name: ic_exact_variables
ic_exact_variables.doc: Restrict the IC-exact ansatz to these variable names. Empty means every PINN variable. Name the conserved field explicitly (e.g. ``['c']``) on a split Cahn-Hilliard deck so the chemical potential - which has no initial condition of its own - stays unanchored. In ``reinit`` continuity the same list selects which variables receive the previous slab's frozen field as their ansatz base.

bounded_variables.name: bounded_variables
bounded_variables.doc: Restrict the bounded transform to these variable names. Empty means every PINN variable - which is wrong for a split Cahn-Hilliard deck whose chemical potential is unbounded; name the order-parameter variable(s) there.

init_output_scale.name: init_output_scale
init_output_scale.doc: Scale applied to the output layer's random init when ``transform_ic_exact`` is active, so the composed field starts near (not randomly far from) its base. ``0`` pins the start exactly to the base — best for anchored-static decks (an equilibrium interface the model must hold), while a small positive value keeps the symmetry breaking a dynamical deck's optimiser uses. The anchor-time IC is exact for any value (the ansatz's time multiplier kills the correction there).

transform_periodic.name: transform_periodic
transform_periodic.doc: Periodic coordinate embedding: each selected axis is replaced by ``[sin(pi x), cos(pi x)]`` on the normalised coordinate, making the network exactly periodic across the domain boundary on that axis for any weights.

periodic_axes.name: periodic_axes
periodic_axes.doc: Spatial axes to embed periodically (0-based). Empty means every spatial axis when ``transform_periodic=true``.

bc_mode.name: bc_mode
bc_mode.doc: How homogeneous Dirichlet BCs are applied. ``soft`` adds a penalty weighted by ``w_dirichlet``; ``hard`` multiplies the transformed field by a distance mask that vanishes on the constrained planes (exact only for zero values on axis-aligned boundary planes; everything else keeps the soft penalty).

weighting.name: weighting
weighting.doc: Loss-weighting strategy. ``fixed`` keeps the declared ``w_*`` weights; ``gradient`` balances the per-term weights by inverse gradient norm every step (the grad-norm variant of the NTK weighting in the mitigation stack, via ``AdaptiveWeighter``).

w_physics.name: w_physics
w_physics.doc: Weight of the physics (strong-residual) loss term.

w_dirichlet.name: w_dirichlet
w_dirichlet.doc: Weight of the Dirichlet penalty term.

w_neumann.name: w_neumann
w_neumann.doc: Weight of the flux-Neumann penalty term.

w_ic.name: w_ic
w_ic.doc: Weight of the initial-condition penalty (when not structural).

w_continuity.name: w_continuity
w_continuity.doc: Weight of the slab-interface data term (``continuity=data``).

w_mass.name: w_mass
w_mass.doc: Weight of the mass-invariant term ``w_mass * (mean(c) * measure - reference)^2`` (Algorithm PF-PINN step 5's lambda_M L_M). Zero disables it. The pointwise conservation residual does not constrain the spatial mean of ``c`` beyond the boundary flux, so a deck that needs the drift pinned declares this term.

mass_variable.name: mass_variable
mass_variable.doc: Variable whose domain integral the mass term pins. Empty means the first PINN variable. Only consumed when ``w_mass is positive``.

residual_form.name: residual_form
residual_form.doc: P6 residual form. 'strong' penalises the pointwise PDE residual through autodiff (second derivatives included). 'weak' integrates the residual against element-patch polynomial test functions on a declared partition of the scaled space-time box (halving the derivative order: one autodiff pass per field instead of the Laplacian's second pass). 'energy' minimises the Allen-Cahn-family Lyapunov functional F = int f(eta) + kappa/2 |grad eta|^2 dOmega directly (the CH pair has no scalar energy form and is refused). Both weak and energy reuse the P1 closure layer for f and its derivatives.

test_degree.name: test_degree
test_degree.doc: Element-patch polynomial degree of the weak-form test space (Berrone et al.): 1 = Q1 corner nodes, 2 = Q2 with mid-edge nodes. Only consumed when residual_form is 'weak'.

quadrature_order.name: quadrature_order
quadrature_order.doc: Gauss-Legendre points per axis for the weak-form quadrature. Only consumed when residual_form is 'weak' or 'energy'.

weak_patches.name: weak_patches
weak_patches.doc: Patches of the hp-VPINN partition of the spatial box (1-D). Only consumed when residual_form is 'weak' or 'energy'. The bubble test functions live on the patches, so the partition must RESOLVE the interface: choose it so a patch is at most about two interface widths sqrt(kappa / (8 W)) (the acceptance test uses 32 patches on an 8-long box for a 0.11-wide kink; 4 patches sharpen that kink to half its width because the test space cannot see it).

weak_time_levels.name: weak_time_levels
weak_time_levels.doc: Time levels sampled per slab for the weak/energy loss average. Only consumed when residual_form is 'weak' or 'energy'.

causal.name: causal
causal.doc: Causal temporal weighting (Wang et al.): within each slab the collocation time axis is split into segments and each point's residual is weighted by the cumulative residual of *earlier* segments, so late times only train once early ones are satisfied.

causal_epsilon.name: causal_epsilon
causal_epsilon.doc: Causality strength epsilon (``w_n = exp(-eps * sum earlier)``).

causal_segments.name: causal_segments
causal_segments.doc: Number of equal-width time segments the causal weights use per slab.

causal_update_every.name: causal_update_every
causal_update_every.doc: Recompute the causal weights every this many Adam epochs.

sampling.name: sampling
sampling.doc: Collocation strategy. ``uniform`` draws the initial space-time slab uniformly; ``residual_adaptive`` seeds the draw the same way and names the growth rule explicitly; ``interface_biased`` grows the set where the primary field's gradient is steepest. Every resampling event (``resample_every`` > 0) grows the set by the residual (RAD/RAR-D) rule unless ``interface_biased`` is declared (Algorithm PF-PINN step 8: the interface occupies O(w/L) of the domain, so a uniform set alone starves it).

interface_bias_fraction.name: interface_bias_fraction
interface_bias_fraction.doc: Fraction of extra collocation points pulled toward the current field's steepest gradient (the interface) at the start of each slab. ``0`` disables the interface-biased pool.

resample_every.name: resample_every
resample_every.doc: Residual-adaptive resampling cadence in Adam epochs. With staggering active and this unset, the Sharp-PINNs cadence ``2 * stagger_period`` applies. ``0`` with no staggering disables resampling.

resample_add.name: resample_add
resample_add.doc: Number of collocation points added at each resample.

resample_max.name: resample_max
resample_max.doc: Cap on the total collocation count under resampling (0 = uncapped).

collocation_interior.name: collocation_interior
collocation_interior.doc: Number of interior collocation points (spatial, shared across slabs).

collocation_boundary.name: collocation_boundary
collocation_boundary.doc: Number of boundary collocation points per node/side set.

time_strata.name: time_strata
time_strata.doc: Number of equal time sub-windows the interior collocation set is stratified over within each slab. Stratification makes every stratum a near-uniform spatial slice, which is what keeps the purely spatial residual terms (the chemical-potential row) from blowing up between scattered space-time samples. ``1`` recovers joint space-time sampling.

nondim.name: nondim
nondim.doc: Non-dimensionalisation block. ``auto`` derives the characteristic time from the kernels' coefficients (AC: ``tau = L0^2/(L*kappa)``; CH: ``tau = L0^4/(M*kappa)``) and reports it with the nondimensional groups; ``manual`` uses the declared ``nondim_time``; ``none`` reports only the coordinate normalisation. The reported factors land in the result dict and summary.json either way.

nondim_length.name: nondim_length
nondim_length.doc: Characteristic length L0 for the nondimensional groups. ``0`` uses the largest domain span.

n_grid.name: n_grid
n_grid.doc: Points per axis of the uniform grid used for the invariant reports.

seed.name: seed
seed.doc: RNG seed for this run. Defaults to the deck's ``global.seed``; the backend RNG is seeded once at the top of ``run`` and every later draw derives from it.

name: pfd_steady
doc: Linearized steady-state phase-field damage executioner.
full_doc:
Linearized steady-state phase-field damage executioner.

Args:
    params: Validated parameter dict (see :meth:`PFDSteadyExecutioner.params`).

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered executioner name. ``fem_steady`` solves a single Newton step (steady FEM); ``fem_quasi_static`` runs a load-stepping loop with adaptive cutback; ``fem_transient`` runs an implicit-Euler time loop on the scalar mass + gradient stiffness operators (Phase M5); ``pinn_transient`` trains a PINN over the kernels' strong residuals; ``cp_quasi_static`` drives the crystal-plasticity field with adaptive cutback (Phase M6); ``pfd_steady`` is the linearized steady-state phase-field damage driver (Phase M7); ``staggered`` / ``monolithic`` orchestrate per-variable-group sub-solves (Phase M7 coupling); ``pinn_fem_hybrid`` trains a spatial PINN and uses it as a predictor / initial guess / preconditioner for a FEM Newton corrector (Phase M13; modes registered in :mod:`pinnacle.solvers.hybrid`).

n_load_steps.name: n_load_steps
n_load_steps.doc: Number of load steps (the legacy ``[PhaseFieldDamage] n_load_steps`` knob). The executioner is monotone in step_factor; ``n_load_steps = 1`` reproduces the legacy single-solve signature.

boundary_node_set.name: boundary_node_set
boundary_node_set.doc: Node set on which homogeneous Dirichlet ``boundary_damage`` is applied. The legacy default is ``all_boundary``; the composed path may declare a smaller node set on a deck-by-deck basis.

boundary_damage.name: boundary_damage
boundary_damage.doc: Value of the homogeneous Dirichlet condition on the damage field.

prescribed_driving.name: prescribed_driving
prescribed_driving.doc: Optional prescribed driving-energy block (the legacy ``driving_field`` sub-block). When present, the executioner feeds the prescribed energy to the history field at every load step.

scalar_field_name.name: scalar_field_name
scalar_field_name.doc: Name under which the field is exposed in the result dict (the legacy monolith used ``damage``; the composed path uses the kernel's variable name).

name: pinn_fem_hybrid
doc: PINN+FEM hybrid executioner (Phase M13).
full_doc:
PINN+FEM hybrid executioner (Phase M13).

Trains a spatial PINN on the registered kernel's strong residuals
and uses the trained field as a predictor for a FEM Newton solve.
The coupling mode is selected by registered name; the FEM
corrector is the registered
:class:`~pinnacle.solvers.hybrid.PinnFEMHybridSolver`.

The executioner is **physics-agnostic**: the kernel owns the
constitutive law (linear elastic, crystal plasticity, phase field,
…) and the residual form. The executioner orchestrates training
and the subsequent Newton refinement.

Args:
    params: Validated ``[Executioner]`` parameter dict (see
        :meth:`params`).

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered executioner name. ``fem_steady`` solves a single Newton step (steady FEM); ``fem_quasi_static`` runs a load-stepping loop with adaptive cutback; ``fem_transient`` runs an implicit-Euler time loop on the scalar mass + gradient stiffness operators (Phase M5); ``pinn_transient`` trains a PINN over the kernels' strong residuals; ``cp_quasi_static`` drives the crystal-plasticity field with adaptive cutback (Phase M6); ``pfd_steady`` is the linearized steady-state phase-field damage driver (Phase M7); ``staggered`` / ``monolithic`` orchestrate per-variable-group sub-solves (Phase M7 coupling); ``pinn_fem_hybrid`` trains a spatial PINN and uses it as a predictor / initial guess / preconditioner for a FEM Newton corrector (Phase M13; modes registered in :mod:`pinnacle.solvers.hybrid`).

collocation_interior.name: collocation_interior
collocation_interior.doc: Number of interior collocation points sampled per epoch.

collocation_boundary.name: collocation_boundary
collocation_boundary.doc: Number of boundary collocation points sampled per side / node set.

bc_mode.name: bc_mode
bc_mode.doc: How Dirichlet BCs are applied to the PINN predictor. ``soft`` adds a penalty term to the loss, weighted by ``w_dirichlet``. ``hard`` multiplies the network output by a distance mask that vanishes on the constrained planes, so the BC holds exactly for any network weights. The mask is exact only for a **zero** value prescribed on a node set lying in an axis-aligned plane of the domain bounding box; every other Dirichlet BC keeps the soft penalty. Note the FEM corrector applies all Dirichlet BCs strongly regardless of this setting — ``bc_mode`` only shapes the predictor.

residual_form.name: residual_form
residual_form.doc: Residual form fed to the PINN. ``strong`` minimises the L2 norm of the strong-form PDE residual; ``energy`` minimises the total potential energy.

adam_epochs.name: adam_epochs
adam_epochs.doc: Adam epochs for the PINN predictor.

adam_lr.name: adam_lr
adam_lr.doc: Adam learning rate for the PINN predictor.

lbfgs_iters.name: lbfgs_iters
lbfgs_iters.doc: Optional L-BFGS refinement iters after Adam.

w_physics.name: w_physics
w_physics.doc: Weight of the physics residual loss term.

w_dirichlet.name: w_dirichlet
w_dirichlet.doc: Weight of the Dirichlet penalty term.

w_neumann.name: w_neumann
w_neumann.doc: Weight of the Neumann penalty term.

regularization.name: regularization
regularization.doc: L2 regularisation coefficient on the network weights.

hidden_layers.name: hidden_layers
hidden_layers.doc: Number of hidden layers in the MLP network.

neurons.name: neurons
neurons.doc: Width of each hidden layer in the MLP network.

fourier_features.name: fourier_features
fourier_features.doc: Whether to apply Fourier positional encoding to the network input (Phase 37 ``fourier_features``).

seed.name: seed
seed.doc: Optional RNG seed for the collocation sampler. Defaults to the deck's ``global.seed``.

time_function.name: time_function
time_function.doc: Optional :class:`Function` name for the time-axis sampling (Phase M5). When set, the executioner logs a warning and falls back to a uniform-random sample in ``[t_min, t_max]``; the function-driven path lands in a follow-up phase.

t_min.name: t_min
t_min.doc: Lower bound of the time-axis sample (Phase M5).

t_max.name: t_max
t_max.doc: Upper bound of the time-axis sample (Phase M5).

mode.name: mode
mode.doc: How the PINN prediction is used by the FEM corrector. ``warm_start`` uses the PINN displacement as the Newton initial guess (default); ``predictor_corrector`` alternates PINN prediction and FEM correction with optional online fine-tuning (``online_finetune``); ``preconditioner`` uses the PINN field as the initial iterate for the inner linear CG solve (conservative; the Newton path is untouched); ``increment_predictor`` (Phase M15-2) trains the PINN once on step 1, re-uses the frozen network to predict the increment between steps (warm-start), and reports warm vs cold Newton iterations per step so the user can see whether the warm-start actually paid. All modes are registered strategies in :mod:`pinnacle.solvers.hybrid`.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the ``[Variables]`` entry this executioner corrects. Optional for a standalone deck with one physics; **required in practice** when wired as a sub-block of a coupled deck, where more than one variable carries ``family = fem`` and the fall-back would otherwise assemble the wrong field. When unset the executioner takes the ``fem``-family twin of its PINN variable, then the first ``fem``-family variable, then the PINN variable itself.

accuracy_target.name: accuracy_target
accuracy_target.doc: **Absolute** residual tolerance the FEM-corrected solution must reach. The hybrid corrector returns the same field whether the PINN is correct or only approximate; the FEM corrector guarantees the residual is below this threshold. See ``accuracy_rel_target`` — on a stiff material this target alone is not reachable.

accuracy_rel_target.name: accuracy_rel_target
accuracy_rel_target.doc: **Relative** residual tolerance: the corrector stops once ``||R|| <= max(accuracy_rel_target * ||R_0||, accuracy_target)``, where ``||R_0||`` is the first iteration's residual norm. The residual carries the units of a nodal force, so on a stiff material it bottoms out on the assembled tangent's floating-point noise floor and the absolute target alone can never fire; this scale-free test is what terminates such a solve. Set to ``0`` to use the absolute target alone.

max_pinn_budget.name: max_pinn_budget
max_pinn_budget.doc: Cap on total PINN fine-tune epochs (0 = unlimited). Only used by ``predictor_corrector`` mode.

fem_max_iter.name: fem_max_iter
fem_max_iter.doc: Maximum Newton iterations for the FEM corrector.

linear_method.name: linear_method
linear_method.doc: Linear solver for the Newton corrector. ``direct`` uses dense NumPy; ``cg`` uses conjugate-gradient and is the natural target for the ``preconditioner`` mode.

linear_tol.name: linear_tol
linear_tol.doc: Linear-system residual tolerance for the FEM corrector.

n_load_steps.name: n_load_steps
n_load_steps.doc: Number of pseudo-time load steps for ``predictor_corrector`` mode. The traction vector is scaled linearly from 0 to 1 across the steps.

online_finetune.name: online_finetune
online_finetune.doc: Enable online fine-tuning of the PINN on the corrected field after each load step (only ``predictor_corrector``).

finetune_epochs.name: finetune_epochs
finetune_epochs.doc: Adam epochs per online fine-tune step.

finetune_lr.name: finetune_lr
finetune_lr.doc: Learning rate for the online fine-tune step.

fem_tol.name: fem_tol
fem_tol.doc: Residual L2-norm tolerance for the standalone Newton fallback.

fem_tangent_method.name: fem_tangent_method
fem_tangent_method.doc: Tangent computation method for the FEM corrector. ``analytic`` uses the material's ``tangent()`` callback; ``autodiff`` uses the backend Jacobian.

name: pinn_fem_hybrid_coupled_physics
doc: Orchestrate staggered / monolithic coupling between FEM and PINN components.
full_doc:
Orchestrate staggered / monolithic coupling between FEM and PINN components.

This executioner does **not** implement physics residuals directly. Instead,
it selects a coupling strategy (via the ``mode`` parameter) and delegates
to that strategy's fixed-point loop. The default mode is ``cp_pfd``
(crystal-plasticity state on mesh ↔ phase-field damage as PINN field).

**Extensibility:** To add a new coupled-physics mode, create a
:class:`CoupledPhysicsStrategy` subclass and register it with
:func:`register_coupled_mode`. The executioner core is never edited — only
the strategy module grows and the ``allowed`` tuple on ``params().mode``
gains one new value.

Parameters follow CLAUDE.md §3 — backend isolation, GPU policy via config,
precision honouring, type hints everywhere, and a documented ``params()``
declaration.

Args:
    params: Validated parameter dict (see :meth:`params`).

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered executioner name. ``fem_steady`` solves a single Newton step (steady FEM); ``fem_quasi_static`` runs a load-stepping loop with adaptive cutback; ``fem_transient`` runs an implicit-Euler time loop on the scalar mass + gradient stiffness operators (Phase M5); ``pinn_transient`` trains a PINN over the kernels' strong residuals; ``cp_quasi_static`` drives the crystal-plasticity field with adaptive cutback (Phase M6); ``pfd_steady`` is the linearized steady-state phase-field damage driver (Phase M7); ``staggered`` / ``monolithic`` orchestrate per-variable-group sub-solves (Phase M7 coupling); ``pinn_fem_hybrid`` trains a spatial PINN and uses it as a predictor / initial guess / preconditioner for a FEM Newton corrector (Phase M13; modes registered in :mod:`pinnacle.solvers.hybrid`).

mode.name: mode
mode.doc: Coupling mode: selects the coupled-physics protocol. Each mode wires together a mesh-based solver (FEM) and a PINN field with dedicated bridge logic. Currently available: ``cp_pfd`` (crystal-plasticity state on mesh ↔ phase-field damage as PINN field) and ``j2_pfd_hybrid`` (the same split with J2 isotropic hardening on the mesh, driven by the rate-independent ``fem_quasi_static`` sub-solver instead of the CP one). Future modes will be added here without changing this executioner's core — they are registered strategies, not elif branches. Add new mode names by extending the ``allowed`` tuple and registering a strategy class with ``@register_coupled_mode``.

coupling_iters.name: coupling_iters
coupling_iters.doc: Maximum fixed-point iterations in the staggered / monolithic coupling loop. Each iteration alternates FEM and PINN sub-solves.

coupling_tol.name: coupling_tol
coupling_tol.doc: Convergence tolerance for the fixed-point residual norm. The loop terminates when ``||d_new - d_old|| < coupling_tol`` (measured in the norm specified by ``coupling_resid_norm``).

coupling_resid_norm.name: coupling_resid_norm
coupling_resid_norm.doc: Norm used to measure the coupling residual between successive fixed-point steps. ``l2`` is the Euclidean norm, ``l1`` is the sum of absolute values, ``linf`` is the maximum absolute value.

damage_gd_func.name: damage_gd_func
damage_gd_func.doc: Degradation function ``g(d)`` applied to the elastic tangent. Options: ``'(1-d)^2'`` (default, quadratic), ``'1-d'`` (linear), ``'(1-d)^3'`` (cubic). For cp_pfd mode this is used in both the stress and the PFD driving-force computation. See :func:`coupling.degradation.degradation_function` for the closed-form expressions.

mechanics.name: mechanics
mechanics.doc: ``[./mechanics]`` sub-block: the mesh-side sub-executioner and its parameters. ``type`` names any registered FEM executioner (``cp_quasi_static`` for a crystal-plasticity field — the default — or ``fem_quasi_static`` for the elastic limit); the remaining keys are that executioner's own. It must return a ``strain`` field, because the Miehe split of that strain is what drives damage.

damage.name: damage
damage.doc: ``[./damage]`` sub-block: the PINN-side sub-executioner and its parameters. ``type`` defaults to ``pinn_fem_hybrid`` (train the ``pfd_evolution`` strong residual, then drive a Newton corrector to FEM tolerance); the remaining keys — ``adam_epochs``, ``collocation_interior``, ``hidden_layers``, … — are that executioner's own and are documented on its page.

fem.name: fem
fem.doc: ``[./fem]`` sub-block (pf_transport mode): the conserved-side sub-executioner. ``type`` defaults to ``pf_fem_transient`` — the split Cahn-Hilliard block-Newton transient, which owns the mass and the no-flux boundary conditions; the remaining keys are its own (``n_steps``, ``dt``, ``scheme``, ...).

pinn.name: pinn
pinn.doc: ``[./pinn]`` sub-block (pf_transport mode): the order-parameter sub-executioner. ``type`` defaults to ``pf_pinn``; the remaining keys are that executioner's own (``slabs``, ``slab_epochs``, ...).

coupling_material.name: coupling_material
coupling_material.doc: pf_transport mode: the phase_coupling [Materials] entry that carries the two-way exchange (eta -> mobility scaling, concentration -> eta driving force). Empty means the coupling is one-directional and the fixed-point loop converges on the eta residual immediately.

classical_fallback_fraction_max.name: classical_fallback_fraction_max
classical_fallback_fraction_max.doc: Maximum fraction of quadrature points allowed to fall back to the classical CP integrator during coupling. If more points than this threshold revert, the run logs a warning — the surrogate (future work, ADR 0016) has left its validity band. Until the integrated surrogate ships, this value is always 1.0 and the warning is suppressed.

name: pinn_transient
doc: PINN executioner: collocation + composite loss + Adam/L-BFGS trainer.
full_doc:
PINN executioner: collocation + composite loss + Adam/L-BFGS trainer.

Args:
    params: Validated parameter dict (see :meth:`PinnTransientExecutioner.params`).

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered executioner name. ``fem_steady`` solves a single Newton step (steady FEM); ``fem_quasi_static`` runs a load-stepping loop with adaptive cutback; ``fem_transient`` runs an implicit-Euler time loop on the scalar mass + gradient stiffness operators (Phase M5); ``pinn_transient`` trains a PINN over the kernels' strong residuals; ``cp_quasi_static`` drives the crystal-plasticity field with adaptive cutback (Phase M6); ``pfd_steady`` is the linearized steady-state phase-field damage driver (Phase M7); ``staggered`` / ``monolithic`` orchestrate per-variable-group sub-solves (Phase M7 coupling); ``pinn_fem_hybrid`` trains a spatial PINN and uses it as a predictor / initial guess / preconditioner for a FEM Newton corrector (Phase M13; modes registered in :mod:`pinnacle.solvers.hybrid`).

collocation_interior.name: collocation_interior
collocation_interior.doc: Number of interior collocation points sampled per epoch.

collocation_boundary.name: collocation_boundary
collocation_boundary.doc: Number of boundary collocation points sampled per side set.

resample_every.name: resample_every
resample_every.doc: Residual-adaptive refinement (RAR): re-sample the interior collocation set every N Adam epochs, adding points where the strong-form residual is largest. This is the PINN's counterpart to mesh h-refinement — the network cannot be given smaller elements, but it can be shown more of the region it is getting wrong. ``0`` disables it (the default), because on a smooth solution it costs time and buys little; it pays on sharp layers, crack tips and stress concentrations. Requires ``resample_add > 0``.

resample_add.name: resample_add
resample_add.doc: Number of collocation points added at each residual-adaptive resample. New points are drawn near existing points chosen with probability proportional to their residual magnitude, then jittered within the domain. Ignored unless ``resample_every > 0``.

resample_max.name: resample_max
resample_max.doc: Cap on the total interior collocation count under adaptive refinement. ``0`` means uncapped, so the set grows by ``resample_add`` at every resample; set it to bound memory and per-epoch cost on a long run.

resample_method.name: resample_method
resample_method.doc: Residual-adaptive sampler variant (Phase 42/HT-4). 'adaptive': jitter parents proportional to |r| (the original RAR). 'rad': Wu et al. 2023 RAD weights |r|^k/mean(|r|^k) + c, growing the set. 'rar_d': the budget-capped RAD variant — keeps the best points and replaces the 'resample_add' worst, so the set size never grows.

resample_k.name: resample_k
resample_k.doc: RAD/RAR-D weight exponent k (sharpens the bias toward high residual).

resample_c.name: resample_c
resample_c.doc: RAD/RAR-D floor constant c (keeps the whole domain sampled).

density_function.name: density_function
density_function.doc: Optional [Functions] entry (e.g. 'ellipsoid_path') whose value at each collocation point multiplicatively scales the 'rad'/'rar_d' sampling weight — the function-driven collocation density that concentrates points around a moving source. A transient batch's per-row time is passed to the function as t=. Only valid with resample_method = 'rad' or 'rar_d'.

bc_mode.name: bc_mode
bc_mode.doc: How Dirichlet BCs are applied. ``soft`` adds a penalty term to the loss, weighted by ``w_dirichlet``. ``hard`` multiplies the network output by a distance mask that vanishes on the constrained planes, so the BC is satisfied exactly for any network weights and no penalty is needed. The mask is exact only for a **zero** value prescribed on a node set lying in an axis-aligned plane of the domain bounding box; any Dirichlet BC that does not qualify (non-zero value, curved or interior node set) keeps the soft penalty, so the two modes coexist on the same deck.

residual_form.name: residual_form
residual_form.doc: Residual form fed to the PINN. ``strong`` minimises the L2 norm of the strong-form PDE residual; ``energy`` minimises the total potential energy.

w_physics.name: w_physics
w_physics.doc: Weight of the physics residual loss term.

w_dirichlet.name: w_dirichlet
w_dirichlet.doc: Weight of the Dirichlet penalty term.

w_neumann.name: w_neumann
w_neumann.doc: Weight of the Neumann penalty term.

regularization.name: regularization
regularization.doc: L2 regularisation coefficient on the network weights.

hidden_layers.name: hidden_layers
hidden_layers.doc: Number of hidden layers in the MLP network.

neurons.name: neurons
neurons.doc: Width of each hidden layer in the MLP network.

fourier_features.name: fourier_features
fourier_features.doc: Whether to apply Fourier positional encoding to the network input (Phase 37 ``fourier_features``).

seed.name: seed
seed.doc: Optional RNG seed for the collocation sampler. Defaults to the deck's ``global.seed``.

time_function.name: time_function
time_function.doc: Optional :class:`Function` name for the time-axis sampling (Phase M5). When set, the executioner logs a warning and falls back to a uniform-random sample in ``[t_min, t_max]``; the function-driven path lands in a follow-up phase.

t_min.name: t_min
t_min.doc: Lower bound of the time-axis sample (Phase M5).

t_max.name: t_max
t_max.doc: Upper bound of the time-axis sample (Phase M5).

calibration_mode.name: calibration_mode
calibration_mode.doc: How a deck-declared [Calibration] block is consumed. Currently the spatial ``pinn_transient`` executioner accepts the parameter for compatibility with ``cp_constitutive`` but logs a warning when the mode is non-empty (the spatial data-term / inverse path lands in Phase M13).

calibration_sources.name: calibration_sources
calibration_sources.doc: List of calibration sources. See :class:`~pinnacle.system.executioner.cp_constitutive.CPConstitutiveExecutioner` for the entry shape. Reserved for M13.

calibration_strain_rate.name: calibration_strain_rate
calibration_strain_rate.doc: Strain rate used to convert strain-axis CSV data into time.

inverse_parameters.name: inverse_parameters
inverse_parameters.doc: Material parameters to recover in inverse mode (reserved for M13).

inverse_lr.name: inverse_lr
inverse_lr.doc: Adam learning rate for inverse mode (reserved for M13).

inverse_max_epochs.name: inverse_max_epochs
inverse_max_epochs.doc: Max Adam epochs for inverse mode (reserved for M13).

inverse_tol.name: inverse_tol
inverse_tol.doc: Convergence tolerance for inverse mode (reserved for M13).

name: pinn_two_field
doc: Two-field PINN executioner with staggered Adam and irreversibility ansatz.
full_doc:
Two-field PINN executioner with staggered Adam and irreversibility ansatz.

Args:
    params: Validated parameter dict (see :meth:`PinnTwoFieldExecutioner.params`).

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered executioner name. ``fem_steady`` solves a single Newton step (steady FEM); ``fem_quasi_static`` runs a load-stepping loop with adaptive cutback; ``fem_transient`` runs an implicit-Euler time loop on the scalar mass + gradient stiffness operators (Phase M5); ``pinn_transient`` trains a PINN over the kernels' strong residuals; ``cp_quasi_static`` drives the crystal-plasticity field with adaptive cutback (Phase M6); ``pfd_steady`` is the linearized steady-state phase-field damage driver (Phase M7); ``staggered`` / ``monolithic`` orchestrate per-variable-group sub-solves (Phase M7 coupling); ``pinn_fem_hybrid`` trains a spatial PINN and uses it as a predictor / initial guess / preconditioner for a FEM Newton corrector (Phase M13; modes registered in :mod:`pinnacle.solvers.hybrid`).

collocation_interior.name: collocation_interior
collocation_interior.doc: Number of interior collocation points sampled per epoch (shared).

collocation_boundary.name: collocation_boundary
collocation_boundary.doc: Number of boundary collocation points per side / node set (per variable).

bc_mode.name: bc_mode
bc_mode.doc: How Dirichlet BCs are applied. ``hard`` (default for Stage D) multiplies each network's output by a distance mask that vanishes on the constrained planes; ``soft`` adds a penalty term. The hard transform is exact only for a **zero** value prescribed on a node set lying in an axis-aligned plane of the domain bounding box; the damage variable's ``d = 0`` boundary condition qualifies and is enforced exactly. The displacement variable's non-zero ``u = 0.001`` pull is also maskable when the node set sits in an axis-aligned plane.

residual_form.name: residual_form
residual_form.doc: Residual form fed to the PINN. Stage D uses strong.

stagger_super_epochs.name: stagger_super_epochs
stagger_super_epochs.doc: Number of outer passes over the per-variable networks. Each super-epoch visits every PINN-family variable in the deck-declared order with the others frozen. The two-field PINN requires staggered training because a joint loss has a trivial minimiser at ``u = 0``, ``d = 0``.

stagger_inner_steps.name: stagger_inner_steps
stagger_inner_steps.doc: Adam steps per network per super-epoch (1 is the published default).

stagger_order.name: stagger_order
stagger_order.doc: Per-super-epoch visit order. ``u_then_d`` updates the displacement network first; ``d_then_u`` swaps them; ``alternating`` flips the order each super-epoch.

adam_lr_u.name: adam_lr_u
adam_lr_u.doc: Adam learning rate for the displacement network.

adam_lr_d.name: adam_lr_d
adam_lr_d.doc: Adam learning rate for the damage network.

w_physics.name: w_physics
w_physics.doc: Weight of the physics residual loss term (per network).

w_dirichlet.name: w_dirichlet
w_dirichlet.doc: Weight of the Dirichlet penalty term (per network, soft mode only).

w_neumann.name: w_neumann
w_neumann.doc: Weight of the Neumann penalty term (per network).

hidden_layers.name: hidden_layers
hidden_layers.doc: Number of hidden layers in each MLP network.

neurons.name: neurons
neurons.doc: Width of each hidden layer in each MLP network.

fourier_features.name: fourier_features
fourier_features.doc: Whether to apply Fourier positional encoding to the network input.

damage_upper_bound.name: damage_upper_bound
damage_upper_bound.doc: Upper physical bound for the damage network output (item 1 of ADR 0014's *What would close the Case-2 tolerance* list). The damage PINN clamps ``raw → clip(raw, 0, damage_upper_bound)`` so the field respects ``d ≤ damage_upper_bound`` by construction. The bundled Stage D deck uses ``1.0`` (the physical upper limit). The first revision of Stage D only clamped the lower bound, which let the raw network output overshoot ~1.4 at ``x = 0`` and miss the Case-2 tolerance.

u_increment_predictor.name: u_increment_predictor
u_increment_predictor.doc: Whether to wrap the displacement network in a linear-residual ansatz (item 2 of ADR 0014's fix list, the M15-2 increment-prediction lesson applied to Stage D). The closed-form linear-elastic reference ``u_ref(x)`` interpolates the prescribed Dirichlet values along the bar, and the MLP's correction is gated through ``(1 - mask)`` so the BC is satisfied by ``u_ref`` alone. The displacement network only learns the residual left by the damage coupling; the soft-Dirichlet penalty on the non-zero ``u = 1e-3`` pull no longer fights the Adam optimiser. Only supported in 1-D and only when every displacement Dirichlet BC is hard-maskable (zero value on an axis-aligned plane).

seed.name: seed
seed.doc: Optional RNG seed for the collocation sampler.

young.name: young
young.doc: Optional Young's modulus override for the 1-D history-field closure. When unset the executioner reads ``E`` from the first ``stress_divergence`` kernel bound to the displacement variable.

poisson.name: poisson
poisson.doc: Optional Poisson's ratio override for the 1-D history-field closure. The tension/compression split that produces the damage driving force is written in Lamé constants, so it needs ``ν`` as well as ``E``. When unset the executioner reads it from the first ``stress_divergence`` kernel bound to the displacement variable.

damage_bound_mode.name: damage_bound_mode
damage_bound_mode.doc:
How the damage field is confined to ``[0, damage_upper_bound]``.

``smooth`` (default) maps the network output through ``upper · tanh(softplus(raw) / upper)``: strictly inside the interval, and differentiable everywhere. ``clip`` applies a hard ``clip(raw, 0, upper)``, which attains the bounds exactly but is **flat outside them** — a randomly initialised network starts with about half its collocation points in that flat region, receives no gradient there, and the damage field stalls at zero no matter how long it trains. Use ``clip`` only when a run needs the bounds attained exactly and is started from an already-positive field.

loss_balancing.name: loss_balancing
loss_balancing.doc:
Residual non-dimensionalisation strategy. ``none`` feeds each loss term to the optimiser in its raw physical units. ``rms`` divides every term by its own most recently measured magnitude (a detached constant, so the minimiser is unchanged) before the ``w_*`` weights are applied.

Use ``rms`` for any coupled deck in SI units. The two residuals of an elastic + phase-field problem differ by many orders of magnitude — a stress divergence scales with ``E`` (~1e11 Pa) while an AT2 residual scales with ``Gc/l0`` — so with ``none`` the weights cannot express a meaningful balance and whichever term happens to be largest dominates the gradient. Non-dimensionalising the terms is the standard remedy for this gradient-scale imbalance in the PINN literature.

balance_every.name: balance_every
balance_every.doc: Re-measure the ``loss_balancing = rms`` scales every N super-epochs. The residual magnitudes fall as training proceeds, so a scale frozen at the randomly-initialised state stops normalising anything. ``0`` measures once at the start and never again. Ignored when ``loss_balancing = none``.

lbfgs_iters.name: lbfgs_iters
lbfgs_iters.doc: L-BFGS iterations run per network after the staggered Adam schedule finishes (``0`` disables the polish). Adam finds the right basin cheaply but stalls in the flat, ill-conditioned valley a PDE residual leaves behind; a short quasi-Newton pass is what converts that basin into a converged field. It runs once per network with the coupling partner fixed, so it does not reintroduce the two-field non-convexity the staggered schedule exists to avoid.

name: scalar_steady
doc: Steady solve of a scalar-transport equation assembled from its terms.
full_doc:
Steady solve of a scalar-transport equation assembled from its terms.

Drives Poisson, steady heat conduction, Helmholtz, and steady
advection–diffusion — whichever the deck's ``[Kernels]`` add up to.

Args:
    params: Validated ``[Executioner]`` parameter dict (see :meth:`params`).

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered executioner name. ``fem_steady`` solves a single Newton step (steady FEM); ``fem_quasi_static`` runs a load-stepping loop with adaptive cutback; ``fem_transient`` runs an implicit-Euler time loop on the scalar mass + gradient stiffness operators (Phase M5); ``pinn_transient`` trains a PINN over the kernels' strong residuals; ``cp_quasi_static`` drives the crystal-plasticity field with adaptive cutback (Phase M6); ``pfd_steady`` is the linearized steady-state phase-field damage driver (Phase M7); ``staggered`` / ``monolithic`` orchestrate per-variable-group sub-solves (Phase M7 coupling); ``pinn_fem_hybrid`` trains a spatial PINN and uses it as a predictor / initial guess / preconditioner for a FEM Newton corrector (Phase M13; modes registered in :mod:`pinnacle.solvers.hybrid`).

linear_method.name: linear_method
linear_method.doc: Linear solver for the assembled system. ``direct`` uses a dense NumPy factorisation, which is appropriate for the mesh sizes the scalar solvers target.

solve_method.name: solve_method
solve_method.doc: ``linear`` (default) performs the original single linear solve, unchanged bit-for-bit. ``newton`` (Phase 39/HT-1) runs a Newton loop over any kernel that declares an ``fem_operators_nonlinear`` hook (e.g. a temperature-dependent 'thermal_conductivity' material bound to 'diffusion', Phase 40); kernels without the hook contribute their ordinary (field-independent) stiffness as their own tangent, so an all-linear deck run with 'newton' converges in exactly one iteration.

newton_tol.name: newton_tol
newton_tol.doc: Absolute residual L2-norm tolerance for ``solve_method = newton`` (finite, >= 0). An infinite tolerance would report iteration 0 as converged with the untouched initial field.

newton_rel_tol.name: newton_rel_tol
newton_rel_tol.doc: Relative residual tolerance (finite, >= 0; against the first iteration's residual norm) for ``solve_method = newton``; see ``solvers/nonlinear.py::NewtonSolver`` for why a relative test is needed alongside the absolute one.

initial_guess.name: initial_guess
initial_guess.doc: ``zero`` (default) starts the Newton loop's free DOFs at zero. ``warm_start`` (Phase 47/HT-9) trains a small PINN against the same kernels' strong-form residual and uses its prediction as the starting field instead — after screening the predicted field's assembled tangent for positive-definiteness; a field that fails the screen falls back to the zero start with a warning, rather than being silently used. Ignored for ``solve_method = linear``.

warm_start_hidden_layers.name: warm_start_hidden_layers
warm_start_hidden_layers.doc: Hidden-layer count for the 'warm_start' predictor network.

warm_start_neurons.name: warm_start_neurons
warm_start_neurons.doc: Neurons per hidden layer for the 'warm_start' predictor network.

warm_start_epochs.name: warm_start_epochs
warm_start_epochs.doc: Adam epochs for training the 'warm_start' predictor network.

warm_start_lr.name: warm_start_lr
warm_start_lr.doc: Adam learning rate for training the 'warm_start' predictor network.

name: staggered
doc: Staggered (alternating-minimization) coupled executioner.
full_doc:
Staggered (alternating-minimization) coupled executioner.

The executioner wraps :class:`pinnacle.coupling.staggered.StaggeredCoupler`
and orchestrates per-variable-group sub-solves until the damage
increment falls below ``tolerance`` or the iteration budget
``max_iterations`` is exhausted. The history field is fixed during
the inner alternating loop; it is updated once per load step with
the converged positive stored energy.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered executioner name. ``fem_steady`` solves a single Newton step (steady FEM); ``fem_quasi_static`` runs a load-stepping loop with adaptive cutback; ``fem_transient`` runs an implicit-Euler time loop on the scalar mass + gradient stiffness operators (Phase M5); ``pinn_transient`` trains a PINN over the kernels' strong residuals; ``cp_quasi_static`` drives the crystal-plasticity field with adaptive cutback (Phase M6); ``pfd_steady`` is the linearized steady-state phase-field damage driver (Phase M7); ``staggered`` / ``monolithic`` orchestrate per-variable-group sub-solves (Phase M7 coupling); ``pinn_fem_hybrid`` trains a spatial PINN and uses it as a predictor / initial guess / preconditioner for a FEM Newton corrector (Phase M13; modes registered in :mod:`pinnacle.solvers.hybrid`).

n_steps.name: n_steps
n_steps.doc: Number of load steps in the coupled program.

max_iterations.name: max_iterations
max_iterations.doc: Maximum number of iterations for the alternating mechanics ↔ damage scheme (staggered) or Newton-like passes (monolithic). Mirrors the legacy ``Coupling`` block.

tolerance.name: tolerance
tolerance.doc: Convergence tolerance on the maximum damage change between iterations. Matches the legacy ``coupling.tolerance`` block.

prescribed_driving.name: prescribed_driving
prescribed_driving.doc: Optional prescribed driving-energy block (the M7 standalone PFD deck's analog of the legacy ``PhaseFieldDamage.driving_field`` block). When present, the executioner feeds the prescribed energy to the history field between staggered iterations instead of evaluating ``ψ⁺`` from the mechanics solve.

void_amplification.name: void_amplification
void_amplification.doc: Optional void-stress amplification block (the legacy Rezwan case's local stress concentration near the spherical void). Forwarded to the damage sub-solve so the driving energy is locally amplified near the void surface.

name: vpinn_steady
doc: Train a network against the discrete steady weak residual ``K T - f``.
full_doc:
Train a network against the discrete steady weak residual ``K T - f``.

Args:
    params: Validated ``[Executioner]`` parameter dict; see :meth:`params`.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered executioner name. ``fem_steady`` solves a single Newton step (steady FEM); ``fem_quasi_static`` runs a load-stepping loop with adaptive cutback; ``fem_transient`` runs an implicit-Euler time loop on the scalar mass + gradient stiffness operators (Phase M5); ``pinn_transient`` trains a PINN over the kernels' strong residuals; ``cp_quasi_static`` drives the crystal-plasticity field with adaptive cutback (Phase M6); ``pfd_steady`` is the linearized steady-state phase-field damage driver (Phase M7); ``staggered`` / ``monolithic`` orchestrate per-variable-group sub-solves (Phase M7 coupling); ``pinn_fem_hybrid`` trains a spatial PINN and uses it as a predictor / initial guess / preconditioner for a FEM Newton corrector (Phase M13; modes registered in :mod:`pinnacle.solvers.hybrid`).

norm.name: norm
norm.doc: Norm the discrete weak residual is measured in. 'identity' is the plain L2 residual; 'energy' weights by A^-1 (the Berrone et al. dual/energy norm the a-posteriori error estimator is built on).

log_every.name: log_every
log_every.doc: Record a history entry every N epochs.

name: vpinn_transient
doc: Train a network against the discrete implicit-Euler weak residual.
full_doc:
Train a network against the discrete implicit-Euler weak residual.

The network takes ``(x, t)`` and is evaluated at the mesh nodes for a
fixed sequence of time steps
``t_n = n * dt``; the loss sums each step's discrete residual
``(M + dt K) T_n - M T_{n-1} - dt f_n`` — the same implicit-Euler system
``fem_transient`` solves directly, here used as an algebraic training
target instead. ``causal_weighting`` (Phase 43) is **auto-activated**
whenever a ``time_derivative`` kernel is bound to the variable: no deck
change is needed, because causality is a property of the term
structure, not something a user has to remember to turn on.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered executioner name. ``fem_steady`` solves a single Newton step (steady FEM); ``fem_quasi_static`` runs a load-stepping loop with adaptive cutback; ``fem_transient`` runs an implicit-Euler time loop on the scalar mass + gradient stiffness operators (Phase M5); ``pinn_transient`` trains a PINN over the kernels' strong residuals; ``cp_quasi_static`` drives the crystal-plasticity field with adaptive cutback (Phase M6); ``pfd_steady`` is the linearized steady-state phase-field damage driver (Phase M7); ``staggered`` / ``monolithic`` orchestrate per-variable-group sub-solves (Phase M7 coupling); ``pinn_fem_hybrid`` trains a spatial PINN and uses it as a predictor / initial guess / preconditioner for a FEM Newton corrector (Phase M13; modes registered in :mod:`pinnacle.solvers.hybrid`).

causal_epsilon.name: causal_epsilon
causal_epsilon.doc: Causal-weighting strength (finite, >= 0; 0 disables the weighting), auto-activated whenever a 'time_derivative' kernel is bound to the variable. Ignored otherwise.

log_every.name: log_every
log_every.doc: Record a history entry every N epochs.

name: u10zr
doc: Reference data row for fuel_system 'u10zr'. Loaded from packaged CSV; see pinnacle.components.uzr.materialsystems.
full_doc: Reference data row for fuel_system 'u10zr'. Loaded from packaged CSV; see pinnacle.components.uzr.materialsystems.

name: constant
doc: Registered constant-function factory; the kind is forced.
full_doc: Registered constant-function factory; the kind is forced.

kind.name: kind
kind.doc: Function kind. ``constant`` evaluates to a fixed scalar; ``ramp`` linearly interpolates from ``initial`` to ``1.0`` between ``t=0`` and ``t=t_end``; ``cyclic`` switches between ``±amplitude`` with period ``period`` (R-ratio follows the Phase-35 contract); ``cyclic_ramp`` produces a triangular strain waveform ``0 → amp → R·amp → 0`` for load-reversal problems; ``piecewise_table`` uses a user-supplied ``[[t, value], ...]`` knot list; ``parsed`` evaluates a safe math expression in ``x y z t``.

t_end.name: t_end
t_end.doc: Ramp end time (``kind=ramp``); after ``t_end`` the function holds at ``1.0``.

period.name: period
period.doc: Cyclic period (``kind=cyclic`` / ``kind=cyclic_ramp``). For ``cyclic_ramp`` this is the duration of one full triangular cycle.

n_cycles.name: n_cycles
n_cycles.doc: Number of cycles to run for ``kind=cyclic`` / ``kind=cyclic_ramp`` (informational; ``cyclic_ramp`` clips to zero after ``n_cycles * period``).

r_ratio.name: r_ratio
r_ratio.doc: Stress/strain ratio ``R = σ_min/σ_max`` for cyclic functions (``-1.0`` ⇒ symmetric tension/compression, the Phase-35 default).

knots.name: knots
knots.doc: Piecewise knots for ``kind=piecewise_table``. In a ``.i`` deck write them flat and alternating — ``knots = 't0 v0 t1 v1 ...'`` — which is how the deck parser renders a list; the nested ``[[t0, v0], ...]`` form is accepted on the JSON path. Knots are sorted by ``t`` and interpolated linearly, clamping outside the tabulated range.

name: notched_plate
doc: Two-dimensional rectangle with a rectangular edge notch.
full_doc:
Two-dimensional rectangle with a rectangular edge notch.

The notch is removed from one of the four exterior sides and creates a
stress-concentrating root from which a crack can nucleate.  This is the
canonical Phase-26 full-field PFD benchmark geometry.

Args:
    origin: Lower-left corner ``(x, y)``.
    dimensions: ``(width, height)``.
    notch_side: Side to cut from: ``left``/``right``/``bottom``/``top``.
    notch_depth: Depth of the notch into the plate.
    notch_width: Width of the notch along the edge.
    notch_position: Centre coordinate of the notch along the chosen edge.
        Defaults to the midpoint of that edge.

Args:
    directions_a: Incoming slip directions ``s^α`` of shape ``(n_a, 3)``.
    normals_a: Incoming slip-plane normals ``n^α`` of shape ``(n_a, 3)``.
    directions_b: Outgoing slip directions of shape ``(n_b, 3)``.

Returns:

    (length ``n_a``) giving the full compatibility matrix and the maximum
    compatibility for each incoming system.

threshold.name: threshold

Registered additive Hall–Petch CRSS contribution.

Args:
    backend: Active numerical backend.

    d: Average grain size ``d`` in m.  Must be positive.
    n_systems: Number of slip systems; the contribution is applied uniformly.

k_hp.name: k_hp
k_hp.doc: Hall-Petch coefficient k_HP. The grain-size strengthening added to the slip resistance is k_HP / sqrt(d); 0 disables it.

d.name: d
d.doc: Average grain size d. Must be positive; smaller grains are stronger.

name: sachs
doc: Iso-stress (Sachs) lower-bound homogenization.
full_doc:
Iso-stress (Sachs) lower-bound homogenization.

All grains feel the same macroscopic stress; compatibility is not enforced.
The macroscopic strain is the volume-weighted average of the grain strains.
Full implementation requires solving for the grain deformation gradients
that produce the common stress — deferred to a later phase.

volume_fractions.name: volume_fractions
volume_fractions.doc: Per-grain volume fractions used to weight the average. Empty means equal weighting across all grains.

name: self_consistent
doc: Mean-field self-consistent homogenization.
full_doc:
Mean-field self-consistent homogenization.

Each grain is embedded in an effective homogeneous medium; the macroscopic
response follows from the Eshelby inclusion problem.  This is a placeholder
for a later phase.

volume_fractions.name: volume_fractions
volume_fractions.doc: Per-grain volume fractions used to weight the average. Empty means equal weighting across all grains.

max_iterations.name: max_iterations
max_iterations.doc: Maximum self-consistency iterations for the effective medium.

tolerance.name: tolerance
tolerance.doc: Convergence tolerance on the effective stiffness between iterations.

name: taylor
doc: Iso-strain (Taylor) upper-bound homogenization.
full_doc:
Iso-strain (Taylor) upper-bound homogenization.

Every grain is constrained to the macroscopic deformation gradient.  The
macroscopic Cauchy stress is the volume-weighted average of the grain
stresses:

    σ̄ = Σ_i f_i σ_i ,    with Σ_i f_i = 1 .

volume_fractions.name: volume_fractions
volume_fractions.doc: Per-grain volume fractions used to weight the average. Empty means equal weighting across all grains.

name: ac_bulk
doc: Allen–Cahn bulk driving term :math:`L\,\partial f/\partial \eta`.
full_doc:
Allen–Cahn bulk driving term :math:`L\,\partial f/\partial \eta`.

The MOOSE ``AllenCahn`` kernel: the chemical driving force of the
free energy, scaled by the interface mobility. Composed with
``time_derivative`` and ``ac_interface`` it reconstructs the monolithic
``allen_cahn`` residual exactly, so a deck chooses between the one-kernel
and the per-term spelling without any physics difference.

The mobility and the free energy come from the kernel's own params, or
— when the deck binds a quantitative material — from the material
itself: a kernel whose ``material =`` names a ``gb_evolution``
material (see :mod:`pinnacle.materials.gb_evolution`) reads the mapped
:math:`L` (and the ``free_energy`` the runner injects from that
material) instead of the bare params.

Args:
    name: Kernel name (sub-block key inside ``[Kernels]``).
    variable: Variable name.
    params: Validated parameter dict (see :meth:`params`).

type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

The builder wires this from the deck's ``[Materials]`` block; users do not pass it directly. Declared as ``dict`` so the schema is valid; the value is actually a backend-aware free-energy object.

Use this to swap the underlying bulk energy (e.g. from ``double_well`` to ``grain_growth_energy``) without changing the kernel.

name: ac_interface
doc: Allen–Cahn gradient-energy term :math:`-L\,\kappa\,
full_doc:
Allen–Cahn gradient-energy term :math:`-L\,\kappa\,
abla^2\eta`.

    The MOOSE ``ACInterface`` kernel: the weak form is the gradient-energy
    stiffness :math:`L\kappa(
abla\eta, 
abla\psi)`, the strong form the
    Laplacian term of the Allen–Cahn flow. Composed with
    ``time_derivative`` and ``ac_bulk`` it reconstructs the monolithic
    ``allen_cahn`` residual exactly.

    The mobility :math:`L` and gradient coefficient :math:`\kappa` come
    from the kernel's own params, or from the bound quantitative material:
    a kernel whose ``material =`` names a ``gb_evolution`` material (see
    :mod:`pinnacle.materials.gb_evolution`) reads the mapped
    :math:`L = 4M_{GB}/(3w_{GB})` and :math:`\kappa = 3\sigma w_{GB}/4`
    off it — the map lands directly in the slots the FEM transient
    executioner and the PINN loss consume.

    Note on mixed mobilities: ``ac_bulk`` and ``ac_interface`` may legally
    carry different mobility scales (e.g. ``ac_bulk(material=dw,
    mobility=1.0)`` next to ``ac_interface(material=gb)``) — that changes the
    equation (the bulk term then scales differently from the interface), which
    is a modelling choice, NOT a bookkeeping error. A deck asserting that the
    split terms sum exactly to a given monolithic residual must give both
    kernels the SAME effective L; the leading-order curvature velocity of the
    area laws is independent of the bulk scaling, which is why the fitted-slope
    verification survives a mixed binding.

    Args:
        name: Kernel name (sub-block key inside ``[Kernels]``).
        variable: Variable name.
        params: Validated parameter dict (see :meth:`params`).

name: ac_linearised
doc: Allen–Cahn kernel in the linearised variable :math:`\psi`.
full_doc:
Allen–Cahn kernel in the linearised variable :math:`\psi`.

The strong residual is the exact chain-rule transform of the
monolithic Allen–Cahn equation (see the module docstring):

.. math::

    R_\psi = \partial_t\psi
            + L\bigl[
                \sqrt{2}\,\xi(\kappa|\nabla\psi|^2 - 16W)
                - \kappa\nabla^2\psi
            \bigr],
    \qquad \xi = \tanh(\psi/\sqrt2),

so a deck that swaps the standard :math:`\eta` formulation for this
one solves the *same* physics with a linear equilibrium interface —
the linearised-vs-standard agreement the phase verifies. The mobility
:math:`L` and :math:`\kappa` come from the kernel params or from a
bound ``gb_evolution`` material (``material_obj`` precedence, as for
the split terms); ``barrier_height`` is the :math:`W` of the double
well the transform linearises.

Args:
    name: Kernel name (sub-block key inside ``[Kernels]``).
    variable: The transformed variable's name (``psi`` by convention).
    params: Validated parameter dict (see :meth:`params`).

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

mobility.name: mobility
mobility.doc: Interface mobility ``L`` of the transformed Allen–Cahn flow. When the kernel's ``material =`` names a ``gb_evolution`` material, the mapped ``L = 4 M_GB / (3 w_GB)`` takes precedence.

gradient_coefficient.name: gradient_coefficient
gradient_coefficient.doc: Gradient-energy coefficient ``kappa``. With a bound ``gb_evolution`` material the mapped ``kappa = 3 sigma w_GB / 4`` takes precedence.

barrier_height.name: barrier_height
barrier_height.doc: Barrier ``W`` of the double well the transform linearises (the ``double_well`` material's barrier). Sets the equilibrium width ``a = sqrt(kappa / (8 W))`` of the eta-space kink; the psi-space equilibrium ramp has slope sqrt(16 W / kappa).

free_energy.name: free_energy
free_energy.doc: Injected free energy (unused by this kernel — the transformed residual carries the bulk physics through the barrier_height map). Declared for uniformity with the other phase-field kernels.

material.doc: Optional material registry name to bind. A ``gb_evolution`` material supplies the mapped L / kappa through the builder's material_obj injection.

name: advection
doc: Advection term ``+ v·∇u`` for a prescribed velocity field.
full_doc:
Advection term ``+ v·∇u`` for a prescribed velocity field.

The velocity is a constant vector: this is passive transport of the
scalar by a known flow, not a momentum solve. Coupling to a computed
velocity field is a materials-level extension, not a change here.

Numerical note: the Galerkin discretisation of advection is unstable for
cell Péclet numbers above ~2 (``|v| h / 2D``), producing oscillations
rather than a wrong-but-smooth answer. Refine, raise ``diffusivity``, or
use the PINN path — no stabilisation (SUPG) is applied.

doc: Antitrapping flux :math:`\mathbf J_A = F_0\,\hat{\mathbf n}\,\partial_t\eta`.
full_doc:
Antitrapping flux :math:`\mathbf J_A = F_0\,\hat{\mathbf n}\,\partial_t\eta`.

With :math:`\mathbf g = \nabla\eta`, :math:`\hat{\mathbf n} = \mathbf g /
(|\mathbf g| + \epsilon)` and the backward-difference rate
:math:`\dot\eta = (\eta - \eta_{\text{old}})/\Delta t` read from the
quadrature state, the weak contribution :math:`(\mathbf J_A, \nabla\psi)`
joins the split-CH conservation row. The exact tangents are

.. math::

    \frac{\partial\mathbf J_A}{\partial\eta} = \frac{F_0}{\Delta t}\hat{\mathbf n},
    \qquad
    \frac{\partial\mathbf J_A}{\partial\mathbf g}
        = F_0\,\dot\eta\left[\frac{\mathbf I}{|\mathbf g| + \epsilon}
          - \frac{\mathbf g\,\mathbf g^{\mathsf T}}
                 {|\mathbf g|\,(|\mathbf g| + \epsilon)^2}\right],

the second from :math:`\partial|\mathbf g|/\partial g_j = g_j/|\mathbf g|`.
The rate is the first-order backward difference whatever the executioner's
scheme (``bdf2`` included) — the term is a stabilising correction, and a
first-order rate keeps it local to the current step.

Args:
    name: Kernel name (sub-block key inside ``[Kernels]``).
    variable: The chemical-potential variable (``mu``), as for
        ``split_ch_wres`` — the row is the conservation equation.
    params: Validated parameter dict (see :meth:`params`).

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must be 'antitrapping_current' — the Karma antitrapping flux on the conservation row of the split Cahn-Hilliard pair (MOOSE AntitrappingCurrent).

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the chemical-potential variable (``mu`` by convention) — the same binding as ``split_ch_wres``: the flux lands on the ``split_ch_conservation`` row of the pair.

phase_variable.name: phase_variable
phase_variable.doc: Name of the coupled order-parameter fem variable ``eta`` whose interface normal ``grad(eta)/|grad(eta)|`` and backward-difference rate ``(eta - eta_old)/dt`` drive the current (an Allen-Cahn field of the same deck).

amplitude.name: amplitude
amplitude.doc: Amplitude ``F0`` of the current ``J = F0 n d(eta)/dt``. In the classical alloy-solidification model it stands for ``a_t W (1 - k) c_l``-type prefactors (antitrapping coefficient ``a_t = 1/(2 sqrt 2)``, interface width ``W``, partition coefficient ``k``, the local liquid composition); PINNACLE keeps it a single number the deck supplies. ``F0 > 0`` expels solute from the growing phase (physical current ``-J`` points against grad(eta) where d(eta)/dt > 0); ``0`` (default) switches the term off.

regularisation.name: regularisation
regularisation.doc: Regularisation ``eps`` in the normal ``grad(eta)/(|grad(eta)| + eps)`` that keeps the flux and its tangent finite in the bulk, where ``grad(eta) = 0``. Choose it far below the interface's typical |grad(eta)| ~ 1/width.

equation.name: equation
equation.doc: Row of the block system the flux joins. Empty (default) selects the split Cahn-Hilliard conservation row ``split_ch_conservation``. Set it explicitly only for a custom composition.

name: body_source
doc: Volumetric source term ``- f`` (heat generation, a forcing function).
full_doc:
Volumetric source term ``- f`` (heat generation, a forcing function).

Kept separate from ``diffusion`` so that "what is being solved" and
"what is driving it" stay independently declarable — the same reason
MOOSE separates ``BodyForce`` from the operator kernels.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

dim.name: dim
dim.doc: Spatial dimension of the field (1, 2 or 3). Must match the mesh dimension and the connected Variable.

equation.name: equation
equation.doc: Row of the nonlinear block transient (``pf_fem_transient``) the source joins: empty (the variable's own row), the literal row name of a paired kernel (``split_ch_conservation``), or the symbolic ``@accumulation`` / ``@definition``. A manufactured-solution source for the split Cahn-Hilliard pair belongs on the conservation row although it is bound to ``c``. Ignored by the scalar executioners.

value.name: value
value.doc: Constant volumetric source ``f`` in ``- f``. Positive adds to the field (heat generation); negative removes it (a sink). Ignored when ``function`` is set.

function.name: function
function.doc: Name of a ``[Functions]`` entry supplying a **spatially varying** source ``f(x, y, z)``, which is what a manufactured solution needs. Use ``kind = parsed`` with an ``expression`` in ``x``/``y``/``z``; for example ``expression = '2*pi*pi*sin(pi*x)*sin(pi*y)'`` is the source whose exact solution is ``sin(pi x) sin(pi y)`` for unit diffusivity. Leave empty to use the constant ``value``.

name: cahn_hilliard
doc: Cahn–Hilliard kernel — mixed formulation ``(c, μ)``.
full_doc:
Cahn–Hilliard kernel — mixed formulation ``(c, μ)``.

The network predicts both the concentration ``c`` and the chemical
potential ``μ``; the residual is the Cahn–Hilliard conservation law
and the chemical-potential definition. This mirrors
:class:`pinnacle.phasefield.pde_residuals.CahnHilliardResidual`.

The kernel only exposes the strong form; the weak form is a fourth-order
PDE and is not in the M5 scope.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

spatial_dim.name: spatial_dim
spatial_dim.doc: Spatial dimension of the PDE (1, 2 or 3).

free_energy.name: free_energy
free_energy.doc: Injected :class:`~pinnacle.phasefield.free_energy.DoubleWellBulkEnergy` (or :class:`GrainGrowthEnergy`). The builder wires this from the deck's ``[Materials]`` block; users do not pass it directly. Declared as ``dict`` so the schema is valid; the value is actually a backend-aware free-energy object.

material.name: material
material.doc: Optional :class:`material` registry name to bind. When set, the builder looks the material up in the deck's ``[Materials]`` block and injects its ``free_energy`` attribute. Use this to swap the underlying bulk energy (e.g. from ``double_well`` to ``grain_growth_energy``) without changing the kernel.

name: coupled_time_derivative
doc: The accumulation term :math:`(\partial c/\partial t,\psi)` of split CH.
full_doc:
The accumulation term :math:`(\partial c/\partial t,\psi)` of split CH.

This is the one kernel of the system that is *not* split out: it is the
mass-matrix contribution to the conserved-variable equation. It is
registered on the :math:`c` variable so the executioner recognises it as
the term that carries the time derivative.

Args:
    name: Kernel name (sub-block key inside ``[Kernels]``).
    variable: The conserved variable (``c`` by convention).
    params: Validated parameter dict. ``coefficient`` is :math:`1`.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must be 'coupled_time_derivative'.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the conserved variable this accumulation term binds to (``c`` by convention for split Cahn-Hilliard).

coefficient.name: coefficient
coefficient.doc: Coefficient of the accumulation term ``\\partial c / \\partial t``. The default is 1: the term is the mass-matrix contribution to the conserved-variable equation.

name: diffusion
doc: Diffusion term ``-∇·(D ∇u)`` — the Laplacian of a scalar field.
full_doc:
Diffusion term ``-∇·(D ∇u)`` — the Laplacian of a scalar field.

The workhorse of the family. On its own it is the Poisson/Laplace
equation and steady heat conduction; with ``time_derivative`` it is the
heat equation; with ``reaction`` it is Helmholtz; with
``second_time_derivative`` it is the wave equation.

``diffusivity`` doubles as thermal conductivity ``k``, mass diffusivity
``D``, or the squared wave speed ``c²`` — the operator is the same and
the deck's units decide what it means.

Args:
    name: Kernel name (the sub-block key inside ``[Kernels]``).
    variable: Variable the kernel binds to.
    params: Validated parameters; see :meth:`params`.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

dim.name: dim
dim.doc: Spatial dimension of the field (1, 2 or 3). Must match the mesh dimension and the connected Variable.

diffusivity.name: diffusivity
diffusivity.doc: Diffusion coefficient ``D``. A scalar is isotropic; a ``dim``-vector is a diagonal (orthotropic) tensor; a full ``dim x dim`` matrix is used as given. Reads as thermal conductivity ``k`` for heat conduction, mass diffusivity for species transport, or the squared wave speed ``c^2`` when paired with ``second_time_derivative``.

function.name: function
function.doc: Optional [Functions] entry giving a **spatially varying** scale on 'diffusivity' — k(x) = function(x) * diffusivity — resolved at quadrature points the same way body_source resolves a spatially varying source. Mutually EXCLUSIVE with 'material' — declaring both is a deck error (the paths would compose them inconsistently); fold a combined k(T)*s(x) into one route.

material.name: material
material.doc: Optional thermal_conductivity [Materials] entry making the diffusivity a function of the *field* (k(T)), consumed through the same material = <name> indirection stress_divergence uses. The Newton path in scalar_steady (solve_method = newton) resolves k(T) and its consistent tangent through this material. Mutually exclusive with 'function =' (k(x)) — declaring both is a deck error.

name: fission_source
doc: Lanthanide birth term ``-γ·Fdot`` from a power history.
full_doc:
Lanthanide birth term ``-γ·Fdot`` from a power history.

The source is the fission rate times a lanthanide yield. Rather than
baking a duty cycle into the kernel, the *shape* comes from a named
``[Functions]`` entry evaluated in time, so an irradiation history —
startup ramp, steady operation, a shutdown, a restart — is deck data
that composes with the existing ``piecewise_table`` / ``ramp`` /
``cyclic`` functions. That composition is what lets the reactive-sink
BC's threshold gate be exercised: growth arrests when the function
returns to zero.

Sign follows the module convention of :mod:`~pinnacle.system.transport_kernels`:
the term is returned as it appears on the left-hand side of ``… = 0``,
so a *positive* yield is a *negative* contribution.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

dim.name: dim
dim.doc: Spatial dimension of the field (1, 2 or 3). Must match the mesh dimension and the connected Variable.

fission_rate.name: fission_rate
fission_rate.doc: Nominal volumetric fission rate ``Fdot`` at full power. The ``function`` history scales it, so a history normalised to 1.0 reads as a power fraction.

yield_fraction.name: yield_fraction
yield_fraction.doc: Lanthanide yield ``gamma`` per fission, in [0, 1]. Defaults to zero so a deck that forgets it gets no source rather than an invented one.

function.name: function
function.doc: Name of a ``[Functions]`` entry giving the power history as a fraction of full power. Empty means steady at ``fission_rate``. Use ``piecewise_table`` for a duty cycle with shutdowns -- that is what exercises the reactive-sink threshold gate.

name: joule_source
doc: ``sigma_e * |grad V|^2`` volumetric heat source.
full_doc:
``sigma_e * |grad V|^2`` volumetric heat source.

``gradient_function`` supplies the PRECOMPUTED ``|grad V|^2(x)``
(typically a :class:`~pinnacle.system.p1_radiation.NodalInterpolant1DFunction`
built by :func:`solve_joule_heating` from an already-solved potential
field) — see the module docstring for why this is not read from a live
second coupled Variable. ``sigma_e`` comes from either a bound
``material = electrical_conductivity`` restricted to its ``constant``
form (a field-dependent form is rejected at build time — a genuinely
``T``-dependent ``sigma_e`` would need the same monolithic coupling
this module does not have) or, when no material is bound, the plain
``sigma_e`` float parameter.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

dim.name: dim
dim.doc: Spatial dimension of the field (1, 2 or 3). Must match the mesh dimension and the connected Variable.

sigma_e.name: sigma_e
sigma_e.doc: Electrical conductivity, used when no 'material' is bound. Must be finite and > 0 — a negative value would turn Joule heating into a distributed cooling source.

gradient_function.name: gradient_function
gradient_function.doc: Name of a [Functions] entry supplying |grad V|^2(x) (typically a 'nodal_interpolant_1d' built by solve_joule_heating from an already-solved potential field).

material.name: material
material.doc: Optional electrical_conductivity [Materials] entry supplying sigma_e, consumed through the same material = <name> indirection the diffusion kernel uses. Only its 'constant' form is accepted — a field-dependent form (linear/table/parsed) is REJECTED at build time, because the one-way V -> T coupling would silently flatten it to a single reference value. Overrides 'sigma_e' when set.

name: kks_ac_bulk_c
doc: The concentration driving term of the KKS Allen-Cahn equation.
full_doc:
The concentration driving term of the KKS Allen-Cahn equation.

Residual :math:`-L\,h'(\eta)\,\mu_{\mathrm{rec}}\,(c_b - c_a)` —
the constraint-consistent concentration part of
:math:`\delta F/\delta\eta` (report key
``concentration_driving_residual``). Together with ``kks_ac_bulk_f``
it reconstructs :math:`L\,h'(\eta)[(f_b - f_a) -
\mu_{\mathrm{rec}}(c_b - c_a)]`.

Args:
    name: Kernel name.
    variable: The order parameter ``eta``.
    params: Validated parameter dict — ``c_a`` / ``c_b`` name the
        coupled phase concentrations; the phase energies come from a
        bound ``kks_phase_pair`` or inline params.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

c_a.name: c_a
c_a.doc: Name of the a-phase concentration variable entering ``mu_rec (c_b - c_a)``.

c_b.name: c_b
c_b.doc: Name of the b-phase concentration variable entering ``mu_rec (c_b - c_a)``.

mobility.name: mobility
mobility.doc: Allen-Cahn mobility ``L`` scaling the driving term.

switching.name: switching
switching.doc: Switching-function variant whose derivative ``h'(eta)`` weights the driving term.

material.name: material
