material.doc: Optional ``kks_phase_pair`` [Materials] entry by name (the builder injects its live instance). Leave empty to use the inline ``curvature_*`` / ``equilibrium_*`` params.

name: kks_ac_bulk_f
doc: The phase-energy driving term of the KKS Allen-Cahn equation.
full_doc:
The phase-energy driving term of the KKS Allen-Cahn equation.

Residual :math:`L\,h'(\eta)\,[f_b(c_b) - f_a(c_a)]` — the free-energy
difference part of :math:`\delta F/\delta\eta` (report key
``phase_driving_residual``), paired with ``kks_ac_bulk_c`` for the
concentration part and with the interface/barrier kernels for the
gradient and double-well terms.

Args:
    name: Kernel name.
    variable: The order parameter ``eta``.
    params: Validated parameter dict — ``c_a`` / ``c_b`` name the
        coupled phase concentrations, ``mobility`` is :math:`L`, the
        phase energies come from a bound ``kks_phase_pair`` or inline
        params.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

c_a.name: c_a
c_a.doc: Name of the a-phase concentration variable whose free energy enters the driving difference.

c_b.name: c_b
c_b.doc: Name of the b-phase concentration variable whose free energy enters the driving difference.

mobility.name: mobility
mobility.doc: Allen-Cahn mobility ``L`` scaling the driving term.

switching.name: switching
switching.doc: Switching-function variant whose derivative ``h'(eta)`` weights the driving term.

material.name: material
material.doc: Optional ``kks_phase_pair`` [Materials] entry by name (the builder injects its live instance). Leave empty to use the inline ``curvature_*`` / ``equilibrium_*`` params.

name: kks_phase_chem_potential
doc: The equal-chemical-potential row ``f_a'(c_a) - f_b'(c_b)``, on ``c_a``.
full_doc:
The equal-chemical-potential row ``f_a'(c_a) - f_b'(c_b)``, on ``c_a``.

**The phase-equilibrium row** — the algebraic constraint whose residual
is the diagnostic P8 reports separately from the PDE residuals. At
equilibrium it vanishes; a solution of the transport PDE alone can
violate it (see the module docstring and the negative-control test).

Args:
    name: Kernel name.
    variable: The phase concentration this row binds to (``ca``).
    params: Validated parameter dict — ``c_b`` names the other phase
        concentration; the phase energies come from a bound
        ``kks_phase_pair`` material or inline ``curvature_*`` /
        ``equilibrium_*`` params.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

c_b.name: c_b
c_b.doc: Name of the other phase-concentration variable (``cb`` by convention); the row reads ``f_a'(ca) - f_b'(cb)``.

material.name: material
material.doc: Optional ``kks_phase_pair`` [Materials] entry by name; the builder injects its live instance and the kernel reads ``.fa`` / ``.fb`` from it. Leave empty to use the inline ``curvature_*`` / ``equilibrium_*`` params instead.

curvature_a.name: curvature_a
curvature_a.doc: Inline a-phase curvature ``A_a`` (used when no ``material`` is bound): ``f_a = A_a/2 (c_a - c_eq_a)^2``.

curvature_b.name: curvature_b
curvature_b.doc: Inline b-phase curvature ``A_b`` (used when no ``material`` is bound): ``f_b = A_b/2 (c_b - c_eq_b)^2``.

name: kks_phase_concentration
doc: The interpolation identity ``c = (1-h) c_a + h c_b``, bound to ``c_b``.
full_doc:
The interpolation identity ``c = (1-h) c_a + h c_b``, bound to ``c_b``.

The algebraic row that slaves the phase concentrations to the global
composition and the order parameter. The kernel binds to one of the
two phase-concentration variables (``c_b`` by convention, mirroring
the MOOSE kernel); its test function carries the row.

Args:
    name: Kernel name.
    variable: The phase concentration this row binds to (``cb``).
    params: Validated parameter dict — ``c_a``, ``concentration``,
        ``eta`` name the coupled variables; ``switching`` picks ``h``.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

c_a.name: c_a
c_a.doc: Name of the other phase-concentration variable (``ca`` by convention); must be declared in ``[Variables]``.

concentration.name: concentration
concentration.doc: Name of the global (conserved) composition variable ``c``.

eta.name: eta
eta.doc: Name of the order-parameter variable ``eta`` whose switching function ``h(eta)`` weights the interpolation.

switching.name: switching
switching.doc: Switching-function variant ``h(eta)`` interpolating the phase concentrations.

name: kks_split_ch_res
doc: The KKS conservation law on ``c``, written through ``mu_rec``.
full_doc:
The KKS conservation law on ``c``, written through ``mu_rec``.

Strong residual :math:`\partial c/\partial t -
\nabla\cdot(M\nabla\mu_{\mathrm{rec}})` with
:math:`\mu_{\mathrm{rec}} = (1-h) f_a'(c_a) + h f_b'(c_b)` computed
in-graph from the coupled fields. This is a **PDE** residual: it is
reported under ``transport_residual`` and never mixed with the
algebraic rows.

Args:
    name: Kernel name.
    variable: The conserved composition ``c``.
    params: Validated parameter dict — ``c_a`` / ``c_b`` / ``eta``
        name the coupled variables, ``mobility`` is :math:`M`, the
        phase energies come from a bound ``kks_phase_pair`` or inline
        params.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

c_a.name: c_a
c_a.doc: Name of the a-phase concentration variable the reconstruction ``mu_rec`` reads.

c_b.name: c_b
c_b.doc: Name of the b-phase concentration variable the reconstruction ``mu_rec`` reads.

eta.name: eta
eta.doc: Name of the order-parameter variable weighting the reconstruction ``mu_rec``.

mobility.name: mobility
mobility.doc: Scalar mobility ``M`` of the transport law ``div(M grad mu_rec)``.

switching.name: switching
switching.doc: Switching-function variant ``h(eta)`` weighting the phase reconstruction.

material.name: material
material.doc: Optional ``kks_phase_pair`` [Materials] entry by name (the builder injects its live instance). Leave empty to use the inline ``curvature_*`` / ``equilibrium_*`` params.

name: langevin_noise
doc: Random source ``A ξ(x)`` redrawn every step (MOOSE Langevin/ConservedNoise).
full_doc:
Random source ``A ξ(x)`` redrawn every step (MOOSE Langevin/ConservedNoise).

Ships through the load protocol the transient executioners refresh every
step (``time_dependent_load`` + :meth:`set_time`, then
:meth:`fem_operators`): the assembled nodal load is
:math:`f_i = \sum_{e,q} w_{eq} N_i A \xi_{eq}` with one draw per
quadrature point, projected to zero quadrature-weighted mean when
``conserved`` is on. Joins the accumulation row of its variable by
default (its own row for an Allen–Cahn order parameter, the
conservation row for a split Cahn–Hilliard concentration).

Args:
    name: Kernel name (sub-block key inside ``[Kernels]``).
    variable: The forced variable.
    params: Validated parameter dict (see :meth:`params`).

Raises:
    PinnacleError: If the amplitude is negative / non-finite or the
        distribution is unknown.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

amplitude.name: amplitude
amplitude.doc: Noise amplitude ``A`` multiplying the unit random field: the forcing ``A xi(x)`` enters the equation on the right-hand side (``dphi/dt = ... + A xi``). The load's variance scales as A^2; with ``distribution = uniform`` the per-point variance is A^2/3, with ``normal`` it is A^2.

seed.name: seed
seed.doc: Base RNG seed. Each step's field is drawn from ``numpy.random.default_rng([seed, bits(t)])`` with ``t`` the step's target time, so the same deck and seed give bit-identical fields, a different seed a different realisation, and every step an independent draw. LEAVE IT UNSET to inherit ``[Global] seed`` (mixed with this block's name so two noise blocks in one deck stay independent): sweeping the global seed then sweeps the realisation, which is what an ensemble needs. Set it only to pin one block against the rest of the deck.

conserved.name: conserved
conserved.doc: ``true`` projects every step's random field to zero quadrature-weighted mean over the domain before assembly (the MOOSE ConservedNoise idea), so the assembled load sums to zero to round-off and the integral of a conserved variable is left untouched. Use it for a split Cahn-Hilliard concentration; leave ``false`` (plain LangevinNoise) for a non-conserved Allen-Cahn order parameter.

distribution.name: distribution
distribution.doc: Distribution of the unit random field ``xi`` at each quadrature point: ``uniform`` on [-1, 1] (the MOOSE default; variance 1/3) or ``normal`` (standard Gaussian; variance 1).

equation.name: equation
equation.doc: Row of the block system the load joins. The default ``@accumulation`` resolves to the row carrying the variable's time derivative: the variable's own row for an Allen-Cahn order parameter, ``split_ch_conservation`` for a split Cahn-Hilliard concentration (where the forcing belongs in the conservation law, ``dc/dt = div(M grad mu) + A xi``). Set a literal row name for other compositions.

name: nucleation_penalty
doc: Local penalty free energy ``½ P m(x) (q − q*)²`` where the mask is on.
full_doc:
Local penalty free energy ``½ P m(x) (q − q*)²`` where the mask is on.

The discrete-nucleation *drive*: wherever the smooth mask :math:`m` is
active, the penalty
:math:`f_{\mathrm{nuc}} = \tfrac12 P\,m(\mathbf x)\,(q - q^*)^2`
biases the field :math:`q` toward the nucleus value :math:`q^*` — the
harmonic MATCH targeting of MOOSE's ``DiscreteNucleation``. Its gradient
enters the chemical potential,

.. math::

    \frac{\partial f_{\mathrm{nuc}}}{\partial q}
        = P\,m(\mathbf x)\,(q - q^*),

so on the split-CH pair the kernel binds to the conserved variable and
its strong residual is a **contribution** to the :math:`\mu` equation,
composable with ``split_ch_parsed`` — the same convention the split
kernels use.

The mask comes either from explicit nucleus geometry (``center`` /
``radius`` / ``width`` — one kernel block per nucleus, the deck path) or
from an injected callable (``params["mask_obj"]`` / :meth:`bind_mask` —
the service path, typically :meth:`NucleationInserter.mask`). Like every
P9 piece it is explicit: no executioner gathers it yet, so a deck block
is validated and carried, and the FEM/PINN wiring is a later-phase
concern.

Args:
    name: Kernel name (sub-block key inside ``[Kernels]``).
    variable: The field the penalty drives (``c`` for split CH).
    params: Validated parameter dict (see :meth:`params`).

Raises:
    PinnacleError: If neither a mask callable nor nucleus geometry is
        supplied, or ``penalty`` is negative.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

penalty.name: penalty
penalty.doc: Penalty amplitude ``P`` of the local free energy ``½ P m(x) (q − q*)²``. The drive toward the nucleus state scales with P; the block Jacobian stiffens the same way.

target.name: target
target.doc: Nucleus value ``q*`` the penalty drives the field toward inside the mask (MATCH targeting; the +1 well of the double well by convention).

mobility.name: mobility
mobility.doc: Kinetic coefficient multiplying the penalty force in the weak row: ``1`` on a split Cahn-Hilliard chemical-potential row (the penalty enters ``mu`` directly), the Allen-Cahn mobility ``L`` when the driven field is a non-conserved order parameter.

equation.name: equation
equation.doc: Row of the block system the penalty joins. Empty (default) resolves it from the driven variable: the variable's own row for an Allen-Cahn order parameter, or the potential-definition row (``split_ch_potential``) for a split Cahn-Hilliard concentration. Set it explicitly for other compositions.

center.name: center
center.doc: Nucleus centre for the deck path (one kernel block per nucleus). Ignored when a mask callable is injected.

radius.name: radius
radius.doc: Nucleus radius of the deck-path mask: the bump is 1 inside and decays over ``width`` (0 = automatic: radius/4).

width.name: width
width.doc: Interface width of the smooth mask bump (0 = automatic: radius/4).

name: p1_radiation
doc: ``-div(Gamma grad G) + sigma_a (G - 4 sigma T(x)^4) = 0``.
full_doc:
``-div(Gamma grad G) + sigma_a (G - 4 sigma T(x)^4) = 0``.

``T`` is supplied as a prescribed ``temperature_function`` (a plain
spatial function — typically a :class:`NodalInterpolant1DFunction`
updated between :func:`solve_p1_coupled` Picard iterations), not a
live second Variable — see the module docstring.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

dim.name: dim
dim.doc: Spatial dimension of the field (1, 2 or 3). Must match the mesh dimension and the connected Variable.

gamma.name: gamma
gamma.doc: P1 diffusion coefficient Gamma = 1 / (3 (sigma_a + sigma_s')) — finite and > 0 (it multiplies the gradient; zero removes the diffusion operator entirely).

sigma_a.name: sigma_a
sigma_a.doc: Absorption coefficient (finite, >= 0). Zero is the non-absorbing (pure-scattering) limit: the equation reduces to -div(Gamma grad G) = 0 and the companion energy sink vanishes.

temperature_function.name: temperature_function
temperature_function.doc: Name of a [Functions] entry supplying the medium temperature T(x) (typically 'nodal_interpolant_1d', updated between solve_p1_coupled's Picard iterations).

name: p1_radiation_sink
doc: The energy equation's ``+ sigma_a (4 sigma T^4 - G(x))`` term.
full_doc:
The energy equation's ``+ sigma_a (4 sigma T^4 - G(x))`` term.

Genuinely nonlinear in its OWN variable ``T`` (a volumetric ``T^4``
reaction, the same nonlinearity :class:`~pinnacle.system.thermal_bcs.RadiativeBC`
has at a boundary, here inside the domain): implements
:meth:`fem_operators_nonlinear` using the SAME frozen-coefficient trick
``DiffusionKernel`` uses for ``k(T)`` — ``4 sigma_a sigma T_q^3`` frozen
at the current quadrature-point temperature makes
``stiffness @ field`` reproduce ``4 sigma_a sigma T_q^4`` exactly, and
because this is a pure POINTWISE quartic (no spatial-gradient
cross-term), the exact Newton tangent is simply ``4 * stiffness`` — no
separate chain-rule correction term is needed.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

dim.name: dim
dim.doc: Spatial dimension of the field (1, 2 or 3). Must match the mesh dimension and the connected Variable.

sigma_a.name: sigma_a
sigma_a.doc: Absorption coefficient (finite, >= 0). Zero is the non-absorbing (pure-scattering) limit: the equation reduces to -div(Gamma grad G) = 0 and the companion energy sink vanishes.

incident_radiation_function.name: incident_radiation_function
incident_radiation_function.doc: Name of a [Functions] entry supplying the incident radiation G(x) (typically 'nodal_interpolant_1d', updated between solve_p1_coupled's Picard iterations).

name: pf_advection_supg
doc: Advection ``v·∇φ`` of a phase field with streamline-diffusion (SUPG).
full_doc:
Advection ``v·∇φ`` of a phase field with streamline-diffusion (SUPG).

Contributes, on the FEM side, the source :math:`g = \mathbf v\cdot\nabla\phi`
tested by :math:`\psi` and — when ``supg`` is on — the flux
:math:`\mathbf J = \tau\,(\mathbf v\cdot\nabla\phi)\,\mathbf v`
tested by :math:`\nabla\psi`, with exact tangents
:math:`\partial g/\partial\nabla\phi = \mathbf v` and
:math:`\partial\mathbf J/\partial\nabla\phi = \tau\,\mathbf v\mathbf v^T`.
Both terms are linear in :math:`\phi`, so block Newton converges in
one iteration on a pure translation. A multi-component variable is
advected component-wise by the same velocity.

The element size :math:`h` behind :math:`\tau = h/(2|\mathbf v|)` is
read off the mesh when the executioner discovers the kernel
(:meth:`fem_operators` is called once at that point) or set explicitly
through the ``h`` parameter; :meth:`bind_mesh` exposes the same
resolution for programmatic use.

Args:
    name: Kernel name (sub-block key inside ``[Kernels]``).
    variable: The advected phase-field variable.
    params: Validated parameter dict (see :meth:`params`).

Raises:
    PinnacleError: If the velocity is empty, has more than three
        components, or ``tau_scale`` / ``h`` are negative.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

velocity.name: velocity
velocity.doc: Prescribed advection velocity ``v`` as a dim-component vector (one entry per mesh dimension), constant in space and time: passive transport of the phase field by a known flow, not a momentum solve. The mesh / collocation dimension must match the component count.

supg.name: supg
supg.doc: Add the streamline-diffusion SUPG term ``(tau (v.grad phi) v, grad psi)`` on the FEM side (default true). This is the classical streamline-upwind perturbation applied to the advective residual only — not the fully consistent SUPG weighting of every term of the equation. ``false`` leaves the plain Galerkin advection, which oscillates at cell Peclet numbers above ~1 (always, for a diffusion-free translation). No stabilisation is applied on the PINN path in either case.

tau_scale.name: tau_scale
tau_scale.doc: Dimensionless multiplier on the stabilisation parameter ``tau = tau_scale * h / (2 |v|)``. 1 is the textbook value; smaller values weaken the added streamline diffusion ``tau |v|^2 = tau_scale * h |v| / 2`` (and the smearing that comes with it) at the price of residual overshoot.

h.name: h
h.doc: Optional element-size override for ``tau``. When omitted (default) h is the mean, over the elements, of the element extent along the flow direction, read off the mesh when the executioner discovers the kernel (the element length in 1-D, the edge length along the flow on an axis-aligned quad/hex).

equation.name: equation
equation.doc: Row of the block system the term joins. Empty (default) means the advected variable's own row — the Allen-Cahn case. For an advected split Cahn-Hilliard concentration set it to ``split_ch_conservation`` so that ``v.grad c`` sits next to ``dc/dt`` in the conservation law, not in the potential definition.

name: pfd_evolution
doc: Phase-field damage evolution kernel.
full_doc:
Phase-field damage evolution kernel.

Strong form (PINN path): the same residual
:class:`pinnacle.phasefield.damage.DamageFieldResidual` evaluates
today,

.. math::

    r(d) = \frac{G_c}{l_0} \left( d - l_0^2 \nabla\cdot(\mathbf A
        \nabla d) \right) - 2 (1 - d) H

with the user-selected AT1/AT2 form. Weak form (FEM path): the kernel
exposes a :class:`_PFDFemMaterial` whose ``make_operators`` builds the
same scalar mass + anisotropic gradient stiffness pair
:func:`pinnacle.phasefield.damage_field.build_damage_operators` builds
today. The history field ``H`` is held on the kernel so every
sub-solver sees the same irreversibility.

The kernel requires three ``[Materials]`` entries (the deck wires them
by name):

* ``fracture`` → :class:`PFDFractureMaterial` (``Gc``, ``l0``, ``A``);
* ``driving_force`` → :class:`PFDDrivingForceMaterial` (the ``H`` field
  the kernel reads and the coupling executioner updates);
* optionally ``degradation`` → :class:`PFDDegradationMaterial` (the
  same ``g(d) = (1 - d)²`` the legacy monolith uses; declared
  explicitly so the M7 contract "the mechanics↔damage pairing is
  declared in the deck" is honored).

Args:
    name: Kernel name (sub-block key inside ``[Kernels]``).
    variable: Variable name (the damage field ``d``).
    params: Validated parameter dict (must include ``dim``,
        ``fracture``, ``driving_force``; ``degradation`` and
        ``boundary_damage`` are optional).

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

dim.name: dim
dim.doc: Spatial dimension of the damage field (``1``, ``2``, or ``3``). Must match the connected :class:`Variable`'s component count.

fracture.name: fracture
fracture.doc: Name of the ``[Materials]`` sub-block of kind ``pfd_fracture`` providing ``Gc``, ``length_scale``, the structural tensor ``A`` and the AT1/AT2 form. The runner wires it via :meth:`bind_materials`.

driving_force.name: driving_force
driving_force.doc: Name of the ``[Materials]`` sub-block of kind ``pfd_driving_force`` carrying the history field ``H`` (irreversibility). The coupling executioner feeds the positive stored energy to :meth:`update` between staggered iterations; the standalone PFD deck feeds a prescribed energy field.

degradation.name: degradation
degradation.doc: Optional name of the ``[Materials]`` sub-block of kind ``pfd_degradation`` providing ``g(d) = (1 - d)²``. The mechanics kernel reads it via :meth:`bind_degradation` and applies it to the trial stress; the M7 contract requires this pairing to be **declared** in the deck, not assumed.

boundary_damage.name: boundary_damage
boundary_damage.doc: Homogeneous Dirichlet value applied on the damage field's boundary node set. Defaults to 0 (the canonical undamaged boundary).

name: radial_diffusion
doc: Cylindrical diffusion ``-D(∂_rr c + (1/r) ∂_r c)`` on the pin radius.
full_doc:
Cylindrical diffusion ``-D(∂_rr c + (1/r) ∂_r c)`` on the pin radius.

The operator is the axisymmetric Laplacian with no angular or axial
dependence — the reduction a fuel-performance analysis makes when the
pin is long compared with its radius and the power is azimuthally
uniform.

``diffusivity`` is the constant-coefficient default. The porosity- and
temperature-dependent :func:`~.correlations.nd_effective_diffusivity`
is a *material*, bound through ``uzr_nd_diffusivity``; a deck that wants
the varying coefficient names that material in ``material`` and leaves
``diffusivity`` alone. Keeping the two separate is deliberate: the
kernel owns the geometry, the material owns the physics.

Where the state comes from
--------------------------

The closure consumes a temperature and a porosity, and this reduction
does not solve for either: the framework's scalar executioners carry one
field per deck, and that field is the lanthanide concentration. So the
state is deck data — ``temperature`` / ``porosity`` for a uniform value,
or ``temperature_function`` / ``porosity_function`` naming
``[Functions]`` entries for a radial profile, which is how a burnup- or
thermal-gradient-driven porosity distribution reaches the operator.

Both arms evaluate the coefficient **per point** through
:meth:`_diffusivity_at`, and with a material bound and no state supplied
they refuse rather than fall back. That refusal is the fix for a real
defect: the assembly multiplied by ``self.diffusivity`` regardless of
what was bound, so a deck naming ``uzr_nd_diffusivity`` built it,
attached it, and then solved a constant-coefficient problem — with
porosity, interconnection, sodium logging and every ablation switch
inert. Pinned by
``test_bound_material_changes_the_assembled_operator``.

Args:
    name: Kernel name (the sub-block key inside ``[Kernels]``).
    variable: Variable the kernel binds to (the concentration field).
    params: Validated parameters; see :meth:`params`.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

dim.name: dim
dim.doc: Spatial dimension of the field (1, 2 or 3). Must match the mesh dimension and the connected Variable.

diffusivity.name: diffusivity
diffusivity.doc: Constant effective diffusivity ``D``. Leave at the default and bind a ``uzr_nd_diffusivity`` material when the porosity- and temperature-dependent closure is wanted; the kernel owns the geometry, the material owns the physics.

material.name: material
material.doc: Name of a ``[Materials]`` block supplying the varying coefficient -- a ``uzr_nd_diffusivity``. Bound by the composed builder through the standard ``bind_material`` protocol. When set, ``diffusivity`` is not used and the state below becomes mandatory.

temperature.name: temperature
temperature.doc: Uniform temperature the bound closure is evaluated at, in K (absolute). Required when a ``material`` is bound and no ``temperature_function`` is given. Ignored otherwise.

porosity.name: porosity
porosity.doc: Uniform porosity the bound closure is evaluated at, a volume fraction in [0, 1). Required when a ``material`` is bound and no ``porosity_function`` is given. This is the variable the three transport regimes switch on, so a deck studying interconnection sweeps it.

temperature_function.name: temperature_function
temperature_function.doc: Name of a ``[Functions]`` entry giving temperature as a function of radius, for a thermal gradient across the slug. Wins over the uniform ``temperature``.

porosity_function.name: porosity_function
porosity_function.doc: Name of a ``[Functions]`` entry giving porosity as a function of radius. Wins over the uniform ``porosity``. Use ``kind = parsed`` with an expression in ``x`` (the radius).

axis_tolerance.name: axis_tolerance
axis_tolerance.doc: Radius inside which the strong form blends onto the L'Hopital limit ``(1/r) dc/dr -> d2c/dr2`` required by symmetry on the axis. Must be > 0: the blend is smooth because the PINN loss differentiates through this residual. Has no effect on the weak form, whose ``r dr`` measure makes the singular term integrable.

name: reaction
doc: Linear reaction term ``+ c u``.
full_doc:
Linear reaction term ``+ c u``.

Positive ``coefficient`` is decay/absorption; **negative** is the
Helmholtz term, where ``c = -k²`` turns ``diffusion + reaction`` into
``∇²u + k²u = 0``.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

dim.name: dim
dim.doc: Spatial dimension of the field (1, 2 or 3). Must match the mesh dimension and the connected Variable.

coefficient.name: coefficient
coefficient.doc: Reaction coefficient ``c`` in ``+ c u``. Positive is decay/absorption. Set ``c = -k^2`` alongside a ``diffusion`` kernel to obtain the Helmholtz equation ``lap(u) + k^2 u = 0``.

function.name: function
function.doc: Optional [Functions] entry giving a spatially varying scale on 'coefficient', resolved at quadrature points the same way body_source resolves a spatially varying source.

name: second_time_derivative
doc: Inertia term ``ρ ∂²u/∂t²`` — the wave equation's time operator.
full_doc:
Inertia term ``ρ ∂²u/∂t²`` — the wave equation's time operator.

Paired with ``diffusion`` (whose ``diffusivity`` is then the squared wave
speed ``c²``) this gives ``u_tt - c² ∇²u = 0``.

The FEM path returns the same mass matrix the first-order term does; a
second-order-in-time FEM integrator is not implemented, so the weak form
is currently only meaningful to a caller that supplies its own time
scheme. The **PINN path is the supported route for the wave equation**,
because a space–time collocation network differentiates twice in time
without needing one.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

dim.name: dim
dim.doc: Spatial dimension of the field (1, 2 or 3). Must match the mesh dimension and the connected Variable.

density.name: density
density.doc: Coefficient ``rho`` of the inertia term ``rho * d2u/dt2``. Leave at 1.0 for the standard wave equation, where the paired ``diffusion`` kernel's ``diffusivity`` carries the squared wave speed ``c^2``.

name: soret_diffusion
doc: Thermodiffusion flux :math:`\mathbf J_S = D Q c\,\nabla T / (k_B T^2)`.
full_doc:
Thermodiffusion flux :math:`\mathbf J_S = D Q c\,\nabla T / (k_B T^2)`.

Weak contribution :math:`(\mathbf J_S, \nabla\psi)` to the split-CH
conservation row, with the exact tangent

.. math::

    \frac{\partial\mathbf J_S}{\partial c} = \frac{DQ}{k_B T^2}\nabla T,
    \qquad
    \frac{\partial\mathbf J_S}{\partial T} = -\frac{2DQc}{k_B T^3}\nabla T,
    \qquad
    \frac{\partial\mathbf J_S}{\partial(\nabla T)} = \frac{DQc}{k_B T^2}\,\mathbf I.

The temperature is an ordinary fem variable of the deck (typically a
``diffusion`` kernel with Dirichlet ends — a steady algebraic row the
block executioner solves alongside the pair). It must be strictly
positive everywhere: give it a positive ``[ICs]`` entry.

Args:
    name: Kernel name (sub-block key inside ``[Kernels]``).
    variable: The chemical-potential variable (``mu``), as for
        ``split_ch_wres`` — the row is the conservation equation.
    params: Validated parameter dict (see :meth:`params`).

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must be 'soret_diffusion' — the split-form thermodiffusion flux (MOOSE SoretDiffusion) on the conservation row of the split Cahn-Hilliard pair.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the chemical-potential variable (``mu`` by convention) — the same binding as ``split_ch_wres``: the kernel lands on the ``split_ch_conservation`` row, next to the ``(M grad mu, grad psi)`` transport term, NOT on the potential-definition row of ``c``.

concentration.name: concentration
concentration.doc: Name of the conserved concentration fem variable ``c`` that the flux ``D Q c grad T / (k_B T^2)`` is proportional to.

temperature.name: temperature
temperature.doc: Name of the coupled temperature fem variable ``T`` (a deck variable with its own row, e.g. a ``diffusion`` kernel with Dirichlet ends). It must be strictly positive everywhere. Note the translator lower-cases [Variables] sub-block names, so a deck variable spelled ``[./T]`` is ``t`` after translation; set this key to the translated name (the shipped deck uses ``temp``).

diffusivity.name: diffusivity
diffusivity.doc: Solute diffusivity ``D`` multiplying the thermodiffusion flux.

heat_of_transport.name: heat_of_transport
heat_of_transport.doc: Heat of transport ``Q`` (per atom, in the energy unit ``boltzmann`` is quoted in). ``Q > 0`` drives solute toward the COLD side (physical current ``-J_S`` runs down grad T); ``Q < 0`` toward the hot side; ``0`` (default) switches the term off.

boltzmann.name: boltzmann
boltzmann.doc: Boltzmann constant ``k_B`` in the deck's energy/temperature units. Default 8.617333262e-5 eV/K (``Q`` in eV, ``T`` in kelvin); set to 1 for a nondimensional deck where ``Q`` is quoted in units of k_B T.

equation.name: equation
equation.doc: Row of the block system the flux joins. Empty (default) selects the split Cahn-Hilliard conservation row ``split_ch_conservation`` (the row ``split_ch_wres`` and ``coupled_time_derivative`` share). Set it explicitly only for a custom composition.

name: split_ch_parsed
doc: The chemical-potential definition on the conserved variable :math:`c`.
full_doc:
The chemical-potential definition on the conserved variable :math:`c`.

The residual :math:`f'(c) - \mu - \nabla\cdot(\kappa\nabla c)` closes
the pair: :math:`\mu` is :math:`f'(c) - \nabla\cdot(\kappa\nabla c)`.
The bulk term :math:`f'(c)` comes from the registered free energy
(``free_energy``); the gradient term is the standard isotropic gradient
energy with coefficient :math:`\kappa`.

Args:
    name: Kernel name.
    variable: The conserved variable (``c`` by convention).
    params: Validated parameter dict. ``free_energy`` selects the
        registered free-energy material by name; ``gradient_coefficient``
        is :math:`\kappa`.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must be 'split_ch_parsed' — the chemical-potential definition of split Cahn-Hilliard on the conserved variable.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the conserved variable this definition binds to (``c`` by convention).

free_energy.name: free_energy
free_energy.doc: Name of a [Materials] scalar free-energy block. The default double_well uses the inline barrier_height/minima unless a block of that name is declared. The bulk term is its first derivative.

chemical_potential.name: chemical_potential
chemical_potential.doc: Name of the chemical-potential fem variable ``mu`` that closes the definition ``mu = f'(c) - kappa laplacian(c)``; the block executioner reads it to assemble the ``-(mu, psi)`` coupling.

gradient_coefficient.name: gradient_coefficient
gradient_coefficient.doc: Gradient-energy coefficient ``\\kappa`` weighting the ``\\nabla\\cdot(\\kappa \\nabla c)`` term.

barrier_height.name: barrier_height
barrier_height.doc: Energy barrier ``W`` of the double-well bulk free energy; scales f(c) and hence f'(c) in the chemical potential.

minima.name: minima
minima.doc: The two minima of the double-well bulk free energy. Use ``[-1, 1]`` for the symmetric Cahn-Hilliard concentration double well.

name: split_ch_wres
doc: The transport term :math:`(M\nabla\mu,\nabla\psi)` on the chemical potential.
full_doc:
The transport term :math:`(M\nabla\mu,\nabla\psi)` on the chemical potential.

The weak form is the mass-weighted diffusion of :math:`\mu`, so this
kernel binds to the :math:`\mu` variable. The mobility :math:`M` is read
from a :class:`~pinnacle.materials.mobility.MobilityTensor` (the
``mobility_tensor`` / ``mobility`` material); an isotropic scalar mobility
is the common case.

Args:
    name: Kernel name.
    variable: The chemical-potential variable (``mu`` by convention).
    params: Validated parameter dict. ``mobility`` selects the registered
        ``mobility_tensor`` material by name; a bare scalar is also allowed.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must be 'split_ch_wres' — the transport term of split Cahn-Hilliard on the chemical potential variable.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the chemical-potential variable this transport term binds to (``mu`` by convention).

material.name: material
material.doc: Optional ``mobility_tensor`` / ``mobility`` [Materials] entry by name; the builder injects its live instance and it supplies the diffusivity tensor the transport term contracts at quadrature. Leave empty to use the bare scalar ``mobility =`` instead.

mobility.name: mobility
mobility.doc: Bare scalar mobility ``M0`` for the transport term ``M \nabla \mu`` when no ``material =`` is bound. To bind a spatially varying or anisotropic mobility, name a ``mobility_tensor`` material on the kernel's ``material =`` key — the builder injects its live instance and it takes precedence over this scalar.

name: stress_divergence
doc: Linear-elasticity kernel: weak + strong ``∇·σ + b = 0`` form.
full_doc:
Linear-elasticity kernel: weak + strong ``∇·σ + b = 0`` form.

The kernel binds to a :class:`Variable` of family ``fem`` or ``pinn``
(component count must equal the spatial dimension). The material is
isotropic linear-elastic and may be specified either as direct
``young``/``poisson`` params **or** as ``material = <name>``
referencing an ``isotropic_linear_elastic`` ``[Materials]`` entry.

When both spellings are present, the direct params win (the
material's values are silently ignored). The builder does not raise
here — Phase M14 ships both spellings as a *migration aid*; a future
phase can switch to a hard error once the decks are migrated.

Args:
    name: Kernel name (the sub-block key inside ``[Kernels]``).
    variable: Variable name the kernel binds to.
    params: Validated parameter dict. Must include ``dim`` and
        either ``young`` + ``poisson`` or ``material``.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

young.name: young
young.doc: Young's modulus ``E`` for the isotropic linear-elastic constitutive law. Required when no ``material`` reference is set.

poisson.name: poisson
poisson.doc: Poisson's ratio ``ν`` (dimensionless). Required when no ``material`` reference is set. Must lie in (-1, 0.5) for physical stability.

material.name: material
material.doc: Optional :class:`material` registry name to bind. When set, the builder looks the material up in the deck's ``[Materials]`` block and forwards its ``young`` / ``poisson`` to the kernel. Use this to share a single constitutive declaration across multiple kernels.

dim.name: dim
dim.doc: Spatial dimension of the problem (``1``, ``2``, or ``3``). Must match the connected :class:`Variable`'s component count.

body_force.name: body_force
body_force.doc: Optional constant body-force vector per unit volume. Defaults to zero. Length must equal ``dim``.

name: stress_divergence_cp
doc: Crystal-plasticity stress-divergence kernel (weak + strong form).
full_doc:
Crystal-plasticity stress-divergence kernel (weak + strong form).

The kernel binds to a :class:`Variable` of family ``fem`` or ``pinn``.
The CP material is looked up in the problem's materials bag by name
(``material`` parameter). The weak form reuses
:class:`~pinnacle.materials.cp_field_callback.CPFieldCallback`; the strong
form provides a PINN residual. Two strong-form variants are supported:

* **Displacement-only network** (the Rezwan PINN-constitutive route): the
  network outputs ``u(x, t)`` and the residual is ``∇·σ(∇u)`` with the CP
  material evaluated at its initial state.
* **Full-state network** (future spatial CP PINN): the network outputs
  ``(u, F^p, ρ, τ_c)`` and the residual delegates to
  :class:`~pinnacle.pinn.transient_cp_residual.TransientCPResidual`.

Args:
    name: Kernel name (the sub-block key inside ``[Kernels]``).
    variable: Variable name the kernel binds to.
    params: Validated parameter dict.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

dim.name: dim
dim.doc: Spatial dimension of the problem (``1``, ``2``, or ``3``). Must match the connected :class:`Variable`'s component count. ``3`` requires ``finite_strain=true``.

material.name: material
material.doc: Name of the ``[Materials]`` sub-block providing the CP constitutive law. The named material must implement :class:`~pinnacle.materials.constitutive_base.CrystalPlasticityModel` (exposes ``n_systems``, ``initial_state``, ``compute``). The kernel accepts any registered name; capability errors are reported by the protocol, not a name whitelist.

finite_strain.name: finite_strain
finite_strain.doc: When ``True`` the input ``H = ∇u`` is treated as the full displacement gradient and ``F = I + H`` is used.  Required for 3-D solves; rejected for 1-D/2-D small-strain solves.

gnd.name: gnd
gnd.doc: Toggle strain-gradient GND evolution. When ``True``, the :class:`CPFieldCallback` integrates the edge/screw GND densities from the slip-rate gradient; the FEM gradient operator is supplied by the executioner after the mesh is assembled.

gnd_backstress.name: gnd_backstress
gnd_backstress.doc: Placeholder flag for a future GND-gradient backstress. When ``True`` a zero per-system backstress field is stored but does not yet affect the flow rule (mirrors the legacy behaviour).

degradation.name: degradation
degradation.doc: Phase M7: optional name of the ``[Materials]`` entry of kind ``pfd_degradation`` that provides the ``g(d) = (1 - d)²`` stiffness reduction. The M7 contract requires the mechanics↔damage pairing to be **declared** in the deck (the runner wires it via :meth:`bind_degradation`); an empty string leaves the legacy undamaged path in place.

name: stress_divergence_j2
doc: Stress-divergence kernel for J2 isotropic hardening plasticity.
full_doc:
Stress-divergence kernel for J2 isotropic hardening plasticity.

The kernel binds to a displacement :class:`Variable` and enforces
``∇·σ = 0`` with ``σ`` from a J2 elastoplastic constitutive law. The
material is named by the ``material`` parameter and resolved against the
deck's ``[Materials]`` block; the builder injects the live instance under
``material_obj`` and via :meth:`bind_material`.

Args:
    name: Kernel name (sub-block key inside ``[Kernels]``).
    variable: Displacement variable name this kernel applies to.
    params: Validated parameter dict. Must include ``dim`` and ``material``.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

dim.name: dim
dim.doc: Spatial dimension of the problem (1, 2 or 3). Must match the component count of the bound displacement variable. ``2`` is solved as **plane strain**: the return map runs on the 3-D embedding with ε₃₃ = 0, so the deviatoric split and the yield surface are the three-dimensional ones. ``1`` is the uniaxial-stress bar.

material.name: material
material.doc: Name of the ``[Materials]`` entry providing the J2 constitutive law (``j2_isotropic_hardening``, or any material exposing the same ``update_batch`` / ``yield_stress`` interface). The kernel accepts any registered name; capability errors are reported by the protocol, not a name whitelist.

body_force.name: body_force
body_force.doc: Optional constant body force per unit volume, one entry per spatial dimension (N/m³). Enters the strong form as ``∇·σ + b`` and defaults to zero.

degradation.name: degradation
degradation.doc: Optional name of the ``[Materials]`` entry of kind ``pfd_degradation`` supplying ``g(d)``. When set, the coupled executioner pushes the damage field through it and the quadrature-point stress and tangent are multiplied by ``g(d)`` — the mechanics←damage leg of the staggered coupling. An empty string leaves the undamaged path in place.

displacement_variable.name: displacement_variable
displacement_variable.doc: Optional explicit name of the displacement field variable. If omitted, the kernel's ``variable`` parameter is used.

name: switching_constraint_eta
doc: The multiplier force row on one order parameter ``eta_i``.
full_doc:
The multiplier force row on one order parameter ``eta_i``.

The weak load :math:`\bigl(\lambda\,h'(\eta_i),\ \psi_i\bigr)` is
the :math:`\lambda\,\partial k/\partial\eta_i` term of the KKT
system — paired with the ``switching_constraint_lagrange`` row on the
multiplier, one instance per order parameter.

Args:
    name: Kernel name.
    variable: The order parameter ``eta_i`` this force row binds to.
    params: Validated parameter dict — ``lambda`` names the multiplier
        variable, ``switching`` picks ``h``.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

lambda.name: lambda
lambda.doc: Name of the Lagrange-multiplier variable the KKT force row couples to. Must be declared in ``[Variables]`` and carried by a ``switching_constraint_lagrange`` kernel.

switching.name: switching
switching.doc: Switching-function variant ``h(eta)`` whose derivative ``h'(eta)`` weights the force row.

name: switching_constraint_lagrange
doc: The Lagrange-multiplier row of the switching constraint, on ``lambda``.
full_doc:
The Lagrange-multiplier row of the switching constraint, on ``lambda``.

The weak row :math:`\bigl(\sum_i h(\eta_i) - 1 -
\tfrac{\epsilon}{2}\lambda,\ \psi_\lambda\bigr)` closes the KKT
system whose ``eta`` rows come from the ``switching_constraint_eta``
kernels. The deck must declare the multiplier in ``[Variables]`` and
add both kernel kinds; see ``switching_constraints_2d.i``.

Args:
    name: Kernel name.
    variable: The multiplier variable (``lambda`` by convention).
    params: Validated parameter dict — ``phase_fields`` lists the order
        parameters, ``switching`` picks ``h``, ``epsilon`` is the
        Jacobian regulariser.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

phase_fields.name: phase_fields
phase_fields.doc: Names of the order-parameter variables the switching constraint sums: ``sum_i h(eta_i) = 1``. Every name must be declared in ``[Variables]``.

switching.name: switching
switching.doc: Switching-function variant ``h(eta)``: ``simple`` is ``3eta^2 - 2eta^3`` (satisfies ``h(1-eta) = 1 - h(eta)``, the identity the hard two-phase elimination relies on); ``high`` is ``eta^3(6eta^2 - 15eta + 10)``.

epsilon.name: epsilon
epsilon.doc: Jacobian regulariser of the multiplier row: the row reads ``sum h - 1 - eps/2 * lambda``. Without it (eps = 0) the multiplier row has no diagonal and the block Jacobian is nearly rank-deficient; the default avoids that at the cost of a constraint violation of order ``eps`` at the linearised solution. Set 0 only with a least-squares solve.

name: switching_penalty
doc: The penalty force row on one order parameter ``eta_i``.
full_doc:
The penalty force row on one order parameter ``eta_i``.

The gradient of the penalty energy
:math:`\tfrac{W_{\mathrm{pen}}}{2}\bigl(\sum_i h(\eta_i) - 1\bigr)^2`
w.r.t. :math:`\eta_i`: the weak load
:math:`\bigl(2 W_{\mathrm{pen}}\,k\,h'(\eta_i),\ \psi_i\bigr)`.
The constraint is enforced only to a scale of
:math:`\sim 1/W_{\mathrm{pen}}` (the acceptance tests measure the
scaling); a very large ``penalty`` makes the block Jacobian stiff, the
same trade the Lagrange variant makes explicitly.

Args:
    name: Kernel name.
    variable: The order parameter ``eta_i`` this force row binds to.
    params: Validated parameter dict — ``phase_fields`` lists all order
        parameters (including this one), ``penalty`` is
        :math:`W_{\mathrm{pen}}`.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

phase_fields.name: phase_fields
phase_fields.doc: Names of the order-parameter variables the switching constraint sums (including the variable this kernel binds to — every instance needs the whole list to evaluate ``sum h - 1``).

switching.name: switching
switching.doc: Switching-function variant ``h(eta)`` whose derivative ``h'(eta)`` weights the penalty force.

penalty.name: penalty
penalty.doc: Penalty stiffness ``W_pen > 0`` of the soft constraint energy ``W_pen/2 (sum h - 1)^2``. The switching-sum violation at the solution scales as ``1 / W_pen``; large values stiffen the block Jacobian.

name: time_derivative
doc: Kernel that contributes the time-derivative term ``∂u/∂t``.
full_doc:
Kernel that contributes the time-derivative term ``∂u/∂t``.

The kernel is the *sum* of the mass-matrix part of the Allen–Cahn /
Cahn–Hilliard / grain-growth systems; it is registered as a first-class
kernel so that mixed equations (e.g. Cahn–Hilliard + AC) can be built by
registering multiple kernels against the same variable.

Args:
    name: Kernel name (sub-block key inside ``[Kernels]``).
    variable: Variable name.
    params: Validated parameter dict. The only required key is
        ``variable`` (set by the builder); ``make_material`` is
        optional — pass ``make_material=true`` to use the kernel in
        a FEM executioner.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered kernel name; must match a ``@registry.register('kernel', <name>)``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Name of the :class:`Variable` this kernel applies to. Must match a ``[Variables]`` sub-block key.

make_material.name: make_material
make_material.doc: When ``true``, the FEM executioner builds a scalar mass + stiffness pair from this kernel. Disable for purely PINN transient solves where the strong form is sufficient.

coefficient.name: coefficient
coefficient.doc: Coefficient of the time term, ``rho*c * du/dt``. For heat conduction this is the volumetric heat capacity ``rho * c_p`` (J/m^3/K), so that paired with a ``diffusion`` kernel carrying the conductivity ``k`` the two make the physical heat equation. Leave at 1.0 for a normalised diffusion problem.

dim.name: dim
dim.doc: Spatial dimension, accepted for uniformity with the other scalar-transport kernels and ignored. The time term is genuinely dimension-independent — the mass matrix comes from the shape functions alone — so this kernel takes the dimension from the mesh. Declaring it keeps a heat-equation deck consistent, where the ``diffusion`` term beside it does require ``dim``.

name: barrier_function
doc: Interface barrier function ``g(η)`` with ``g'`` and ``g''``.
full_doc:
Interface barrier function ``g(η)`` with ``g'`` and ``g''``.

Implements the three barrier functions of the phase-field literature:

.. math::
    g(n) = n^2(1-n)^2 \quad\text{(SIMPLE)}, \qquad
    g(n) = n(1-n) \quad\text{(LOW)}, \qquad
    g(n) = n^2(1-n^2)^2 \quad\text{(HIGH)},

each vanishing at the two phase end-points (``g(0)=g(1)=0``) so the
interface has finite, localised energy. The SIMPLE form peaks at
``g(1/2)=1/16``; the LOW form is the grand-potential model's linear barrier.
Derivatives are closed-form.

variant.name: variant
variant.doc: Which barrier function to use: ``simple`` (``η²(1−η)²``), ``low`` (``η(1−η)``, the grand-potential linear barrier) or ``high`` (``η²(1−η²)²``).

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: The field the barrier acts on.

name: clad_properties
doc: Cladding creep rupture and void swelling.
full_doc:
Cladding creep rupture and void swelling.

Void swelling carries an **incubation dose**, which is HT9's engineering
advantage: no swelling accumulates until the threshold is exceeded.
Creep rupture uses Larson--Miller in its native units (hours), converted
internally to seconds.

.. warning::
   The default Larson--Miller coefficients are **fitted to two
   order-of-magnitude-plausible anchor points for 12Cr
   ferritic-martensitic cladding, not taken from a qualified HT9 rupture
   correlation.** They are exposed as parameters precisely so that a deck
   making a life claim must supply its own. Use this for ranking and
   sensitivity, never for a licensing life prediction.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered component name; must match a ``@registry.register(<category>, <name>)``.

kind.name: kind
kind.doc: Registered material name, injected by the builder.

alloy.name: alloy
alloy.doc: Cladding alloy. Only the void-swelling parameters are alloy-resolved today; the creep coefficients are supplied directly (see the class warning).

lmp_a.name: lmp_a
lmp_a.doc: Larson-Miller intercept A in LMP = A + B log10(sigma/sigma_ref). Default FITTED to the LMP_ANCHORS points, not a qualified HT9 correlation -- supply your own for any life claim.

lmp_b.name: lmp_b
lmp_b.doc: Larson-Miller stress slope B. Negative: higher stress shortens life. Default FITTED to LMP_ANCHORS; see lmp_a.

lmp_constant.name: lmp_constant
lmp_constant.doc: Larson-Miller constant C in log10(t_r[h]) = 1000*LMP/T - C. 20 is the conventional value for ferritic steels.

reference_stress.name: reference_stress
reference_stress.doc: Stress normalisation sigma_ref inside the LMP log term.

swelling_incubation_dpa.name: swelling_incubation_dpa
swelling_incubation_dpa.doc: Void-swelling incubation dose. No swelling accumulates below it. HT9's large incubation dose is the reason it displaced the austenitic claddings for high-burnup service. The default shown is the HT9 row; omitting this resolves it from the SELECTED alloy instead, and alloys whose sources carry no value (D9, SS316) raise rather than borrow HT9's.

swelling_rate_per_dpa.name: swelling_rate_per_dpa
swelling_rate_per_dpa.doc: Void-swelling rate once the incubation dose is exceeded. Alloy-resolved on the same terms as swelling_incubation_dpa.

cdf_limit.name: cdf_limit
cdf_limit.doc: Cumulative damage fraction limit used as the failure criterion. 0.05 is the IFR-era design value for EBR-II metallic-fuel pins.

name: clad_wastage_empirical
doc: Empirical FCCI wastage of the cladding, alloy-keyed.
full_doc:
Empirical FCCI wastage of the cladding, alloy-keyed.

Parabolic kinetics ``w = sqrt(K t)`` with an alloy-specific rate constant
that adds a thermal (Arrhenius) and an irradiation-assisted (flux-linear)
contribution. The two terms are separately switchable because their
relative size is the discriminator between cladding families rather than
a detail: the flux term supplies most of the rate for D9 and SS316 at
450 C but a minority of it for HT9.

Because the interaction layer impedes further attack, depth grows as the
square root of time -- so **temperature dominates duration**. A 50 K rise
outweighs a doubling of exposure.

.. warning::
   ``wall_thickness`` is **required** and has no default anywhere in this
   chain. Stress amplification goes as ``t_w / (t_w - w)``, so an
   over-stated wall *under-states* stress -- the non-conservative
   direction -- by a margin that grows with wastage. The primary-source
   EBR-II pin wall is 406.4 um (16 mil).

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered component name; must match a ``@registry.register(<category>, <name>)``.

kind.name: kind
kind.doc: Registered material name, injected by the builder.

alloy.name: alloy
alloy.doc: Cladding alloy selecting the wastage coefficient set. Required with no default: a severity answer computed for the wrong cladding is worse than an error.

wall_thickness.name: wall_thickness
wall_thickness.doc: As-fabricated cladding wall thickness. REQUIRED, no default. The EBR-II X447/X430 pins are 406.4e-6 m (16 mil). An over-stated wall under-states hoop stress; see the warning in this class's docstring and docs/physics/uzr_metallic_fuel.md section 3.2.

coolant_side_allowance.name: coolant_side_allowance
coolant_side_allowance.doc: Coolant-side (CCCI) wall loss subtracted alongside FCCI. Defaults to 0.0 to reproduce the FCCI-only literature comparison -- NOT because 0.0 is conservative. The X447 page reports ~20e-6 m of coolant-side wastage at the same axial station where FCCI peaks, so an FCCI-only result is optimistic by roughly that much.

kinetic_exponent.name: kinetic_exponent
kinetic_exponent.doc: Exponent n in the moving-boundary law delta = sqrt(K t_ref) (t/t_ref)^n. 0.5 is parabolic (diffusion-limited) and reduces exactly to sqrt(K t). Left as a deck parameter because the source material does not settle it, and n > 0.5 would mean the interaction layer is less protective than parabolic kinetics implies -- a severity question. Note the exponent applies to the dimensionless time ratio, not to K t, which would only be dimensionally consistent at n = 0.5.

reference_exposure.name: reference_exposure
reference_exposure.doc: Reference exposure t_ref at which all kinetic exponents give the same depth; defaults to one year. Has no effect at the default kinetic_exponent of 0.5. For other exponents it sets where the deviation from parabolic is centred, so a deck sweeping the exponent should set this to the campaign length it cares about.

include_thermal.name: include_thermal
include_thermal.doc: Include the Arrhenius term (sensitivity ablation switch).

include_irradiation.name: include_irradiation
include_irradiation.doc: Include the flux-linear term (sensitivity ablation switch).

name: dislocation_density_cp
doc: Dislocation-density-based CP constitutive model.
full_doc:
Dislocation-density-based CP constitutive model.

Optional Armstrong–Frederick kinematic hardening is supported through the
material keys ``backstress_c`` and ``backstress_d``.  When both are zero the
model reduces to the isotropic-hardening baseline.

mu.name: mu
mu.doc: Shear modulus used in Taylor hardening. Defaults to C44.

gamma0.name: gamma0
gamma0.doc: Reference slip rate of the power law.

rate_exponent_n.name: rate_exponent_n
rate_exponent_n.doc: Power-law rate-sensitivity exponent n. Larger values are more rate-insensitive (and stiffer to train a PINN on).

tau_c0.name: tau_c0
tau_c0.doc: Initial critical resolved shear stress (slip resistance).

q_lat.name: q_lat
q_lat.doc: Latent-hardening ratio: off-diagonal entries of the slip-system interaction matrix (1.0 = isotropic hardening).

k1.name: k1
k1.doc: Kocks–Mecking storage coefficient (athermal accumulation). With k2 it sets the saturation density rho* = (k1/k2)^2.

backstress_c.name: backstress_c
backstress_c.doc: Armstrong–Frederick direct-hardening modulus. Non-zero enables kinematic hardening (Bauschinger effect under load reversal).

backstress_d.name: backstress_d
backstress_d.doc: Armstrong–Frederick dynamic-recovery coefficient for the backstress.

name: double_well
doc: Free-energy density provider backed by a :class:`DoubleWellBulkEnergy`.
full_doc:
Free-energy density provider backed by a :class:`DoubleWellBulkEnergy`.

Registered under the **legacy** name ``double_well`` (unchanged, so
existing decks and the golden parity harness keep working). The class now
additionally satisfies :class:`FreeEnergyClosure`, so it can be read by the
P1-split kernels, the ``pf_pinn`` executioner and the energy loss without
any kernel change.

barrier_height.name: barrier_height
barrier_height.doc: Bulk energy barrier ``W`` between the two minima.

name: electrical_conductivity
doc: Electrical conductivity ``sigma_e``, reusing ``k(T)``'s generic constant/linear/parsed forms.
full_doc:
Electrical conductivity ``sigma_e``, reusing ``k(T)``'s generic constant/linear/parsed forms.

The underlying math (a scalar coefficient, optionally a function of one
scalar field) is identical to ``thermal_conductivity`` — this is a
distinctly-registered name for deck clarity (``[Materials] kind =
electrical_conductivity``, consumed as the ``diffusion`` kernel's
``material =`` on the potential Variable, and by :class:`JouleSourceKernel`
for the source coefficient), not a duplicated implementation.

form.name: form
form.doc: Functional form of k(T). 'constant': k = k0. 'linear': k = k0 * (1 + alpha * (T - T_ref)), the MOOSE HeatConductionMaterial temperature-coefficient form. 'table': piecewise-linear interpolation of 'temperature_values' / 'conductivity_values' pairs with flat extrapolation (FEM-only). 'parsed': an arbitrary expression in T (FEM-only; no PINN autodiff route).

temperature_values.name: temperature_values
temperature_values.doc: Strictly increasing tabulated temperatures for form='table' (at least two entries).

k0.name: k0
k0.doc: Reference (or, for 'constant', the only) conductivity value.

reference_temperature.name: reference_temperature
reference_temperature.doc: Reference temperature T_ref the linear form is centred on.

expression.name: expression
expression.doc: Expression in 'T' (plus 'k0', 'alpha', 'T_ref' and NumPy math functions) for kind='parsed', e.g. 'k0 * exp(-alpha * T)'.

name: gb_evolution
doc: Isotropic quantitative grain-growth parameter map (MOOSE ``GBEvolution``).
full_doc:
Isotropic quantitative grain-growth parameter map (MOOSE ``GBEvolution``).

Constructed through the builder's ``params=`` contract (a
``[Materials]`` entry with ``kind = gb_evolution``) or directly with
keywords (tests, plugins). The instance is backend-agnostic: it is a
constant map, so ``bind`` only builds the multi-order-parameter bulk
energy the runner injects into kernels through the ``free_energy`` slot.

Attributes:
    M0: The declared base mobility :math:`M_0`.
    mobility_mode: ``"constant"`` or ``"arrhenius"``.
    Q: Activation energy (J/mol) for the Arrhenius branch.
    temperature: Declared temperature (K); ``0.0`` keeps the constant
        mobility.
    R: Gas constant used in the Arrhenius denominator.
    L: Mapped Allen–Cahn mobility :math:`L = 4M_{GB}/(3w_{GB})`.
    mu: Mapped bulk energy scale :math:`\mu = 6\sigma/w_{GB}`.
    kappa: Mapped gradient-energy coefficient
        :math:`\kappa = 3\sigma w_{GB}/4`.
    gamma: Moelans multi-order-parameter coupling.
    free_energy: The :class:`GrainGrowthEnergy` built by ``bind`` —
        ``None`` until the runner (or a test) binds a backend.

M_GB.name: M_GB
M_GB.doc: Grain-boundary mobility ``M0`` (> 0). With ``mobility_mode = arrhenius`` this is the pre-exponential factor and the effective mobility is ``M0 exp(-Q/(R T))``.

w_GB.name: w_GB
w_GB.doc: Diffuse-interface width ``w_GB`` (> 0). Sets the spatial resolution the mesh needs (keep ``h <= w_GB / 3``) and the mapped mobility/energy split; the physics (``L * kappa = M_GB * sigma``) is independent of it.

sigma.name: sigma
sigma.doc: Isotropic grain-boundary energy ``sigma`` (> 0). With the map this is the surface tension the curvature flow uses.

gamma.name: gamma
gamma.doc: Moelans multi-order-parameter coupling ``gamma`` (> 0). 1.5 is the quantitative isotropic form; it also fixes the ``grain_growth_energy`` bulk energy this material exposes.

mobility_mode.name: mobility_mode
mobility_mode.doc: Mobility branch: 'constant' uses ``M_GB`` as-is; 'arrhenius' activates ``M_GB(T) = M0 exp(-Q/(R T))`` and requires a positive ``temperature``.

Q.name: Q
Q.doc: Activation energy of the Arrhenius mobility (>= 0). Use the same per-quantity convention as ``R`` (J/mol with the molar gas constant, or eV/atom with R = 8.617e-5 eV/K).

temperature.name: temperature
temperature.doc: Temperature for the Arrhenius branch (>= 0; 0 keeps the constant mobility). Required (> 0) when ``mobility_mode = arrhenius``.

energy_units.name: energy_units
energy_units.doc: Unit system of the activation energy ``Q``: ``J/mol`` pairs with the molar gas constant, ``eV`` (per atom, the MOOSE GBEvolution convention) with the Boltzmann constant 8.617e-5 eV/K. Sets the default of ``R`` so a MOOSE deck's ``Q = 0.23`` is not silently read as 0.23 J/mol.

R.name: R
R.doc: Gas (or Boltzmann) constant in the Arrhenius denominator (> 0). Defaults from ``energy_units``: 8.314462618 J/(mol·K) for J/mol, 8.617333262e-5 eV/K for eV; set explicitly to override.

name: grain_growth_energy
doc: Moelans-type multi-order-parameter grain-growth free energy.
full_doc:
Moelans-type multi-order-parameter grain-growth free energy.

Registered under the legacy name ``grain_growth_energy`` (unchanged).
Satisfies :class:`FreeEnergyClosure`: the multi-component coupling term
``γ Σ_{i<j} η_i² η_j²`` has a short closed-form gradient/Hessian, so no
autodiff is needed for the energy itself.

gamma.name: gamma
gamma.doc: Coupling coefficient in the Moelans energy: penalises co-occupation of two order parameters. Use ``gamma = 1.5`` for the standard form (sum of squared pair products). The limiting case ``gamma = 0`` decouples the wells (degenerate).

name: isotropic_linear_elastic
doc: Bag for an isotropic linear-elastic constitutive law.
full_doc:
Bag for an isotropic linear-elastic constitutive law.

Carries ``young`` (Pa) and ``poisson`` (dimensionless, in
``(-1, 0.5)``) and exposes ``as_dict()`` for the legacy translator.
The :class:`ComposedProblem` builder stores this object in the
materials bag keyed by the deck's sub-block name; the kernel binds
the values into its own state via the ``material`` parameter.

This mirrors the phasefield ``double_well`` / ``grain_growth_energy``
material pattern: a registered, declarative provider whose
*attributes* feed the kernel. We do not call ``.bind(backend)`` here
because :class:`IsotropicLinearElasticDim` and
:class:`ElasticityResidual` are backend-agnostic — the elastic
constants are plain floats.

young.name: young
young.doc: Young's modulus ``E`` for the isotropic linear-elastic constitutive law. Required. Aliases: ``E``.

poisson.name: poisson
poisson.doc: Poisson's ratio ``ν`` (dimensionless). Required. Must lie in (-1, 0.5) for physical stability. Aliases: ``nu``.

name: j2_constitutive_pinn
doc: Local J2 constitutive PINN: a learned scalar consistency factor.
full_doc:
Local J2 constitutive PINN: a learned scalar consistency factor.

The component is inert until :meth:`bind` supplies a backend and a
reference material; the ``j2_constitutive`` executioner does both and then
calls :meth:`train`.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered component name; must match a ``@registry.register(<category>, <name>)``.

hidden_layers.name: hidden_layers
hidden_layers.doc: Number of hidden layers in the constitutive neural network.

hidden_units.name: hidden_units
hidden_units.doc: Number of neurons per hidden layer in the constitutive network.

activation.name: activation
activation.doc: Activation function used in the constitutive network's hidden layers.

learning_rate.name: learning_rate
learning_rate.doc: Adam learning rate for training the constitutive PINN weights.

n_epochs.name: n_epochs
n_epochs.doc: Number of Adam epochs used to train the constitutive PINN.

reference_material.name: reference_material
reference_material.doc: Name of the [Materials] entry holding the classical j2_isotropic_hardening law. It supplies the elastic constants, the hardening curve σ_y(α) and the supervision targets. Required before training; the executioner injects it.

alpha_ref.name: alpha_ref
alpha_ref.doc: Reference equivalent plastic strain used to non-dimensionalise the network's hardening-state input. Set it near the largest α the model will see so the input stays O(1).

finite_strain.name: finite_strain
finite_strain.doc: Enable finite-strain mode: the input tensor is interpreted as the deformation gradient F and mapped to the objective Hencky strain ½ln(F Fᵀ) before the return map, matching the finite_strain option of j2_isotropic_hardening.

name: j2_isotropic_hardening
doc: J2 isotropic hardening material with a consistent radial return.
full_doc:
J2 isotropic hardening material with a consistent radial return.

Parameters are declared via :meth:`params` and validated by the component
framework. The constitutive update is backend-agnostic: the local return
map runs in NumPy (it is a per-quadrature-point scalar Newton solve, and
the FEM Newton consumes the *analytic* consistent tangent rather than
differentiating through it), and the results are handed back through the
active backend's tensor constructor.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered component name; must match a ``@registry.register(<category>, <name>)``.

sigma_y0.name: sigma_y0
sigma_y0.doc: Initial yield stress σ_y0 in Pa.

K.name: K
K.doc: Isotropic hardening modulus K in Pa (power-law mode).

n.name: n
n.doc: Isotropic hardening exponent n (dimensionless) in σ_y(α) = σ_y0 + K α^n. n = 1 gives linear hardening, which is the only law the differentiable PINN strong form supports.

hardening_mode.name: hardening_mode
hardening_mode.doc: Hardening law mode: 'power' for σ_y0 + K α^n, 'piecewise' for a tabulated curve.

plastic_strain_points.name: plastic_strain_points
plastic_strain_points.doc: Equivalent plastic strain abscissae of the piecewise hardening table. Must be ascending and the same length as yield_stress_points.

yield_stress_points.name: yield_stress_points
yield_stress_points.doc: Yield stress ordinates (Pa) of the piecewise hardening table.

hardening_function.name: hardening_function
hardening_function.doc: Optional [Functions] name evaluated at α to give σ_y(α). Takes precedence over hardening_mode; the MOOSE PiecewiseLinear hardening idiom maps onto it directly.

finite_strain.name: finite_strain
finite_strain.doc: Enable finite-strain kinematics. When True the tensor handed to the constitutive update is interpreted as the deformation gradient F and mapped to the objective spatial Hencky strain E = ½ ln(F Fᵀ) before the return map, so the response is objective under a rigid rotation F → R F.

name: kalidindi
doc: Phenomenological power-law CP model with saturation hardening.
full_doc:
Phenomenological power-law CP model with saturation hardening.

Optional Armstrong–Frederick kinematic hardening is supported through the
material keys ``backstress_c`` and ``backstress_d``.  When both are zero the
model reduces to the isotropic-hardening baseline.

gamma0.name: gamma0
gamma0.doc: Reference slip rate of the power law.

m.name: m
m.doc: Rate-sensitivity exponent of the flow rule (the reciprocal of the 'n' used by dislocation_density_cp; smaller m is more rate-insensitive).

g_sat.name: g_sat
g_sat.doc: Saturation slip resistance the hardening evolves toward.

hardening_exp.name: hardening_exp
hardening_exp.doc: Exponent 'a' shaping the approach to saturation.

backstress_d.name: backstress_d
backstress_d.doc: Armstrong–Frederick dynamic-recovery coefficient for the backstress.

name: kks_phase_free_energy
doc: Parabolic phase free energy :math:`f(c) = \tfrac{A}{2}(c - c_{\mathrm{eq}})^2`.
full_doc:
Parabolic phase free energy :math:`f(c) = \tfrac{A}{2}(c - c_{\mathrm{eq}})^2`.

The standard KKS test energy: a single composition well per phase. The
equal-chemical-potential constraint :math:`f_a'(c_a) = f_b'(c_b)` is
linear in the phase concentrations for parabolic wells, which is what
makes the P8 acceptance criteria analytically checkable.

Constructed through the builder's ``params=`` contract (a
``[Materials]`` entry with ``kind = kks_phase_free_energy``) or directly
with keywords (tests, plugins, kernels).

Args:
    params: Deck parameter dict (the ``[Materials]`` sub-block), or
        ``None`` when constructed by keyword.
    curvature: Curvature :math:`A > 0` (energy per composition-squared).
    equilibrium: Well bottom :math:`c_{\mathrm{eq}}` (dimensionless
        composition).

curvature.name: curvature
curvature.doc: Curvature ``A > 0`` of the parabolic phase free energy ``f(c) = A/2 (c - c_eq)^2``; sets the phase's stiffness against composition excursions.

equilibrium.name: equilibrium
equilibrium.doc: Equilibrium composition ``c_eq`` of the phase well (dimensionless); the bottom of the parabola.

name: kks_phase_pair
doc: The two-phase free-energy pair the ``kks_*`` kernels bind.
full_doc:
The two-phase free-energy pair the ``kks_*`` kernels bind.

A KKS kernel needs **both** phase energies (the equal-chemical-potential
row and the phase-reconstructed chemical potential each read
:math:`f_a` *and* :math:`f_b`), but the builder injects exactly one
``material_obj`` per kernel. This container is that one material: it
holds an :math:`a`- and a :math:`b`-phase
:class:`KKSPhaseFreeEnergy` and exposes them as :attr:`fa` / :attr:`fb`.

Args:
    params: Deck parameter dict (the ``[Materials]`` sub-block), or
        ``None`` when constructed by keyword.
    curvature_a: Curvature of the :math:`a`-phase parabola.
    equilibrium_a: Well bottom of the :math:`a`-phase parabola.
    curvature_b: Curvature of the :math:`b`-phase parabola.
    equilibrium_b: Well bottom of the :math:`b`-phase parabola.

curvature_a.name: curvature_a
curvature_a.doc: Curvature ``A_a > 0`` of the a-phase parabolic free energy ``f_a(c_a) = A_a/2 (c_a - c_eq_a)^2``.

equilibrium_a.name: equilibrium_a
equilibrium_a.doc: Equilibrium composition ``c_eq_a`` of the a-phase well (dimensionless).

curvature_b.name: curvature_b
curvature_b.doc: Curvature ``A_b > 0`` of the b-phase parabolic free energy ``f_b(c_b) = A_b/2 (c_b - c_eq_b)^2``.

equilibrium_b.name: equilibrium_b
equilibrium_b.doc: Equilibrium composition ``c_eq_b`` of the b-phase well (dimensionless).

phase_a.name: phase_a
phase_a.doc: Optional name of a sibling ``[Materials]`` block of kind ``kks_phase_free_energy`` to use as the a-phase energy; when set it replaces ``curvature_a`` / ``equilibrium_a`` (the by-name route).

phase_b.name: phase_b
phase_b.doc: Optional name of a sibling ``[Materials]`` block of kind ``kks_phase_free_energy`` to use as the b-phase energy; when set it replaces ``curvature_b`` / ``equilibrium_b``.

name: mobility
doc: Simple isotropic mobility scalar :math:`M_0` for split Cahn–Hilliard.
full_doc:
Simple isotropic mobility scalar :math:`M_0` for split Cahn–Hilliard.

Thin wrapper around :class:`MobilityTensor` in the ``"scalar"`` branch,
kept as a first-class material so a deck can write ``[Materials] M {
kind = mobility }`` rather than reaching into the tensor variant.

Args:
    params: Builder-style parameter dict (``mobility`` key).
    mobility: Direct keyword form of the base scalar :math:`M_0 > 0`.

name: mobility_tensor
doc: Spatially varying mobility (inverse-diffusivity) for split Cahn–Hilliard.
full_doc:
Spatially varying mobility (inverse-diffusivity) for split Cahn–Hilliard.

Constructed either directly (keyword form, used by tests and the kernel's
bare-scalar fallback) or through the builder's ``params=`` contract (used
by ``[Materials]`` blocks).

Args:
    params: Builder-style parameter dict with the keys ``mobility``,
        ``branch``, ``spatial_scale_fn`` and ``M0``. The deck's ``kind``
        key (the registry selector) is ignored here.
    backend: Active numerical backend (unused for the NumPy reductions
        here, but kept so the object slots into the ``material`` registry
        like every other component).
    mobility: Base scalar :math:`M_0 > 0` (fallback when ``params`` does
        not carry one).
    kind: Branch name, keyword form (fallback when ``params`` does not
        carry a ``branch``).
    spatial_scale_fn: Optional callable mapping ``(n, dim)`` quadrature
        coordinates to ``(n,)`` multipliers :math:`k(\mathbf x)`.
    M0: ``(dim, dim)`` symmetric positive-definite tensor for the
        ``"tensor"`` branch (defaults to the identity).

Attributes:
    backend: Active backend.
    mobility: Base scalar :math:`M_0`.
    kind: Mobility branch (``"scalar"`` / ``"spatial"`` / ``"tensor"``).
    spatial_scale_fn: Optional spatial multiplier callable.
    M0: Inverse-mobility tensor for the ``"tensor"`` branch.

branch.name: branch
branch.doc: Mobility branch: 'scalar' (isotropic ``mobility``), 'spatial' (``mobility * k(x)`` through 'spatial_scale_fn') or 'tensor' (anisotropic ``mobility * k(x) * M0`` through 'M0'). Note the deck's ``kind`` key selects the *material*; this key selects the branch.

spatial_scale_fn.name: spatial_scale_fn
spatial_scale_fn.doc: Optional ``[Functions]`` block name giving the spatial profile k(x) (evaluated at the quadrature points through the function's spatial values, e.g. a ``parsed`` function of x, y, z); empty for a spatially uniform mobility.

M0.name: M0
M0.doc: Flattened symmetric positive-definite anisotropic mobility tensor (row-major, dim x dim entries) multiplying the base ``mobility``; empty means the identity (isotropic). ``'2 0 0 1'`` doubles the mobility along x in 2-D.

name: multiphase_free_energy
doc: N-phase WBM free energy ``F = sum_i h_i(eta) F_i + W g(eta)``.
full_doc:
N-phase WBM free energy ``F = sum_i h_i(eta) F_i + W g(eta)``.

See the module docstring for the switching / barrier definitions and the
two consumption protocols. Construction accepts the validated deck params
or the same keys as Python keyword arguments; ``phase_energies`` entries
may be sibling ``[Materials]`` names (resolved by
:meth:`bind_material_references`), numbers (constant bulk energies), or
closure objects (Python use).

Args:
    params: Validated parameter dict (see :meth:`params`).
    variables: Names of the ``N`` order parameters, in phase order.
    phase_energies: ``N`` phase free energies (names, numbers or closures).
    switching: ``"normalised"`` or ``"simple"``.
    barrier_height: The barrier scale ``W`` multiplying ``g``.
    gamma: The cross-term coefficient of the multi-well barrier.
    epsilon: Regulariser of the normalised switching denominator.

variables.name: variables
variables.doc: Names of the ``N`` order parameters in phase order (``variables = 'eta1 eta2 eta3'``). For the FEM ``ac_bulk`` path declare ONE fem variable with ``components = N``: the names are then the labels of its columns, in order, and the phase energies may reference them. Every name must be supplied whenever the closure is evaluated on named fields.

phase_energies.name: phase_energies
phase_energies.doc: One phase free energy ``F_i`` per order parameter, in the same order: sibling ``[Materials]`` block names (``'fa fb fc'`` — any closure such as ``double_well``, ``parsed_free_energy``, ``polynomial_free_energy``, resolved after every block is built) or plain numbers (``'0.0 0.0 -0.05'``, constant bulk energies in J/m^3 for an Allen-Cahn-only problem). Entries may be mixed.

switching.name: switching
switching.doc: Switching functions ``h_i``: ``normalised`` is ``eta_i^2 / (epsilon + sum_j eta_j^2)`` (MOOSE SwitchingFunctionMultiPhaseMaterial; ``sum_i h_i = 1`` by construction); ``simple`` is the unnormalised ``3 eta_i^2 - 2 eta_i^3`` per phase, whose sum a deck must enforce with the ``switching_penalty`` / ``switching_constraint_*`` kernels.

barrier_height.name: barrier_height
barrier_height.doc: Barrier scale ``W`` multiplying the multi-well ``g(eta) = sum_i eta_i^2 (1 - eta_i)^2 + gamma sum_{i<j} eta_i^2 eta_j^2``.

gamma.name: gamma
gamma.doc: Cross-term coefficient of the multi-well barrier, penalising co-occupation of two phases at a point; ``1.5`` is the Moelans value shared with ``grain_growth_energy``. ``0`` decouples the wells.

epsilon.name: epsilon
epsilon.doc: Regulariser added to ``sum_j eta_j^2`` in the normalised switching denominator so ``h_i`` is finite (zero) where every order parameter vanishes. The switching sum then reads ``1 - epsilon / (epsilon + sum_j eta_j^2)`` — a relative deviation of ``epsilon`` in the bulk of a phase.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Primary field name reported to scalar consumers (defaults to the first entry of ``variables``). The multiphase closure itself always reads every name in ``variables``.

name: neural_conductivity
doc: A random-features MLP, softplus-floored, giving an architecturally positive ``k(T)``.
full_doc:
A random-features MLP, softplus-floored, giving an architecturally positive ``k(T)``.

Args:
    params: Validated parameter dict; see :meth:`params`. ``hidden_units``,
        ``seed`` control the fixed random hidden layer; ``k_floor`` sets the
        positivity floor; ``temperature_scale`` normalises ``T`` before the
        hidden layer (numerical conditioning, not part of the guarantee —
        the guarantee holds for any scale).

seed.name: seed
seed.doc: Random seed for the fixed hidden layer (and the initial output layer).

k_floor.name: k_floor
