k_floor.doc: Positivity floor: k(T) = k_floor + softplus(...) > k_floor for every T. Must be finite and > 0 — a non-finite floor makes every k(T) non-finite, defeating the architectural guarantee.

temperature_scale.name: temperature_scale
temperature_scale.doc: Normalises T before the hidden layer (conditioning only, not the guarantee). Must be finite and > 0.

name: parsed_free_energy
doc: User-supplied free-energy density via a Python expression.
full_doc:
User-supplied free-energy density via a Python expression.

The Phase-12 analog of MOOSE's ``DerivativeParsedMaterial``: the user
writes a single expression in the fields (``eta`` or ``c``), and the
derivatives are obtained by **backend autodiff** — this is *not* a new
symbolic engine. A bare Python identifier is accepted as a coefficient
(e.g. ``"a * x**4 - b * x**2"``) and resolved against ``coefficients``.

Args:
    backend: Active backend (stored for the closure protocol).
    expression: Python expression string in the field.
    variable: The field the expression is in (``x``).
    coefficients: Mapping of coefficient name → value.

expression.name: expression
expression.doc: Python expression string defining the bulk free-energy density as a function of the field ``x``. Bare identifiers are treated as coefficients resolved against ``coefficients`` (e.g. ``"a * x**4 - b * x**2"``). Derivatives are obtained by backend autodiff on PyTorch; restricted arithmetic symbolic derivatives on NumPy.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: The field the expression is written in (``x``, ``eta`` or ``c``).

coefficients.name: coefficients
coefficients.doc: Optional mapping of coefficient name → value used inside the expression.

name: pfd_degradation
doc: Stiffness-degradation material ``g(d)``, quadratic by default.
full_doc:
Stiffness-degradation material ``g(d)``, quadratic by default.

A mechanics kernel that wants to degrade its stress by ``g(d)``
declares a ``degradation`` param pointing at a ``[Materials]`` entry
of kind ``pfd_degradation``. The runner injects the live instance
via :meth:`PFDDegradationMaterial.bind` + :meth:`PFDKernel.bind_degradation`
on the consumer kernel.

The default ``form = quadratic`` is ``g(d) = (1 - d)²`` (Rezwan et al.
2025). A deck can select another built-in form (``cubic``,
``lorentz``) or supply its own ``expression`` in ``d`` — see
:func:`pinnacle.phasefield.degradation.make_degradation`. Every form
must satisfy ``g(0) = 1`` and ``g(1) = 0``; the parsed form is checked
for those endpoints at bind time so a typo is caught before the solve.

form.name: form
form.doc: Degradation function g(d). 'quadratic' (default) is g = (1-d)^2; 'cubic' is the Borden form with a tunable initial slope 's'; 'lorentz' is the rational Wu form with softening parameters 'm' and 'p'; 'parsed' evaluates the user's 'expression'.

regularization.name: regularization
regularization.doc: Small constant added to g(d) so the tangent stiffness stays non-singular at d = 1. 0 reproduces the exact form.

expression.name: expression
expression.doc: Expression for g(d) when form = parsed, arithmetic in 'd' only (e.g. '(1 - d)**2'). Evaluated on the damage tensor so autodiff flows through it. Must satisfy g(0)=1 and g(1)=0; both endpoints are checked before the solve.

derivative_expression.name: derivative_expression
derivative_expression.doc: Optional analytic dg/dd for form = parsed. When omitted the derivative is taken by central finite differences (step 'fd_step'), which is accurate but less exact than an analytic expression.

s.name: s
s.doc: Initial-slope parameter of the 'cubic' form. Smaller values keep the response linear-elastic longer before softening.

m.name: m
m.doc: First softening parameter of the 'lorentz' form.

p.name: p
p.doc: Second softening parameter of the 'lorentz' form.

fd_step.name: fd_step
fd_step.doc: Central-difference step used for dg/dd when form = parsed and no derivative_expression is supplied.

name: pfd_driving_force
doc: History-field holder for the PFD driving force ``H``.
full_doc:
History-field holder for the PFD driving force ``H``.

The material carries a :class:`pinnacle.phasefield.driving_force.HistoryField`
and exposes:

* ``H`` — the current (monotone) history field;
* :meth:`update` — :math:`H \leftarrow \max(H, \psi^+)`, the
  irreversibility max-update the M7 contract preserves exactly;
* :meth:`value` — a backend-agnostic getter used by the
  :class:`PFDKernel` to read ``H`` at solve time.

The :class:`ComposedProblem` builder instantiates a single
:class:`PFDDrivingForceMaterial` per deck. The M7 coupling executioner
feeds the mechanics kernel's positive stored energy to
:meth:`update` between staggered iterations; the M7 standalone PFD
deck feeds a *prescribed* energy field (e.g. a Gaussian / notch
concentration profile) to :meth:`update` at every load step.

Args:
    params: ``initial`` (optional scalar/list to seed ``H``).

initial.name: initial
initial.doc: Initial value of the history field H. H only ever increases (H = max(H, psi+)), which is what makes damage irreversible; a non-zero initial value pre-damages the material.

name: pfd_fracture
doc: Phase-field fracture-energy material (the ``Gc`` / ``l0`` pair + ``A``).
full_doc:
Phase-field fracture-energy material (the ``Gc`` / ``l0`` pair + ``A``).

The :class:`PFDKernel` reads ``self.fracture_residual`` (a
:class:`pinnacle.phasefield.damage_field.DamageFieldResidual`) from
the bound material; the runner builds the residual after binding the
material to the active backend, so the structural tensor is held as a
backend tensor from the start.

Args:
    params: ``Gc`` (J/m²), ``length_scale`` (m), ``anisotropy`` (``"isotropic"``,
        ``"constant"`` with ``anisotropy_tensor`` list, or ``"slip_plane"``),
        ``damage_model`` (``"at2"`` or ``"at1"``), and the
        ``anisotropy_weight`` / ``anisotropy_exponent`` knobs (slip-plane form).

Gc.name: Gc
Gc.doc: Critical fracture energy G_c: the energy per unit crack area.

length_scale.name: length_scale
length_scale.doc: Regularisation length l0 — the width of the diffuse crack band. The mesh must resolve it with several elements, so halving l0 means refining the mesh.

damage_model.name: damage_model
damage_model.doc: AT1 keeps a genuine elastic stage before damage starts; AT2 begins damaging from the first load increment.

anisotropy.name: anisotropy
anisotropy.doc: Structural tensor A weighting the gradient term: 'isotropic' (identity), 'constant' (supply anisotropy_tensor), or 'slip_plane' (built from the crystal frame so cracks follow cleavage planes).

anisotropy_tensor.name: anisotropy_tensor
anisotropy_tensor.doc: Explicit square structural tensor A, used when anisotropy = constant.

anisotropy_weight.name: anisotropy_weight
anisotropy_weight.doc: Strength of the slip-plane anisotropy (0 = isotropic, 1 = maximal).

anisotropy_exponent.name: anisotropy_exponent
anisotropy_exponent.doc: Sharpness of the slip-plane preference in the structural tensor.

name: phase_coupling
doc: Two-way η ↔ c coupling state shared by the hybrid's sub-solvers.
full_doc:
Two-way η ↔ c coupling state shared by the hybrid's sub-solvers.

Args:
    params: Builder-style dict with ``mobility`` (:math:`M_0`), ``alpha``
        (the η-fraction that suppresses the mobility), ``eta_floor`` (the
        positivity clamp), ``chi`` (the driving-force strength) and
        ``c_ref`` (the reference concentration).

mobility.name: mobility
mobility.doc: Base scalar mobility :math:`M_0 > 0` before the eta scaling.

alpha.name: alpha
alpha.doc: Order-parameter fraction that suppresses the mobility: m = max(1 - alpha * eta, eta_floor).

eta_floor.name: eta_floor
eta_floor.doc: Positivity clamp on the scaling, so the transport operator stays invertible for any eta.

chi.name: chi
chi.doc: Driving-force strength of the composition/order-parameter coupling.

c_ref.name: c_ref
c_ref.doc: Reference concentration the driving force measures against.

name: polynomial_free_energy
doc: Quantitative polynomial free energy (fourth-order form).
full_doc:
Quantitative polynomial free energy (fourth-order form).

The Phase-12 analog of MOOSE's ``PolynomialFreeEnergy``: a polynomial bulk
energy whose minima and barrier are mapped from *measurable* quantities
(equilibrium concentrations, barrier) — the quantitative phase-field
machinery. Only the fourth-order form
``f = 16 W [(c - c_a)(c - c_b)]^2 / (c_a - c_b)^4`` is implemented; the
sixth- and eighth-order MOOSE variants are refused at construction rather
than silently evaluated as the fourth-order one.

Args:
    backend: Active backend.
    order: Polynomial order (4, 6 or 8).
    concentrations: Equilibrium concentrations ``(c_a, c_b)``.
    barrier: The barrier height.
    variable: The concentration field (``c``).

order.name: order
order.doc: Polynomial order of the quantitative bulk energy (4, 6 or 8).

concentrations.name: concentrations
concentrations.doc: Equilibrium concentrations ``(c_a, c_b)`` of the two phases; sets the minima.

barrier.name: barrier
barrier.doc: Barrier height of the polynomial bulk energy.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: The concentration field.

name: sum_free_energy
doc: Additive composition of free-energy contributions.
full_doc:
Additive composition of free-energy contributions.

The Phase-12 analog of MOOSE's ``DerivativeSumMaterial``: the total
free-energy density is a sum of named contributions, each of which is itself
a :class:`FreeEnergyClosure` (or a callable). Derivatives are the term-by
-term sums, so no autodiff is needed for the value; the autodiff fallback
is available for callable contributions.

Args:
    contributions: Sequence of ``(name, closure_or_callable)`` pairs.
    variable: The shared field the contributions act on.

contributions.name: contributions
contributions.doc: Contributions to sum. From a ``.i`` deck: a space-separated list of sibling ``[Materials]`` block names (``contributions = 'chem elastic nuc'``), resolved after every block is built. From JSON / Python: a list of ``{name, kind, ...}`` entries constructing each closure inline (``parsed_free_energy``, ``switching_function``, ``barrier_function``, ...).

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: The shared field the contributions act on.

name: switching_function
doc: Grain-growth switching function ``h(η)`` with ``h'`` and ``h''``.
full_doc:
Grain-growth switching function ``h(η)`` with ``h'`` and ``h''``.

Implements the two standard switching functions of the grain-growth
literature:

.. math::
    h(n) = 3n^2 - 2n^3 \quad\text{(SIMPLE)}, \qquad
    h(n) = n^3(6n^2 - 15n + 10) \quad\text{(HIGH)},

both satisfying ``h(0)=0``, ``h(1)=1``, ``h'(0)=h'(1)=0`` — the smooth
interpolation from 0 to 1 that caps the chemical-potential contribution at
the phase boundaries. The derivatives are closed-form (see the module-level
helpers), so no autodiff is required.

variant.name: variant
variant.doc: Which switching function to use: ``simple`` (``3η²−2η³``, the standard SIMPLE form) or ``high`` (``η³(6η²−15η+10)``, the HIGH form with a flatter profile near the end-points).

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: The field the switching function acts on.

name: thermal_conductivity
doc: Temperature-dependent isotropic thermal conductivity `k(T)`.
full_doc:
Temperature-dependent isotropic thermal conductivity `k(T)`.

Args:
    params: Validated parameter dict; see :meth:`params`.

form.name: form
form.doc: Functional form of k(T). 'constant': k = k0. 'linear': k = k0 * (1 + alpha * (T - T_ref)), the MOOSE HeatConductionMaterial temperature-coefficient form. 'table': piecewise-linear interpolation of 'temperature_values' / 'conductivity_values' pairs with flat extrapolation (FEM-only). 'parsed': an arbitrary expression in T (FEM-only; no PINN autodiff route).

temperature_values.name: temperature_values
temperature_values.doc: Strictly increasing tabulated temperatures for form='table' (at least two entries).

k0.name: k0
k0.doc: Reference (or, for 'constant', the only) conductivity value.

reference_temperature.name: reference_temperature
reference_temperature.doc: Reference temperature T_ref the linear form is centred on.

expression.name: expression
expression.doc: Expression in 'T' (plus 'k0', 'alpha', 'T_ref' and NumPy math functions) for kind='parsed', e.g. 'k0 * exp(-alpha * T)'.

name: two_phase_free_energy
doc: Two-phase free-energy model ``F = (1−h) F_a + h F_b + W g``.
full_doc:
Two-phase free-energy model ``F = (1−h) F_a + h F_b + W g``.

The Phase-12 analog of MOOSE's ``DerivativeTwoPhaseMaterial``: two bulk
energies ``F_a`` (liquid) and ``F_b`` (solid) are blended by the switching
function ``h(η)`` and regularised by the barrier ``g(η)`` with strength
``W``. The single-field gradient is

.. math::
    \frac{dF}{d\eta} = (F_b - F_a) h'(\eta) + W g'(\eta),

which reduces to ``F_a`` at ``η=0`` and ``F_b`` at ``η=1``.

Args:
    backend: Active backend.
    free_energy_a: Closure for the ``η=0`` phase.
    free_energy_b: Closure for the ``η=1`` phase.
    switching: The switching function (``"simple"`` or ``"high"``).
    barrier: The barrier (``"simple"``, ``"low"`` or ``"high"``).
    barrier_strength: The interface-strength scalar ``W``.
    variable: The order-parameter field (``"eta"``).

free_energy_a.name: free_energy_a
free_energy_a.doc: Name of the [Materials] entry for the ``eta=0`` phase (``F_a``).

free_energy_b.name: free_energy_b
free_energy_b.doc: Name of the [Materials] entry for the ``eta=1`` phase (``F_b``).

switching.name: switching
switching.doc: Switching-function variant ``h(η)`` interpolating the two phases.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: The order-parameter field.

name: uzr_nd_diffusivity
doc: Three-regime effective diffusivity of Nd (lanthanide proxy).
full_doc:
Three-regime effective diffusivity of Nd (lanthanide proxy).

Lanthanide transport to the cladding is the mechanistic arm of the FCCI
model: unlike the empirical wastage correlation, it produces a *burnup*
threshold, because the pore network must interconnect before the fast
pathways open. Three additive contributions:

* lattice diffusion through the solid skeleton, scaled by ``(1 - phi)``;
* surface diffusion along interconnected pore walls;
* transport through infiltrated liquid sodium, gated on open porosity.

Each term is **independently ablatable** so the sensitivity study can
measure its contribution rather than assert one. Nd stands in for the
lanthanide group; multi-species transport is out of scope.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered component name; must match a ``@registry.register(<category>, <name>)``.

kind.name: kind
kind.doc: Registered material name, injected by the builder.

interconnection_porosity.name: interconnection_porosity
interconnection_porosity.doc: Porosity at which the pore network percolates. Sets the midpoint of the erf blend between slow and fast transport.

transition_width.name: transition_width
transition_width.doc: Width of the percolation transition. Kept finite (and the blend an erf rather than a step) because the PINN residual path differentiates through this closure.

sodium_logged.name: sodium_logged
sodium_logged.doc: Whether liquid sodium has infiltrated the open porosity. Enables the fastest transport term; has no effect below percolation, since infiltration needs a connected path.

include_bulk.name: include_bulk
include_bulk.doc: Include the lattice-diffusion term (sensitivity ablation switch).

include_surface.name: include_surface
include_surface.doc: Include the pore-surface-diffusion term (sensitivity ablation switch).

include_sodium.name: include_sodium
include_sodium.doc: Include the sodium-infiltrated term (sensitivity ablation switch). Distinct from sodium_logged: this switch removes the term from the model, sodium_logged says whether the physical condition holds.

name: uzr_porosity
doc: Porosity and swelling of U--Zr fuel vs. burnup.
full_doc:
Porosity and swelling of U--Zr fuel vs. burnup.

Porosity is the single upstream state variable of the suite: swelling,
conductivity degradation, fission-gas release and sodium infiltration
are all functions of it. Two regimes meet at the pore-interconnection
event near ~2 at.% burnup -- rapid gas-driven growth, then a much slower
approach to saturation once the network vents to the plenum.

The arrest at interconnection is the mechanism that makes the fuel form
viable at all, which is why the tests assert the *ratio* of the two rates
rather than either rate on its own.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered component name; must match a ``@registry.register(<category>, <name>)``.

kind.name: kind
kind.doc: Registered material name, injected by the builder.

interconnection_burnup.name: interconnection_burnup
interconnection_burnup.doc: Burnup at which the porosity network interconnects and vents to the plenum. Literature places this at 1-2 at.%; the value is a deck parameter because the severity answer is sensitive to it.

swelling_at_interconnection.name: swelling_at_interconnection
swelling_at_interconnection.doc: Volumetric swelling dV/V reached at interconnection. NOTE: this is dV/V, not porosity -- 0.30 dV/V is a porosity of 0.231. The design-basis smear density (~75 %) is chosen to accommodate this much swelling before fuel-cladding contact.

post_transition_rate.name: post_transition_rate
post_transition_rate.doc: Volumetric swelling rate after interconnection. Much smaller than the pre-transition rate because released gas no longer drives bubble growth.

saturation_swelling.name: saturation_swelling
saturation_swelling.doc: Upper bound on volumetric swelling; growth clamps here.

anisotropy_factor.name: anisotropy_factor
anisotropy_factor.doc: Scales the isotropic linear strain derived from volumetric swelling. 1.0 is isotropic; metallic fuel swelling is not, so a directional study sets this per direction.

name: uzr_thermal
doc: Thermal conductivity of porous U--Zr fuel.
full_doc:
Thermal conductivity of porous U--Zr fuel.

Dense conductivity is linear in temperature and reduced by the Zr
fraction (Zr additions lower k); porosity is applied as a
Maxwell--Eucken correction. The composition dependence and the porosity
correction are kept separate because they have different status: the
former is a fit, the latter is a two-phase mixing bound.

This material is the thermal half of the feedback loop that makes the
suite worth running: swelling raises porosity, porosity degrades k, the
fuel and cladding run hotter, and wastage is exponential in temperature.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered component name; must match a ``@registry.register(<category>, <name>)``.

kind.name: kind
kind.doc: Registered material name, injected by the builder.

k_dense_ref.name: k_dense_ref
k_dense_ref.doc: Dense-fuel thermal conductivity at the reference temperature for the reference Zr fraction. Representative of U-10Zr.

dk_dT.name: dk_dT
dk_dT.doc: Temperature slope of the dense conductivity. Positive: metallic fuel conductivity rises with temperature, unlike oxide fuel, which is the reason metallic fuel runs with a far flatter radial temperature profile.

dk_dzr.name: dk_dzr
dk_dzr.units: W/(m*K) per unit Zr weight fraction
dk_dzr.doc: Sensitivity of dense conductivity to Zr weight fraction, relative to zr_ref. Negative: Zr additions degrade conductivity.

temperature_ref.name: temperature_ref
temperature_ref.doc: Reference temperature at which k_dense_ref is stated.

zr_ref.name: zr_ref
zr_ref.doc: Reference Zr weight fraction for k_dense_ref (0.10 = U-10Zr).

shape_factor.name: shape_factor
shape_factor.doc: Maxwell-Eucken pore shape factor. 1.5 is the spherical-pore value; larger values model flatter, more obstructive pores and degrade conductivity faster with porosity.

name: annulus_mesh
doc: Generate a structured hexahedral mesh of a cylindrical shell (annulus).
full_doc:
Generate a structured hexahedral mesh of a cylindrical shell (annulus).

Nodes are placed in cylindrical coordinates and the theta seam is merged so the
resulting mesh has exactly the circular inner/outer walls and top/bottom caps
as its boundary.

Args:
    origin: Center of the bottom face ``(x, y, z)``.
    inner_radius: Inner radius.
    outer_radius: Outer radius.
    height: Shell height.
    divisions: ``(nr, nθ, nz)`` element counts.
    primitive: Optional :class:`Annulus` primitive to derive geometry.
    grading: Optional grading spec with ``feature``/``ratio``.

Returns:
    A 3-D :class:`Mesh` with node/side sets ``inner``, ``outer``, ``bottom``,
    ``top``.

divisions.name: divisions
divisions.doc: Elements in the (radial, circumferential, axial) directions.

grading.name: grading
grading.doc: Optional graded-refinement spec: {'feature': <named feature or coordinate>, 'ratio': <largest/smallest element size>, 'axes': <list of axes>}. Omit for a uniform mesh.

name: bicrystal_2d
doc: Generate a structured 2-D bicrystal mesh with a vertical grain boundary.
full_doc:
Generate a structured 2-D bicrystal mesh with a vertical grain boundary.

The mesh is a regular rectangle split by a vertical interface.  Elements
touching the interface are tagged in side set ``gb`` and their nodes are
tagged in node set ``gb``.  The interface is placed at the horizontal midpoint
unless ``interface_x`` is supplied.

Args:
    bounds: ``((xmin, xmax), (ymin, ymax))``.  Either ``bounds`` or
        ``primitive`` must be provided.
    divisions: ``(nx, ny)`` element counts.  ``nx`` must be even when the
        default midpoint interface is used.
    primitive: Optional :class:`Rectangle` primitive to derive ``bounds``.
    interface_x: Physical x-coordinate of the vertical interface.  Defaults
        to the horizontal midpoint.
    grading: Optional grading spec with ``feature`` and ``ratio``.

Returns:
    A 2-D :class:`Mesh` with ``xmin``/``xmax``/``ymin``/``ymax`` and ``gb``
    side sets.

bounds.name: bounds
bounds.doc: Domain bounds as a list of two (min, max) tuples. In a deck this is usually written as the flat 'domain' key instead.

divisions.name: divisions
divisions.doc: Number of elements along each axis (nx, ny).

interface_x.name: interface_x
interface_x.doc: x-coordinate of the vertical grain boundary. Defaults to the domain mid-plane when 0. Elements are tagged 'elem_grain' = 0 left of the interface and 1 to its right, so per-grain components work on this mesh.

grading.name: grading
grading.doc: Optional graded-refinement spec: {'feature': <named feature or coordinate>, 'ratio': <largest/smallest element size>, 'axes': <list of axes>}. Omit for a uniform mesh.

name: box_mesh
doc: Generate a structured hexahedral / quad / line box mesh.
full_doc:
Generate a structured hexahedral / quad / line box mesh.

The dimensionality is inferred from the lengths of ``bounds`` and
``divisions`` (both must agree: 1 for 1-D, 2 for 2-D, 3 for 3-D).
A 1-D ``box_mesh`` is a line mesh, a 2-D ``box_mesh`` is a quad
mesh, a 3-D ``box_mesh`` is a hex mesh — the same component, just
parametric in the active dimension.

Args:
    bounds: ``((xmin, xmax), (ymin, ymax), (zmin, zmax))`` for 3-D;
        ``((xmin, xmax), (ymin, ymax))`` for 2-D;
        ``((xmin, xmax),)`` for 1-D.
    divisions: Number of elements along each axis.

Returns:
    A :class:`Mesh` with node sets for each face and the full boundary, plus
    side sets for each exterior face.

bounds.name: bounds
bounds.doc: Domain bounds as a list of three (min, max) tuples — ((xmin, xmax), (ymin, ymax), (zmin, zmax)).

divisions.name: divisions

name: box_with_void
doc: Generate a box mesh with a spherical void removed.
full_doc:
Generate a box mesh with a spherical void removed.

Elements whose centroid falls inside the void are removed. The remaining
nodes are renumbered and the mesh carries a ``void_boundary`` node set and
side set.

Args:
    bounds: Box extents ``((xmin, xmax), (ymin, ymax), (zmin, zmax))``.
    divisions: Number of elements along each axis.
    void: :class:`SphericalVoid` instance. Defaults to a centered sphere of
        radius ``0.2``.

Returns:
    A :class:`Mesh` with the void represented by removed elements and the
    void boundary captured in node/side sets.

bounds.name: bounds
bounds.doc: Domain bounds as a list of three (min, max) tuples. In a deck this is usually written as the flat 'domain' key instead.

divisions.name: divisions
divisions.doc: Number of hexahedral elements along each axis (nx, ny, nz).

void.name: void
void.doc: Embedded void to remove: {'shape': 'sphere'|'cylinder', 'center': [cx, cy, cz], 'radius': r, 'height': h}. In a .i deck this is written compactly as void = 'sphere cx cy cz r'. Elements whose centroid falls inside the void are dropped and the exposed surface becomes the 'void_boundary' side set.

name: cylinder_mesh
doc: Generate a structured hexahedral mesh of a solid cylinder.
full_doc:
Generate a structured hexahedral mesh of a solid cylinder.

The cross-section is meshed with the Shirley–Chiu concentric square-to-disk
mapping so the boundary is exactly the cylinder surface and the area
converges to ``π r²`` as the mesh is refined.

Args:
    origin: Center of the bottom face ``(x, y, z)``.
    radius: Cylinder radius.
    height: Cylinder height.
    divisions: ``(nr, nθ, nz)`` element counts in the radial, angular, and
        axial directions.  ``nr`` counts layers in the square-parameter radius
        and ``nθ`` counts angular sectors.
    primitive: Optional :class:`Cylinder` primitive to derive geometry.
    grading: Optional grading spec.  ``feature`` may be ``"side_wall"``,
        ``"center"`` (or a coordinate vector) and ``ratio`` controls radial
        element-size growth.

Returns:
    A 3-D :class:`Mesh` with node/side sets ``bottom``, ``top``, ``side``.

divisions.name: divisions
divisions.doc: Elements in the (radial, circumferential, axial) directions. The circumferential count sets how well the curved surface is resolved.

grading.name: grading
grading.doc: Optional graded-refinement spec: {'feature': <named feature or coordinate>, 'ratio': <largest/smallest element size>, 'axes': <list of axes>}. Omit for a uniform mesh.

name: layered_line_mesh
doc: Generate two abutting 1-D blocks sharing a physical point but not a DOF.
full_doc:
Generate two abutting 1-D blocks sharing a physical point but not a DOF.

Args:
    bounds: ``(x0, xi, x1)`` — left end, interface location, right end.
        A flat triple rather than nested per-block pairs: the ``.i``
        lexer flattens bracket nesting into stray-bracket string tokens
        (space-separated vectors are its only nested-list primitive), so
        every mesh generator in this package that takes a domain uses a
        flat convention (cf. ``box_mesh``'s flat ``domain``); a nested
        ``[[x0, xi], [xi, x1]]`` form would silently fail to parse from
        a deck. The two blocks share the interface point by
        construction, so there is nothing to cross-check.
    divisions: ``(n_left, n_right)`` element counts.

Returns:
    A 1-D :class:`Mesh` with:

    * node sets ``xmin``, ``xmax``, ``interface_primary`` (the left
      block's rightmost node), ``interface_secondary`` (the right
      block's leftmost node, at the same coordinate);
    * element sets ``left``, ``right``.

bounds.doc: [x0, xi, x1]: left end, interface location, right end. Flat triple (not nested per-block pairs) so it parses from a '.i' deck; the two blocks meet at 'xi' by construction.

Generate a structured 2-D quadrilateral mesh.

name: voronoi
doc: Registered ``("mesh", "voronoi")`` factory.
full_doc:
Registered ``("mesh", "voronoi")`` factory.

Args:
    n_grains: Number of Voronoi grains (seed points).
    domain_size: Domain size. A scalar applies to all axes; a list
        gives ``[Lx, Ly]`` in 2-D or ``[Lx, Ly, Lz]`` in 3-D. The
        domain spans ``[0, size]^dim``.
    dim: Spatial dimension (2 or 3). Default: 2.
    periodic: If True, periodic boundary conditions across domain
        faces. Default: ``False``.
    seed: RNG seed for reproducible seed-point generation. Default:
        ``None`` (non-deterministic).
    element_type: Element topology. 2-D: ``"tri3"`` or ``"quad4"``.
        3-D: ``"tet4"`` or ``"hex8"``. ``"auto"`` picks the simplex
        topology (tri3 / tet4). Default: ``"auto"``.
    divisions: Optional override for the per-axis element count.
        ``None`` lets the function derive it from ``n_grains``;
        pass an integer (1-D) or tuple (multi-D) to force a
        specific mesh density. Default: ``None``.

Returns:
    A :class:`~pinnacle.mesh.mesh.Mesh` with per-grain element
    tags in ``element_sets["grain_<i>"]`` and GB side sets in
    ``side_sets["gb_<i>_<j>"]`` plus an aggregate ``"gb"`` set.

Raises:
    PinnacleError: If ``n_grains < 1``, ``dim`` is not 2 or 3, or
        the element type is unknown.

domain_size.name: domain_size
domain_size.doc: Domain size. A scalar applies to all axes; a list gives [Lx, Ly] in 2-D or [Lx, Ly, Lz] in 3-D.

periodic.name: periodic

seed.name: seed

divisions.name: divisions

Mechanistic + data-driven correction network.

    device: Optional device override.

hidden_layers.name: hidden_layers
hidden_layers.doc: Number of hidden layers in the correction pathway.

neurons.name: neurons
neurons.doc: Width of each correction hidden layer.

final_activation.name: final_activation
final_activation.doc: Optional activation on the output layer. Empty means linear output.

name: mlp
doc: Configurable fully-connected network.
full_doc:
Configurable fully-connected network.

Args:
    backend: Active numerical backend.
    input_dim: Number of input features.
    output_dim: Number of output features.
    hidden_dims: Sequence of hidden-layer widths.
    activation: Hidden activation (``'tanh'``, ``'softplus'``, ``'relu'``).
    final_activation: Optional output activation.
    weight_init: Initialization scheme; currently ``'xavier'`` normal.
    dtype: Optional precision override.
    device: Optional device override.

hidden_layers.name: hidden_layers
hidden_layers.doc: Number of hidden layers. Depth buys expressiveness at training cost.

activation.name: activation
activation.doc: Hidden activation. 'tanh' is the default for PINNs because it is smooth enough for second derivatives; 'relu' is not.

final_activation.name: final_activation
final_activation.doc: Optional activation on the output layer. Empty means linear output.

name: allen_cahn
doc: Allen–Cahn residual for a non-conserved order parameter.
full_doc:
Allen–Cahn residual for a non-conserved order parameter.

PDE:

.. math::
    \frac{\partial \eta}{\partial t}
    = -L \left( \frac{\partial f}{\partial \eta}
                 - \kappa \nabla^2 \eta \right)

where ``L`` is the mobility and ``\kappa`` is the gradient-energy
coefficient.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered residual name (matches ``@register('phasefield_model', <type>)``).

spatial_dim.name: spatial_dim
spatial_dim.doc: Spatial dimension of the PDE (1, 2 or 3).

name: anisotropic_interface
doc: Allen–Cahn equation with an orientation-dependent gradient coefficient.
full_doc:
Allen–Cahn equation with an orientation-dependent gradient coefficient.

This mirrors the MOOSE ``anisotropic_interfaces`` example.  The interface
energy depends on the local normal direction through

.. math::
    \kappa(\theta) = \kappa_0 \bigl(1 + \varepsilon
        \cos(m(\theta - \theta_0))\bigr)

where :math:`\theta = \arctan2(\partial_y \eta, \partial_x \eta)`
is the interface normal angle.  The PDE is

.. math::
    \frac{\partial \eta}{\partial t}
    = -L \left(
        \frac{\partial f}{\partial \eta}
        - \nabla \cdot \bigl(\kappa(\theta) \nabla \eta\bigr)
    \right)

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered residual name (matches ``@register('phasefield_model', <type>)``).

spatial_dim.name: spatial_dim
spatial_dim.doc: Spatial dimension of the PDE (1, 2 or 3).

name: cahn_hilliard
doc: Cahn–Hilliard residual for a conserved concentration.
full_doc:
Cahn–Hilliard residual for a conserved concentration.

PDE:

.. math::
    \frac{\partial c}{\partial t} = \nabla \cdot (M \nabla \mu),
    \quad \mu = \frac{\partial f}{\partial c} - \kappa \nabla^2 c

The network predicts both ``c`` and ``\mu`` (a mixed formulation), which
avoids computing fourth-order derivatives directly.

type.name: type
type.doc: Registered residual name (matches ``@register('phasefield_model', <type>)``).

spatial_dim.name: spatial_dim
spatial_dim.doc: Spatial dimension of the PDE (1, 2 or 3).

name: anisotropic_pfd
doc: Anisotropic phase-field damage model (Rezwan et al. 2025).
full_doc:
Anisotropic phase-field damage model (Rezwan et al. 2025).

The model degrades tensile stored energy via ``g(d) = (1 - d)²``,
regularizes cracks over a length scale ``l0``, and can use a structural
tensor to bias the crack resistance toward crystallographic planes.
Irreversibility is enforced through a history field ``H``.

Args:
    backend: Active numerical backend.
    config: Validated run config containing a ``phasefielddamage`` section.
        Optional ``crystal`` section is accepted but not yet consumed
        (crystallographic anisotropy wiring is Phase 08).

Raises:
    PinnacleError: If the ``phasefielddamage`` section is missing or uses an
        unsupported degradation/anisotropy type.

length_scale.name: length_scale
length_scale.doc: Regularisation length l0: the width of the diffuse crack band. The mesh must resolve it with several elements.

damage_model.name: damage_model
damage_model.doc: AT1 has a genuine elastic stage before damage starts; AT2 begins damaging immediately.

anisotropy.name: anisotropy
anisotropy.doc: Structural tensor A weighting the gradient term: 'isotropic' (identity), 'constant' (supply anisotropy_tensor), or 'slip_plane' (built from the crystal frame, so cracks prefer cleavage planes).

anisotropy_tensor.name: anisotropy_tensor
anisotropy_tensor.doc: Explicit square structural tensor A, used when anisotropy = constant.

anisotropy_weight.name: anisotropy_weight
anisotropy_weight.doc: Strength of the slip-plane anisotropy (0 = isotropic, 1 = maximal).

anisotropy_exponent.name: anisotropy_exponent
anisotropy_exponent.doc: Sharpness of the slip-plane preference in the structural tensor.

name: area
doc: Measure of a boundary (MOOSE ``AreaPostprocessor``).
full_doc:
Measure of a boundary (MOOSE ``AreaPostprocessor``).

Reports the ``dimension - 1`` measure of a side set: polygon area in
3-D, edge length in 2-D, and the boundary-point count in 1-D.

side_set.name: side_set
side_set.doc: Name of the boundary (side set) whose measure is reported.

name: average_element_size
doc: Average element size (MOOSE ``AverageElementSize``).
full_doc:
Average element size (MOOSE ``AverageElementSize``).

The size of an element is its measure taken to the power ``1/dim``, so
the result is a length in every dimension.

name: average_nodal_value
doc: Unweighted mean of a nodal field (MOOSE ``AverageNodalVariableValue``).
full_doc: Unweighted mean of a nodal field (MOOSE ``AverageNodalVariableValue``).

field.name: field
field.doc: Name of the solve-result array to reduce (e.g. 'displacement', 'field', 'damage', 'stress', 'strain').

component.name: component
component.doc: Component of a vector or tensor field, as a list: '[0]' picks the x-component of a vector, '[0, 0]' the xx-component of a tensor. Omit for scalar fields.

name: avg_contact_angle
doc: Measured contact angle of a phase field against a wall side set.
full_doc:
Measured contact angle of a phase field against a wall side set.

On every face of the wall the gradient of the nodal field is evaluated at
the face centre with the parent element's shape functions (the P1/Q1
gradient the weak form integrates, sampled on the wall), giving the
interface normal :math:`\mathbf m = \nabla\phi/|\nabla\phi|` and
:math:`\cos\theta = \mathbf m\cdot\mathbf n` against the outward face
normal. Faces whose centre value satisfies :math:`|\phi| < ` ``band`` —
the diffuse-interface band, where the gradient direction is meaningful —
are averaged with weight :math:`|\nabla\phi|\,|\Gamma_f|`; the wells
contribute nothing. The value is the weighted mean angle in degrees
(``value_type = degrees``) or the weighted mean cosine
(``value_type = cosine``).

Reads the nodal field ``field_<variable>`` of the solve result (the key
``pf_fem_transient`` publishes per variable), falling back to the bare
variable name and then to ``field``.

variable.name: variable
variable.doc: Phase-field variable (values in [-1, 1]) whose wall angle is measured; read from the solve result as ``field_<variable>``.

side_set.name: side_set
side_set.doc: Wall side set the angle is measured against (outward normal of its faces).

band.name: band
band.doc: Half-width of the diffuse-interface band: only wall faces with |phi| < band at the face centre vote, so the wells (whose gradient direction is numerical noise) are excluded. In (0, 1].

value_type.name: value_type
value_type.doc: ``degrees`` reports the |grad phi|-weighted mean angle in degrees; ``cosine`` the weighted mean of cos(theta) = m . n.

doc: Report ``Bi = h L / k_ref`` for a convective boundary (Phase 41 / HT-3).
full_doc:
Report ``Bi = h L / k_ref`` for a convective boundary (Phase 41 / HT-3).

A pure diagnostic — the values are deck-declared physical parameters,
not read from the solve result — so ``Bi`` lands in ``summary.json``
for any deck with a convective boundary, per the Phase 41 acceptance
criterion.

reciprocity residual as the postprocessor's scalar value; the row sums
themselves are logged (INFO) so both identities are *reported*, and a
row-sum deviation beyond ``row_sum_tolerance`` raises.

doc: Discrete conservation check reported by ``scalar_steady``.
full_doc:
Discrete conservation check reported by ``scalar_steady``.

Reports one field of the ``energy_balance`` dict the executioner
attaches to its result: ``boundary_reaction``, ``volumetric_load``,
``absolute_imbalance``, or (the default) ``relative_imbalance`` — the
imbalance normalised by the total applied load, which is what the
Phase 39 acceptance test (``< 1e-10`` on the existing steady slab)
checks against.

quantity.name: quantity
quantity.doc: Which field of the executioner's 'energy_balance' diagnostic to report. 'relative_imbalance' (default) is the imbalance normalised by the total applied load.

name: feature_volume_fraction
doc: Volume fraction of a phase, optionally as the Avrami transform.
full_doc:
Volume fraction of a phase, optionally as the Avrami transform.

Reports the volume fraction of the region where ``field`` exceeds the
``threshold`` (``⟨H(q - threshold)⟩``), using a logistic relaxation of the
Heaviside so the fraction is continuous under tiny field drift:

.. math::

    V_f = \frac{1}{|\Omega|}\int \frac{1}{1 + e^{-\beta (q - q^*)}}\, d\Omega

with ``β`` the sharpness ``beta`` (large → a step function) and ``q*`` the
``threshold``. With ``value_type = avrami`` the MOOSE
``FeatureVolumeFraction`` transform is reported instead,

.. math::

    Y = \ln\bigl[-\ln(1 - V_f / V_{eq})\bigr],

whose slope against ``ln t`` is the Avrami exponent of a transformation
kinetics fit; ``equil_fraction`` is :math:`V_{eq}`.

field.name: field
field.doc: Name of the order-parameter / phase field to threshold.

threshold.name: threshold
threshold.doc: Value below which a point is counted as not-in-feature.

beta.name: beta
beta.doc: Logistic sharpness of the threshold: large β makes it a step function.

component.name: component
component.doc: Index of the order parameter to threshold when ``field`` has more than one component. Omitted, a multi-component field is reduced with the MAXIMUM over components — the 'covered by any grain' reading a grain-covered fraction wants.

value_type.name: value_type
value_type.doc: ``volume_fraction`` reports V_f; ``avrami`` reports the transform ln[-ln(1 - V_f / equil_fraction)] (MOOSE FeatureVolumeFraction).

equil_fraction.name: equil_fraction
equil_fraction.doc: Equilibrium volume fraction V_eq normalising the Avrami transform.

name: fin_efficiency
doc: ``eta = Q_actual / Q_ideal`` for a convecting fin.
full_doc:
``eta = Q_actual / Q_ideal`` for a convecting fin.

``Q_actual`` sums the consistent nodal reaction over ``base_node_set``
(the same quantity ``side_heat_rate`` reports); ``Q_ideal = h * P * L *
(T_base - T_inf)`` is the heat an ideal (isothermal, no internal
temperature drop) fin of the same geometry would remove. ``T_base`` is
the mean nodal temperature over ``base_node_set``.

base_node_set.name: base_node_set
base_node_set.doc: Node set at the fin base (the actual heat rate is summed here).

fin_area_fraction.name: fin_area_fraction
fin_area_fraction.doc: Optional A_f / A_t, the finned fraction of the total exposed surface — an area ratio, so it must lie within [0, 1]. 0 (the default) reports the single-fin efficiency eta_f; > 0 reports the overall surface efficiency eta_t = 1 - (1 - eta_f) * A_f / A_t instead.

name: grain_boundary_area
doc: Grain-boundary area ``∫ Σᵢ |∇ηᵢ| dΩ / (g Δη)`` (MOOSE ``GrainBoundaryArea``).
full_doc:
Grain-boundary area ``∫ Σᵢ |∇ηᵢ| dΩ / (g Δη)`` (MOOSE ``GrainBoundaryArea``).

Integrates the total interface length/volume ``Σᵢ |∇ηᵢ|`` and normalises by
``g · Δη``, where ``g`` is the number of order parameters that **change**
across a boundary and ``Δη`` their value span.

``g`` is a property of the representation, not of the colouring budget.
Across a boundary between two grains exactly two fields vary — the one
falling and the one rising — so the co-area integral collects
``2 Δη`` per unit boundary area *however many* order parameters the deck
declares; the unused colours are identically zero and contribute nothing to
the numerator. Dividing by the colour count would therefore make the
reported area shrink as ``2 / nₛ`` (a six-colour polycrystal under-reporting
a unit interface as ``1/3``), which is why the parameter is
``grains_per_side`` — MOOSE's name for the same factor — and defaults to 2.

The audit's acceptance criterion is exact here: a single straight interface
spanning a box of side ``L`` reports area ``L`` (in 2-D) or ``L²`` (in
3-D) up to the discretisation error of the piecewise-linear gradient
reconstruction, which this postprocessor reproduces exactly for the
standard linear element.

fields.name: fields
fields.doc: Names of the order-parameter fields whose interface is counted.

grains_per_side.name: grains_per_side
grains_per_side.doc: Number of order parameters that CHANGE across a boundary — two for the usual polycrystal (the grain on each side), which is the default and MOOSE's ``GrainBoundaryArea`` convention. This is a property of the representation, NOT the colour budget: set it to the total number of order parameters and a unit interface in a six-colour deck would be reported as 1/3 of its length. Use 1 only where a single field carries the whole interface.

delta_eta.name: delta_eta
delta_eta.doc: Value span of each order parameter (Δη = 1 for a 0/1 order parameter).

name: homogenized_conductivity
doc: Report the homogenized conductivity computed from its own layer parameters.
full_doc:
Report the homogenized conductivity computed from its own layer parameters.

Independent of any live FEM state (mirrors ``interface_flux_conservation``
/ ``enclosure_view_factors``'s "recompute from its own params" design):
this is a REPORTING postprocessor for a config-time-constant quantity,
not a reduction over a solved field.

layer_conductivities.doc: Per-layer conductivity, one per layer (>= 2 layers).

layer_fractions.name: layer_fractions
layer_fractions.doc: Per-layer volume fraction, same order, positive and summing to 1.

direction.name: direction

name: interface_flux_conservation
doc: Report the worst mismatch between the two sides' *independently computed* fluxes.
full_doc:
Report the worst mismatch between the two sides' *independently computed* fluxes.

Separate from the constitutive relation itself (which the operator
assembly enforces exactly): this checks that whatever the trained/solved
field is, energy is not created or destroyed crossing the interface. The
check is genuinely independent of the BC — each side's conductive flux
``q = -k dT/dx`` is reconstructed from the solved field by a one-sided
difference into that side's own bulk (using the per-side conductivities
declared here, mirroring the deck's ``[Kernels]``), and the report is
``max(|q_primary_side - q_secondary_side|)``. An earlier revision derived
both fluxes from the same ``H (T+ - T-)`` expression, which is zero for
*any* field by algebra and can never detect a leak; this version reads
nonzero the moment the field stops carrying the same flux into and out
of the interface.

1-D only (the only non-conforming interface mesh in the tree is
``layered_line_mesh``): the one-sided difference is exact for the
piecewise-linear fields a source-free layered slab produces, and O(h)
otherwise. The parameters mirror the deck rather than reaching into the
live BC object — a postprocessor stays a pure reduction over
mesh + result per ``system/postprocessor.py``.

conductivity_primary.name: conductivity_primary
conductivity_primary.doc: Bulk conductivity of the block owning the '+' side, for the one-sided flux. Finite and > 0 — a non-finite value makes the reduction report perfect conservation.

conductivity_secondary.name: conductivity_secondary
conductivity_secondary.doc: Bulk conductivity of the block owning the '-' side, for the one-sided flux. Finite and > 0 — a non-finite value makes the reduction report perfect conservation.

name: macro_stress
doc: Registered ``("postprocessor", "macro_stress")`` component.
full_doc:
Registered ``("postprocessor", "macro_stress")`` component.

Computes the volume-weighted macro stress by averaging QP-level
Cauchy stresses per element (over the element's QPs) and then
averaging over the whole domain. Returns a ``(3, 3)`` tensor with
the absent spatial dimensions zero (a 2-D mesh yields a 2x2 stress
embedded in 3x3).

name: mass_conservation
doc: Relative drift of the conserved ``∫ c dΩ`` against the initial integral.
full_doc:
Relative drift of the conserved ``∫ c dΩ`` against the initial integral.

The split Cahn–Hilliard system conserves the total concentration ``∫ c dΩ``
exactly (up to the round-off of the implicit solve) under no-flux BCs. This
postprocessor reports ``(I - I₀) / |I₀|`` where ``I`` is the current
integral and ``I₀`` the value recorded at the first step; it is the
audit's "mass conservation" acceptance criterion.

The initial integral is provided by the executioner as the ``mass0``
solve-result (``fem_transient`` / ``pf_fem_transient`` record it on the
first step); absent that, the postprocessor falls back to reporting the
instantaneous integral (still a valid, if un-normalised, monitor).

mode.doc: ``relative`` (default): drift divided by |I0|, or by the absolute inventory ∫|c| when I0 is (near) zero so a zero-mean field stays well defined; ``absolute``: the drift ``I - I0`` in the field's units.

name: total_free_energy
doc: Total free energy ``∫ (f(q) + Σᵢ κᵢ/2 |∇qᵢ|²) dΩ`` (MOOSE ``FreeEnergy``.
full_doc:
Total free energy ``∫ (f(q) + Σᵢ κᵢ/2 |∇qᵢ|²) dΩ`` (MOOSE ``FreeEnergy``.

Integrates the bulk free-energy density ``f`` plus the gradient energy of
every order-parameter / concentration field named in ``gradient_fields``,
each weighted by its gradient coefficient ``κ``. The bulk term is read from
a per-element field named by ``energy_density`` when present (an
executioner that already assembled it), otherwise the double-well density
of the named bulk field is evaluated on the same per-element values.

This is the audit's "energy monotonicity" acceptance criterion on a
solver-independent surface: both the FEM and the PINN executioners emit a
value with this exact block, so a rollout that *grows* the total energy
past a previous step is immediately visible.

bulk_field.name: bulk_field
bulk_field.doc: Name of the bulk field whose double-well energy is the chemical term.

free_energy.name: free_energy
free_energy.doc: Name of the [Materials] free-energy closure whose density is integrated over ``bulk_field`` (``double_well``, ``parsed_free_energy``, ``polynomial_free_energy``, ...). Empty falls back to the unit double well with minima (0, 1), which is only correct for decks built on that convention.

energy_density.name: energy_density
energy_density.doc: Optional pre-assembled per-element bulk free-energy density field in the solve result; when named and present it takes precedence over ``bulk_field``.

gradient_fields.name: gradient_fields
gradient_fields.doc: Order-parameter / concentration fields carrying a gradient energy, each weighted by its gradient coefficient. Write one sub-block per entry with 'field' (the solve-result name) and 'kappa'; a bare name (or space-separated list of names) is accepted as shorthand for kappa = 1. A multi-component field contributes every component.

name: uzr_cdf_severity
doc: Creep-rupture cumulative damage fraction against a CDF limit.
full_doc:
Creep-rupture cumulative damage fraction against a CDF limit.

Demand is the Larson--Miller CDF accumulated over ``exposure_s`` at the
reduced field temperature, under the thin-wall hoop stress on the
*wastage-thinned* wall; capacity is ``cdf_limit``. Ignoring the wastage
thinning is the usual way this number comes out optimistic, so the
thinning is applied here rather than left to the deck.

``alloy`` selects **two** coefficient sets, not one
------------------------------------------------------

It picks the wastage coefficients that thin the wall *and* the
Larson--Miller coefficients that turn the resulting stress into a life.
The second half was previously not wired: the rupture call took the
module-level defaults, which are the HT9 row, so a deck writing
``alloy = d9`` thinned the wall on D9 kinetics and then consumed that
wall on **HT9 creep life** -- a number that looks entirely plausible and
is not the alloy the deck named.

The austenitic rows carry ``NOT_AVAILABLE`` for every Larson--Miller
field, so the honest behaviour there is to refuse rather than borrow.
Unstated coefficients are therefore re-resolved through
:meth:`~.materialsystems.CladAlloy.require`, exactly as
``clad_properties`` re-resolves the void-swelling pair: HT9 resolves to
the same numbers it always did, and D9/SS316 raise a message naming the
alloy, the field and its recorded provenance. A deck that has qualified
coefficients states them and they win.

field.name: field
field.doc: Solve array holding cladding temperature in K, reduced with 'reduction' (default 'max'). Give this OR 'temperature', not both.

temperature.name: temperature
temperature.doc: Cladding temperature in K, stated directly instead of reduced from a solve array. Give this OR 'field', not both.

component.name: component
component.doc: Component of a vector or tensor field, as a list ('[0]', '[0, 0]'). Omit for scalar fields.

reduction.name: reduction
reduction.doc: How to reduce the field to the value that governs severity. 'max' (default) is the hot spot that sets the limit; 'mean' is a diagnostic and will under-report a peaked profile.

exposure_s.name: exposure_s
exposure_s.doc: Time at temperature and stress, in seconds. Required with no default so validation rejects an omitted exposure by name. Cross-checked against the solve's end time when it reports one.

wall_thickness.name: wall_thickness
wall_thickness.doc: As-built cladding wall thickness in m. Required unless 'stress_from' is set -- it sets both the ligament and the hoop stress, and there is no default. Must NOT be given alongside 'stress_from': the upstream stage carries it.

radius.name: radius
radius.doc: Cladding mid-wall radius in m, for the thin-wall hoop stress. Required unless 'stress_from' is set -- it is the moment arm. Must NOT be given alongside 'stress_from'.

internal_pressure.name: internal_pressure
internal_pressure.doc: Internal (plenum) pressure in Pa. Required unless 'stress_from' is set. Compute it from gas inventory with the 'plenum_pressure' correlation if the deck does not carry it directly. Must NOT be given alongside 'stress_from'.

cdf_limit.name: cdf_limit
cdf_limit.doc: Allowable cumulative damage fraction. Required -- no default, because the allowable CDF is a design decision.

stress_from.name: stress_from
stress_from.doc: Name of a 'uzr_hoop_stress' block whose value is the hoop stress in Pa on the thinned wall. Unset (the default) rebuilds wastage and stress in this block from the same correlations, which is the single-block form. Set it to compose the four stages instead, so the intermediate wastage, ligament and stress are reported and each stage is independently substitutable.

lmp_a.name: lmp_a
lmp_a.doc: Larson-Miller intercept A in LMP = A + B log10(sigma/sigma_ref). Unstated (the default) resolves it from the SELECTED alloy's row -- 31.52 for HT9; alloys whose sources carry no rupture anchors (D9, SS316) raise rather than borrow HT9's. FITTED, not a qualified correlation -- state your own for any life claim.

lmp_b.name: lmp_b
lmp_b.doc: Larson-Miller stress slope B; negative, so higher stress shortens life. Alloy-resolved on the same terms as lmp_a.

lmp_constant.name: lmp_constant
lmp_constant.doc: Larson-Miller constant C in log10(t_r[h]) = 1000*LMP/T - C. Alloy-resolved on the same terms as lmp_a.

reference_stress.name: reference_stress
reference_stress.doc: Stress normalisation sigma_ref inside the LMP log term. Alloy-resolved on the same terms as lmp_a.

alloy.name: alloy
alloy.doc: Cladding alloy. Selects BOTH the wastage coefficients that thin the wall and the Larson-Miller coefficients that turn the resulting stress into a rupture life; see the class docstring for why the second half must not silently fall back to HT9.

fast_flux.name: fast_flux
fast_flux.doc: Fast neutron flux in n/m^2/s for the irradiation wastage term.

include_irradiation.name: include_irradiation
include_irradiation.doc: Include the flux-driven wastage term when thinning the wall.

name: uzr_clad_void_swelling
doc: Cladding diametral strain from void swelling (dimensionless).
full_doc:
Cladding diametral strain from void swelling (dimensionless).

A **diagnostic**, not a severity: it returns a strain, not a utilization,
so it must never be named in a ``uzr_severity_index``. It is also not the
IFR hoop-strain criterion -- see
:class:`UZrHoopStrainSeverityPostprocessor` for why those are different
deformation mechanisms.

``epsilon_theta = (1/3) * dV/V``, the isotropic partition, from
:func:`~.correlations.void_swelling_ht9` at the driving dose.

Off by default for HT9, on for the austenitics
----------------------------------------------

``alloy`` has **no default**, and HT9 must be asked for explicitly via
``allow_ht9 = true``. That is not fussiness: the X447 documentation lists
HT9 void swelling as *"Neglected"* in both its model sets, on the stated
physical reasoning that a tempered martensitic steel does not swell like
316SS or D9 -- and ``source_discrepancies.md`` §D4 records the resolution
as a per-alloy switchable term, off by default for HT9. The X430 reference
deck does instantiate the BISON object, so the term is not *absent* for
HT9; it is negligible at these fluences, and reporting it without the
reader asking invites it to be read as a structural margin.

The austenitic contrast is the point. D9 and 316SS swell from very low
dose, which is the comparison a parametric study of this fuel form is
usually after, and those alloys need no opt-in.

**No packaged alloy reaches this on defaults alone**, and that is worth
knowing before reaching for it: HT9 needs ``allow_ht9``, and the packaged
D9 and SS316 rows record ``NOT_AVAILABLE`` for the swelling pair, because
the supplied sources carry no incubation-then-linear coefficients for
austenitics. Those alloys therefore refuse at compute, naming the missing
field, until a deck states ``incubation_dpa`` and ``rate_per_dpa`` or
registers a row that carries them. Refusing beats borrowing HT9's 40 dpa
incubation, which would under-predict an austenitic -- non-conservative,
and entirely plausible-looking.

field.name: field
field.doc: Solve array holding cladding displacement damage in dpa, reduced with 'reduction' (default 'max'). Give this OR 'dose_dpa', not both.

dose_dpa.name: dose_dpa
dose_dpa.doc: Peak cladding dose in dpa, stated directly instead of reduced from a solve array. Give this OR 'field', not both.

component.name: component
component.doc: Component of a vector or tensor field, as a list ('[0]', '[0, 0]'). Omit for scalar fields.

reduction.name: reduction
reduction.doc: How to reduce the field to the value that governs severity. 'max' (default) is the hot spot that sets the limit; 'mean' is a diagnostic and will under-report a peaked profile.

alloy.name: alloy
alloy.doc: Cladding alloy, selecting the void-swelling coefficients. Required with no default: void swelling is a per-alloy switchable term (source_discrepancies.md D4) and the alloys differ by more than their coefficients -- HT9 is documented as negligible while the austenitics swell from very low dose. HT9 additionally needs 'allow_ht9'; see the class docstring.

allow_ht9.name: allow_ht9
allow_ht9.doc: Opt in to reporting HT9 void swelling, which the X447 documentation lists as 'Neglected' in both model sets. Has no effect for other alloys.

incubation_dpa.name: incubation_dpa
incubation_dpa.doc: Void-swelling incubation dose; no swelling accumulates below it. Unstated resolves it from the SELECTED alloy's row, which raises for alloys whose sources carry no value rather than borrowing another alloy's.

rate_per_dpa.name: rate_per_dpa
rate_per_dpa.doc: Void-swelling rate once the incubation dose is exceeded. Alloy-resolved on the same terms as incubation_dpa.

name: uzr_fcci_severity
doc: FCCI wall penetration against an allowable fraction of the wall.
full_doc:
FCCI wall penetration against an allowable fraction of the wall.

Demand is the interaction-layer depth grown at the reduced field
temperature over ``exposure_s``; capacity is
``allowable_penetration * wall_thickness``. Severity 1 means the
allowable penetration is fully consumed -- not that the wall is
breached, which is the point of setting the allowable below unity.

field.name: field
field.doc: Solve array holding cladding inner-surface temperature in K, reduced with 'reduction' (default 'max'). Give this OR 'temperature', not both.

temperature.name: temperature
temperature.doc: Cladding inner-surface temperature in K, stated directly instead of reduced from a solve array. This is the right source in the pin-slice reduction, where the deck solves for lanthanide concentration and the interface temperature is a stated operating condition. Give this OR 'field', not both.

component.name: component
component.doc: Component of a vector or tensor field, as a list ('[0]', '[0, 0]'). Omit for scalar fields.

reduction.name: reduction
reduction.doc: How to reduce the field to the value that governs severity. 'max' (default) is the hot spot that sets the limit; 'mean' is a diagnostic and will under-report a peaked profile.

exposure_s.name: exposure_s
exposure_s.doc: Irradiation time in seconds over which the interaction layer grew. Required with no default, so a deck that omits it is rejected by validation naming the parameter rather than losing its severity to a postprocessing warning. Cross-checked against the solve's end time when it reports one.

wall_thickness.name: wall_thickness
wall_thickness.doc: As-built cladding wall thickness in m. Required with no default: it is the denominator of the penetration fraction, so a guessed wall silently sets the severity.

allowable_penetration.name: allowable_penetration
allowable_penetration.doc: Allowable FCCI penetration as a fraction of the as-built wall (0-1). Required -- no default, because the allowable is a design decision, not a material property. NOTE: the 0.25 used in this repository's tests and examples is an UNSOURCED engineering placeholder. Neither NUREG/CR-7305 nor INL/RPT-23-74940 states a 25% allowable; the only clad-thickness allowable in either document is the EBR-II limit of 5% for *eutectic penetration* (ML23214A065.pdf p.28 [2-8]), which is a transient-liquefaction criterion and not a drop-in for this steady-state wastage model -- the same page states the strain and CDF criteria implicitly incorporate steady-state wastage thinning. Choose this value deliberately; read against the 5% figure, 0.25 is 5x non-conservative.

alloy.name: alloy
alloy.doc: Cladding alloy selecting the wastage coefficient set.

fast_flux.name: fast_flux
fast_flux.doc: Fast neutron flux in n/m^2/s driving the irradiation-enhanced wastage term. Zero disables that term.

include_irradiation.name: include_irradiation
include_irradiation.doc: Include the flux-driven wastage term alongside the thermal one.

doc: Stage 1 of the FCCI chain: interaction-layer depth, in **m**.
full_doc:
Stage 1 of the FCCI chain: interaction-layer depth, in **m**.

Reports the empirical wastage depth grown at the driving temperature
over ``exposure_s``. This is a *diagnostic*, not a severity: it returns
metres, not a utilization, so it must not be listed in a
``uzr_severity_index``. ``uzr_fcci_severity`` is the mechanism that
normalises the same depth against an allowable.

Reporting it separately is the point. A CDF of 0.7 does not say whether
the pin reached it through 40 um of attack or 200, and those are
different pins with different remedies.

exposure_s.name: exposure_s
exposure_s.doc: Time at temperature, in seconds. Required with no default, and cross-checked against the solve's end time when it reports one.

alloy.doc: Cladding alloy, selecting the empirical wastage coefficients.

fast_flux.doc: Fast neutron flux for the irradiation-assisted wastage term.

name: uzr_hoop_strain_severity
doc: Cladding plastic hoop strain against the IFR strain limit.
full_doc:
Cladding plastic hoop strain against the IFR strain limit.

Demand is the **thermal component of plastic hoop strain**, taken from the
deck or reduced from a solve array; capacity is ``strain_limit``. Severity
1 means the stated limit is reached.

This postprocessor implements the **criterion**, not a deformation model
-------------------------------------------------------------------------

It deliberately computes no strain of its own. Nothing in this phase solves
cladding thermomechanics -- Phase 38 excludes it, and hoop *stress* here is
a thin-wall closed form -- so the strain has to come from outside: a PIE
measurement, a coupled run, or a deck-stated design value. Normalising a
number the deck supplies is the honest reduction; deriving one would mean
inventing a creep-strain law, and the only rupture correlation this suite
carries (:func:`~.correlations.larson_miller_rupture_time`) is itself
*fitted rather than qualified*, so a strain built on it would be an
unverified number wearing a criterion's name.

An earlier version of this class did exactly that, deriving demand from
``void_swelling_ht9(dose)``. That was wrong twice over and is recorded here
because the failure mode is instructive rather than obvious:

* **Wrong mechanism.** The IFR criterion is the *thermal* component of
  plastic hoop strain -- creep deformation. Void swelling is a different
  deformation mechanism, so a severity built on it does not answer the
  criterion even when it returns a plausible number.
* **Wrong for this alloy in particular.** The X447 documentation lists HT9
  void swelling as *"Neglected"* in both its legacy and enhanced model
  sets, because a tempered martensitic steel does not swell like its
  austenitic counterparts -- which is the physical reason HT9 enabled
  high-burnup metallic fuel at all. ``source_discrepancies.md`` §D4
  already recorded the resolution: clad void swelling is a per-alloy
  switchable term, **off by default for HT9**.

Below HT9's 40 dpa incubation dose that version therefore reported a
severity of exactly **zero** while occupying the row that claims to cover
the 1 % criterion -- worse than having no mechanism at all, because a
reader sees the row and concludes the criterion is covered. Clad void
swelling now lives in :class:`UZrCladVoidSwellingPostprocessor` as a
*diagnostic*, on the per-alloy terms D4 specifies.

Which limit, and why the deck must say
--------------------------------------

Two are in circulation and they differ by a factor of two: the **IFR
design limit** of 1 % (:data:`~.correlations.CLAD_STRAIN_DESIGN_LIMIT`),
and the level at which failures are **observed** to begin, near 2 %
(:data:`~.correlations.CLAD_STRAIN_OBSERVED_FAILURE`) -- the X447 page
notes PIE-measured circumferential peak strain on some pins exceeds 2 %. A
pin at 1.5 % is outside the design basis and not expected to leak: both
true, and they answer different questions.

``strain_limit`` is therefore required with no default, as every limit in
this module is, and the two named constants are what a deck should quote.
Evaluating the same pin against both is one extra block, and the pair is
what the phase's limits table means by "record **both**".

field.name: field
field.doc: Solve array holding cladding plastic hoop strain (dimensionless), reduced with 'reduction' (default 'max'). Give this OR 'hoop_strain', not both.

hoop_strain.name: hoop_strain
hoop_strain.doc: Thermal component of plastic hoop strain, dimensionless (0.01 is 1%), stated directly instead of reduced from a solve array. This phase solves no cladding thermomechanics, so for a pin-slice deck this is measured or design data, not solve output. Give this OR 'field', not both.

component.name: component
component.doc: Component of a vector or tensor field, as a list ('[0]', '[0, 0]'). Omit for scalar fields.

reduction.name: reduction
reduction.doc: How to reduce the field to the value that governs severity. 'max' (default) is the hot spot that sets the limit; 'mean' is a diagnostic and will under-report a peaked profile.

strain_limit.name: strain_limit
strain_limit.doc: Allowable cladding plastic hoop strain, dimensionless (0.01 is the 1% IFR design limit; 0.02 is the level at which failures are observed to begin). Required with no default: the two differ by 2x and answer different questions, so the deck must say which one this severity means.

name: uzr_hoop_stress
doc: Stage 3 of the FCCI chain: thin-wall hoop stress, in **Pa**.
full_doc:
Stage 3 of the FCCI chain: thin-wall hoop stress, in **Pa**.

``sigma_theta = p r / t_rem`` on the ligament stage 2 reported, so the
returned stress already carries the FCCI amplification. Consume a named
``uzr_remaining_wall`` block, or state the ligament directly.

Note that stress rises **non-linearly** as the wall is consumed -- a
third of the wall gone is a 1.5x rise, half gone is 2x. That
amplification is the mechanism by which a chemical process becomes a
structural failure, and separating this stage from the CDF is what lets a
report show it happening.

remaining_wall_from.name: remaining_wall_from
remaining_wall_from.doc: Name of the postprocessor block (normally a 'uzr_remaining_wall') whose value is the ligament in m. Give this OR 'remaining_wall', not both.

remaining_wall.name: remaining_wall
remaining_wall.doc: Load-bearing wall in m, stated directly instead of consumed from another block. Give this OR 'remaining_wall_from'.

radius.name: radius
radius.doc: Cladding mid-wall radius in m. Required with no default -- it is the moment arm of the thin-wall form.

internal_pressure.name: internal_pressure
internal_pressure.doc: Net internal pressure in Pa: plenum gas less coolant, plus any contact pressure. Required. The 'plenum_pressure' correlation computes it from gas inventory when the deck lacks it.

name: uzr_remaining_wall
doc: Stage 2 of the FCCI chain: load-bearing ligament, in **m**.
full_doc:
Stage 2 of the FCCI chain: load-bearing ligament, in **m**.

Consumes a wastage depth -- from a named ``uzr_fcci_wastage`` block, or
stated directly when the deck has a measured depth -- and reports what is
left of the wall.

Unlike :func:`~.correlations.remaining_wall`, which floors its result so
downstream stress stays finite, this **raises**
:class:`WallConsumedError` when the wastage has reached the wall. Reaching
the floor here is not a thin wall, it is a breached one, and returning
1 nm would send an enormous but perfectly finite stress down the chain
that a reader would take for a computed result.

wastage_from.name: wastage_from
wastage_from.doc: Name of the postprocessor block (normally a 'uzr_fcci_wastage') whose value is the wastage depth in m. Give this OR 'wastage_depth', not both.

wastage_depth.name: wastage_depth
wastage_depth.doc: Inner-surface FCCI wastage depth in m, stated directly instead of consumed from another block. Give this OR 'wastage_from'.

wall_thickness.name: wall_thickness
wall_thickness.doc: As-built cladding wall thickness in m. Required with no default -- it is the ligament and the hoop-stress denominator.

coolant_side_allowance.name: coolant_side_allowance
coolant_side_allowance.doc: Outer-surface cladding-coolant interaction thinning the same wall (m). Defaults to 0, which reproduces the FCCI-only literature comparison; ~20 um is the X447 observation.

name: uzr_severity_index
doc: Envelope severity: the maximum over named mechanism severities.
full_doc:
Envelope severity: the maximum over named mechanism severities.

Reads the values of other postprocessors in the same run, so the
mechanisms it names must be blocks in the same deck. The result is the
single number a scenario sweep sorts on; *which* mechanism produced it
is read from those named entries in ``summary.json``, which are all
on the same utilization convention.

A missing or non-scalar input is an error, not a skipped term: taking
the max over a silently shortened list would report the envelope of the
mechanisms that happened to evaluate, which is indistinguishable from a
genuinely lower envelope.

mechanisms.name: mechanisms
mechanisms.doc: Names of the severity postprocessor blocks to envelope. Required; every one must evaluate, so that a missing mechanism fails rather than quietly lowering the envelope.

name: uzr_solidus_severity
doc: Peak fuel temperature against the U--Zr solidus, as a homologous ratio.
full_doc:
Peak fuel temperature against the U--Zr solidus, as a homologous ratio.

Demand is the reduced fuel temperature in K; capacity is the solidus at
the deck's Zr weight fraction. The ratio is reported in absolute
temperature -- a homologous temperature -- so this is the one mechanism
here whose capacity is a material property rather than a design
allowable, and it therefore needs no ``limit`` parameter.

Severity 1 is incipient melting. Note that fuel--clad eutectic
penetration begins several hundred kelvin *below* the fuel solidus, so a
solidus severity comfortably under 1 does not by itself clear a pin --
read ``uzr_fcci_severity`` alongside it.

field.name: field
field.doc: Solve array holding fuel temperature in K (absolute, not Celsius), reduced with 'reduction' (default 'max'). Give this OR 'temperature', not both.

temperature.name: temperature
temperature.doc: Peak fuel temperature in K (absolute, not Celsius), stated directly instead of reduced from a solve array. Give this OR 'field', not both.

component.name: component
component.doc: Component of a vector or tensor field, as a list ('[0]', '[0, 0]'). Omit for scalar fields.

zr_weight_fraction.name: zr_weight_fraction
zr_weight_fraction.doc: Zr weight fraction setting the solidus. Defaults to 0.10 (U-10Zr), the EBR-II driver composition -- a material property, so unlike the design allowables it may default.

name: uzr_swelling_severity
doc: Fuel swelling strain against the strain that closes the fuel--clad gap.
full_doc:
Fuel swelling strain against the strain that closes the fuel--clad gap.

Demand is the linear swelling strain implied by the porosity at the
reduced burnup; capacity is ``gap_closure_strain``. Severity 1 is gap
closure -- the onset of mechanical interaction, not cladding failure.
Below the interconnection burnup the correlation is in its steep
pre-percolation branch, which is exactly where severity is most
sensitive to burnup.

field.name: field
field.doc: Solve array holding local burnup in at%, reduced with 'reduction' (default 'max'). Give this OR 'burnup_at_pct', not both.

burnup_at_pct.name: burnup_at_pct
burnup_at_pct.doc: Peak burnup in at%, stated directly instead of reduced from a solve array. Give this OR 'field', not both.

component.name: component
component.doc: Component of a vector or tensor field, as a list ('[0]', '[0, 0]'). Omit for scalar fields.

reduction.name: reduction
reduction.doc: How to reduce the field to the value that governs severity. 'max' (default) is the hot spot that sets the limit; 'mean' is a diagnostic and will under-report a peaked profile.

gap_closure_strain.name: gap_closure_strain
gap_closure_strain.doc: Linear fuel strain at which the as-built fuel--clad gap closes (dimensionless). Required -- it is set by the smear density and gap of the specific pin design.

interconnection_burnup_at_pct.name: interconnection_burnup_at_pct
interconnection_burnup_at_pct.doc: Burnup at which the pore network percolates and the swelling correlation leaves its steep pre-percolation branch. Unstated uses the packaged U-10Zr value. Exposed because it is the closure parameter a sensitivity study most wants to ablate -- severity is most sensitive to burnup right around it.

anisotropy_factor.name: anisotropy_factor
anisotropy_factor.doc: Ratio of radial to mean linear strain. 1.0 is isotropic; raise it to bias swelling radially into the gap.
