name: pinn_fem
doc: Registered PINN+FEM hybrid solver.
full_doc:
Registered PINN+FEM hybrid solver.

The solver composes a trained :class:`ElasticityFieldModel` (the PINN
predictor) with the Phase-19 batched FEM assembler and Newton solver.  The
coupling mode is selected by registered name from the ``[Hybrid]`` config
block; each mode implements the :class:`_HybridMode` interface.

Args:
    backend: Active numerical backend.
    pinn_model: Spatial PINN model that provides the initial predictor.
    assembler: FEM assembler for the same mesh/material.
    bcs: FEM boundary conditions built from the tagged mesh.
    hybrid_cfg: ``[Hybrid]`` configuration dictionary.

mode.name: mode
mode.doc: How the PINN prediction is used: 'warm_start' seeds the FEM Newton iteration, 'predictor_corrector' alternates prediction and correction, 'preconditioner' uses it to precondition the linear solve, 'increment_predictor' predicts the increment with the frozen step-1 PINN and reports warm vs cold Newton iterations per step (Phase M15-2).

accuracy_target.name: accuracy_target
accuracy_target.doc: **Absolute** residual tolerance the corrected solution must reach. See ``accuracy_rel_target`` — on a stiff material this target alone is not reachable.

accuracy_rel_target.name: accuracy_rel_target
accuracy_rel_target.doc: **Relative** residual tolerance: the corrector stops once ``||R|| <= max(accuracy_rel_target * ||R_0||, accuracy_target)``, where ``||R_0||`` is the first iteration's residual norm. The residual carries the units of a nodal force, so on a stiff material it bottoms out on the assembled tangent's floating-point noise floor and the absolute target alone can never fire; this scale-free test is what terminates such a solve. Set to ``0`` to use the absolute target alone.

max_pinn_budget.name: max_pinn_budget
max_pinn_budget.doc: Cap on total PINN training/finetune epochs (0 = unlimited).

name: feature_flood_count
doc: Registered ``("utility", "feature_flood_count")`` service wrapper.
full_doc:
Registered ``("utility", "feature_flood_count")`` service wrapper.

A thin, params-driven handle over :func:`feature_flood_count` for decks
that declare the counter in ``[Utilities]``: it fixes the threshold (and
optionally an OP ordering) at construction and exposes :meth:`count` for
callers that drive it explicitly between slabs.

threshold.name: threshold
threshold.doc: Flood-count threshold: an element is active when its largest element-averaged OP value is at least this.

fields.name: fields
fields.doc: Optional explicit OP-field name order (empty = the supplied mapping's own order). Fixes which fields are flooded when the solve result carries extra arrays.

name: grain_tracker
doc: Persistent grain identity with OP-collision-free remap bookkeeping.
full_doc:
Persistent grain identity with OP-collision-free remap bookkeeping.

The service holds the ``grain_id -> (OP, representative element)`` map
between invocations. :meth:`update` flood-counts the current OP fields,
matches features to grains, and reports merges, retirements, new ids
and the OP remaps a driver must apply. It is a plain service: nothing
invokes it automatically, and it never touches a field.

Args:
    params: Validated parameter dict (see :meth:`params`).

threshold.name: threshold
threshold.doc: Flood-count threshold below which an element is inactive. The default mirrors MOOSE's GrainTracker (0.1); use a higher value for noisier fields.

fields.name: fields
fields.doc: Names of the nodal fields that are grain ORDER PARAMETERS (empty = every field passed in). In a coupled block solve the executioner publishes every scalar fem field, so a deck that also carries a concentration, chemical potential or temperature MUST name its order parameters here or those fields are tracked as grains; the executioner refuses such a deck rather than guess. Per-component names are '<variable>' for a scalar variable and '<variable>_<i>' for a multi-component one.

n_order_params.name: n_order_params
n_order_params.doc: Size of the OP pool (0 = infer from the fields passed to the first update). The pool bounds how many grains can coexist.

match_tol.name: match_tol
match_tol.doc: Absolute distance cap for the nearest-representative-point fallback (0 = the mesh bounding-box diagonal). Containment matching always runs first and needs no tolerance.

name: nucleation_inserter
doc: Poisson event sampling over candidate sites, keyed per site.
full_doc:
Poisson event sampling over candidate sites, keyed per site.

:meth:`step` consumes the current candidate sites and the step size and
returns the events that fired. Each site's draw is an independent
Bernoulli with probability
:math:`p_s = 1-\exp(-I\,\Delta t\,V_s)` taken from a stream seeded by
``([seed, step_index, site_key])`` — so results are bit-reproducible for
a seed, and independent of how sites are ordered or split across
workers. A site that has fired is removed from the candidate pool
(``allow_refire = True`` keeps it in play for repeated sampling runs).

The inserter is a plain service: nothing invokes it automatically. A
driver calls it between slabs, paints :meth:`mask` onto the field (or
hands the events to a ``nucleation_penalty`` kernel) and evolves on.

Args:
    params: Validated parameter dict (see :meth:`params`).

rate_density.name: rate_density
rate_density.doc: Nucleation rate density ``I``: the mean number of events per unit candidate volume per unit time. The per-site step probability is ``1 - exp(-I dt V_s)``.

radius.name: radius
radius.doc: Default nucleus radius ``r_crit`` (the mask bump's half-height point) for sites that do not carry their own.

hold_time.name: hold_time
hold_time.doc: How long an inserted nucleus stays active in the mask (None = forever). A finite hold time expires the bump.

mask_width.name: mask_width
mask_width.doc: Interface width of the smooth mask bump (0 = automatic: a quarter of the mean nucleus radius).

seed.name: seed
seed.doc: Base RNG seed for the per-site event streams. LEAVE IT UNSET to inherit ``[Global] seed`` (the builder binds it), so sweeping the global seed sweeps the realisation of an ensemble; set it only to pin this service against the rest of the deck. Results are bit-reproducible for a seed and parallel-independent across site splits.

allow_refire.name: allow_refire
allow_refire.doc: Whether an already-fired site may fire again on a later step. False (default) retires the site after its first event, matching physical nucleation; True supports repeated-sampling Monte-Carlo runs.

name: nucleation_timestep_limiter
doc: Cap ``dt`` so at most ``probability_bound`` of steps see two events.
full_doc:
Cap ``dt`` so at most ``probability_bound`` of steps see two events.

Independent per-site Poisson processes merge into ONE Poisson process of
rate ``R = I · Σ V_s``, so the per-step event count is Poisson and the
two-or-more-event probability is the closed-form upper tail
:math:`P(N\ge2) = 1-(1+\lambda)e^{-\lambda}` with
:math:`\lambda = R\,\Delta t`. :meth:`limit_dt` returns
``min(dt, λ_max / R)`` where ``λ_max`` solves the tail equation at the
configured bound — the largest step whose two-event probability stays
under the bound.

A plain service like the inserter: a driver runs
``dt = limiter.limit_dt(dt)`` before each step (MOOSE's
``DiscreteNucleationTimeStep`` analogue, default bound 0.01).

Args:
    params: Validated parameter dict (see :meth:`params`).

rate_density.name: rate_density
rate_density.doc: Nucleation rate density ``I`` — must match the inserter's.

site_volume.name: site_volume
site_volume.doc: TOTAL candidate-site volume ``Σ V_s`` live in a step (the per-call ``site_volume`` argument overrides it).

inserter.name: inserter
inserter.doc: Name of the [Utilities] block whose retired sites this limiter stops counting. Leave empty when the deck has ONE nucleation inserter (the pairing is then unambiguous); with several it must be set, because one inserter's retirements say nothing about another's remaining event rate — the executioner refuses an ambiguous deck rather than intersecting every mask.

probability_bound.name: probability_bound
probability_bound.doc: Maximum allowed two-or-more-event probability per step ``p_max`` (MOOSE default 0.01). Strictly between 0 and 1.

max_dt.name: max_dt
max_dt.doc: Optional hard cap applied on top of the statistical cap (None = the two-event bound only).

name: per_grain_orientation
doc: Registered ``("utility", "per_grain_orientation")`` factory.
full_doc:
Registered ``("utility", "per_grain_orientation")`` factory.

The factory holds the user-supplied ``source`` spec and exposes a
:meth:`to_qp_field` method that materialises the per-QP Euler
angles. The :class:`Component`-like :meth:`params` method declares
the input spec (M1 contract).

source.name: source
source.doc: Orientation source spec. Same shape as the legacy [Polycrystal] orientation_source block. Supported values: ``mackenzie``, ``uniform``, ``explicit``, ``texture``, ``point_file``, ``grain_file``.

n_grains.name: n_grains
n_grains.doc: Number of grains. Must match the mesh's grain ID range.

seed.name: seed
seed.doc: RNG seed for reproducible orientation sampling.

name: displacement
doc: Registered default variable factory (displacement field).
full_doc: Registered default variable factory (displacement field).

name.name: name
name.doc: Variable name; defaults to the sub-block key inside ``[Variables]`` if not set explicitly.

family.name: family
family.doc: Discretisation family. ``fem`` discretises the variable with a finite element and feeds it to the batched FEM assembler; ``pinn`` represents it with a registered neural network and feeds it to the PINN executioner. Kernels and executioners select the matching family automatically.

components.name: components
components.doc: Number of components per node. ``1`` for scalar variables (temperature, pressure, damage), ``dim`` for vector variables (displacement in 1-D/2-D/3-D).

order.name: order
order.doc: Element order for ``family=fem`` variables. ``1`` selects a linear element; ``2`` selects a quadratic element. Ignored for PINN variables (the network is the discretisation).

network.name: network
network.doc: Registered ``network`` name (only used when ``family=pinn``). Defaults to ``mlp``; the registered ``dual_pathway`` and ``slip_encoded`` networks are the other supported choices.

scale.name: scale
scale.doc: Output scale applied to the variable's network prediction so the network learns O(1) values. ``1.0`` is a safe default for PINN training on dimensionless variables; pass the characteristic magnitude of the field (e.g. ``E*eps`` for stress, ``L*eps`` for displacement) when the field has a natural physical scale.
